title: Indie Energy says storage revenue model is shifting beyond arbitrage - Energy Storage
content: Portuguese company Indie Energy develops and operates a virtual power plant (VPP) connecting producers and consumers with market participants such as balance responsible parties (BRPs), balancing service providers (BSPs), and collective self-consumption management entities. Its platform supports participation in energy communities, electricity markets, and system-balancing services. pv magazine spoke with Indie Energy CEO Pedro Rodrigues about the company’s business model, battery storage economics, and plans for the Spanish market. pv magazine: How many renewable energy projects does Indie Energy have in Portugal, and what is their total installed capacity? Pedro Rodrigues: Our platform enables the management and optimization of energy buying and selling in energy communities, in the day-ahead and intraday electricity markets, as well as the provision of system services such as aFRR and mFRR. These assets represent more than 400 MW of installed capacity and 500 GWh of energy traded in the markets. In energy communities, the platform is used by around 10 managing entities for the operational management of energy buying, selling and allocation across 50 collective self-consumption projects. These projects involve more than 250 consumers and 80 producers, representing more than 5 MW of installed capacity and more than 1 GWh of energy shared annually among members. How is the war in the Strait of Hormuz affecting Indie Energy’s plans and projects, if at all? We do not anticipate any impact on our operations or projects. On the contrary, Indie Energy’s value proposition is precisely to help producers and consumers find more stable and predictable solutions to deal with periods of greater uncertainty and volatility in electricity prices. How are control algorithms for BESS being designed to account for capacity limits at connection points to Portugal’s national grid, particularly in regions with high solar penetration such as Alentejo? Our algorithms incorporate the existing capacity limits at the connection point of the facility where the storage system is located. These limits are considered one of the main constraints in the optimization problem, along with factors such as the facility’s power balance, state of charge, number of cycles and battery degradation. Decision variables, such as battery charging and discharging or the operating point of photovoltaic inverters, are determined while respecting the capacity limits. This makes it possible to reduce solar production or consumption curtailment by storing energy when there is excess production and shifting its delivery to more highly valued quarter-hour periods. This allows more efficient use of the grid capacity that has been allocated. In Portugal’s capacity tenders, what are the ideal state-of-charge management strategies for meeting injection ramps without accelerating lithium-cell degradation? The optimization algorithm incorporates constraints that take battery degradation into account based on information from the manufacturer. Our model manages the state of charge within operating bands and considers a maximum number of charge and discharge cycles, mitigating accelerated degradation. In addition, the degradation cost is estimated and incorporated into the model’s objective functions to determine the operating strategy, as well as any outages or limitations that need to be communicated to the Global System Manager. Given Portugal’s substantial installed pumped-hydro capacity, including the Tâmega system, what technical frequency-stability challenges arise from coordinating hydropower dispatch with the ultrafast response of new BESS, particularly in terms of synthetic versus conventional inertia? The technical challenges are being addressed through the dispatch project published by the Directorate-General for Energy and Geology (DGEG), which establishes the technical conditions and requirements for the connection and access to the Public Service Electricity Network (RESP) of standalone or co-located storage facilities. These requirements allow the Global System Manager and transmission system operators to require storage units to meet requirements such as secondary reserve (aFRR), tertiary reserve (mFRR), response to frequency variations, operation in Grid Forming (GFM) mode, provision of synthetic inertia, and observability and control capabilities. In practice, storage systems must meet the applicable requirements according to the significance of each installation – types A, B, C or D – based on its power and connection characteristics. GFM requirements, including synthetic inertia, are intended to ensure that these systems behave similarly to a synchronous machine. The requirements are gradual and cumulative for higher-power or higher-voltage installations, ensuring that the growing integration of BESS complements the response of power generation facilities. In the absence of a long-term capacity mechanism in the Iberian electricity market (MIBEL), what technical requirements must BESS meet to maximize profitability through revenue stacking in system services? Batteries can provide different remunerated system services, such as upward and downward regulation reserves, contributing to the instantaneous balance between production and consumption. These services include aFRR, mFRR and participation in the resolution of technical constraints. They can also provide other services that are not yet remunerated in Portugal: frequency containment reserve (FCR), fast frequency response (FFR), synthetic inertia and voltage regulation. Combining revenues from the electricity market and system services through revenue stacking enables projects to be economically sustainable. In aFRR, a very fast activation time is required: activation must begin in less than 30 seconds and be completed within a maximum of five minutes. For mFRR, activation must take place within 12.5 minutes. Do you see a risk of arbitrage cannibalization due to the battery boom? It is a real and expected risk. As more batteries enter the system, the spread between low-price hours, when there is excess solar generation, and high-price hours at the end of the day tends to narrow. The operation of the batteries themselves – charging during solar hours and discharging at the end of the day — reduces this differential. This does not diminish the importance of storage. It means that profitability will increasingly depend on participating in multiple markets simultaneously. This includes system services, day-ahead and intraday markets, energy communities and self-consumption management. That is why optimization and software become more important as the sector matures. Are you concerned about the risk of BESS technology becoming obsolete and its impact on capital expenditure, given that cells may need to be replaced after 10 to 12 years? It is a risk that needs to be explicitly incorporated into business plans. Cell replacement after 10 to 12 years should be treated as scheduled capex. This means modeling the degradation curve and replacement cost against the expected evolution of cell prices, which have been falling. New chemistries or higher energy density could make early replacement attractive if the retrofit generates benefits that offset the additional capex. Does Indie Energy plan to enter or expand into the Spanish market? In 2027, we intend to consolidate our presence in Portugal in electricity markets, system services and energy communities. There is also the possibility of offering our platform to electricity retailers, connecting producers, consumers and market participants on a single platform. At the end of the first half of 2027, we will evaluate entering the Spanish market, given that we already participate in the Iberian market through OMIE. Finally, is there any particular project planned for 2027 that you would like to highlight for pv magazine? In 2027, we should have utility-scale and commercial and industrial (C&I) hybrid projects in operation that combine solar PV with battery storage. We are supporting customers in developing these projects so they can participate simultaneously in multiple markets: system services, the day-ahead and intraday markets, energy communities and electricity trading. The development of this platform is being supported by the P2P Energy Trading project, funded by COMPETE 2030, which will conclude at the end of this year. title: RWE takes final investment decision to build 1.1 GWh battery in the Netherlands - Energy Storage
content: German energy major RWE has made its final investment decision to build a 400 MW / 1.1 GWh battery storage system at the Moerdijk power station site in the Netherlands using its existing 150 kV substation at Moerdijk-Noord. The Moerdijk plant, located south of Rotterdam, was primarily a 426 MW gas-fired combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) power plant, and the site had a small battery system acting as one of the first synthetic inertia batteries on the European grid, via a 7.5 MW / 11 MWh installation. In a sign of the times, the new battery, with 208 containers from an unspecified manufacturer, will be exactly 100 times larger. The system size at a 2.75-hour duration suggests a split of around 1.92 MW / 5.29 MWh per container, and it will also provide “advanced grid services,” indicating the use of grid-forming inverters. Construction is scheduled to “start in due course,” said RWE, and commissioning is planned for the second quarter of 2028. Connection details Grid connections for generation or demand in the Netherlands are in tremendously short supply, with Transmission System Operator TenneT unable to process an enormous backlog due to system congestion. New batteries added to the grid can either aid the system or add their own capacity demands on already stretched substations and transmission lines. The Moerdijk battery, however, will be dispatched to relieve congestion. This also plays into the nearby 795 MW offshore wind project between RWE and TotalEnergies, helping store energy when wind output is high. In the press release, RWE stated: “Through capacity steering agreements with Transmission System Operator TenneT, the battery will be dispatched to relieve congestion in the Noord-Brabant region. Thanks to this development, space is being created on the grid for parties on the waiting list who wish to purchase electricity. TenneT, together with the regional grid operator Enexis, will be investigating what this means in the coming period. The grid operator will take this development, along with other developments in the region, into account when reviewing the congestion management study in December of 2026. The new battery system will also be equipped to provide advanced grid services such as instantaneous reserve (inertia). The Moerdijk site already hosts the first synthetic inertia battery connected to the continental European grid, with a capacity of 7.5 MW/11 MWh. “ Mark Lentjes, Regional Director of TenneT Southern Netherlands, added: “We are pleased that RWE intends to contribute to a more efficient use of the electricity grid in West Brabant with a large-scale battery that acts as a congestion reliever. RWE’s large-scale battery is located close to the 150,000-volt high-voltage substation at Moerdijk-Noord, where it will help to alleviate the regional bottleneck, which in turn has an impact on congestion across the whole of Noord-Brabant.“ The post RWE takes final investment decision to build 1.1 GWh battery in the Netherlands appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: BYD's $10,000 EV has a big sibling on the way, and here's our first look [Images]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 21 2026 - 8:50 am PT
The Seagull is BYD’s most affordable EV, starting at about $10,000 in China. In Europe, the UK, and other markets, it’s sold as the Dolphin Surf or Mini, but
is preparing to launch a larger variant that may be an even “bigger” hit.
BYD Seagull EV grows up with new ‘Great’ version
BYD’s low-cost electric hatch is among the world’s best-selling electric vehicles. In China, the Seagull starts at just 69,900 yuan, or roughly $10,000.
Overseas, it’s sold as the Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini in places like Europe and the UK. According to
Cleantechnica
, the Seagull, including the Dolphin Surf and Mini, was the
sixth most popular EV
globally in the first half of 2026, with over 27,500 units sold.
BYD is now preparing to launch an updated variant that’s bigger, more powerful, and more advanced than the current model.
Zhang Zhuo, the sales boss for BYD’s Ocean series,
previewed the new Seagull
for the first time in July. Although the images were blurred, the caption read, “As its silhouette gradually emerges in the shadows, the promise of growing up is about to be fulfilled. #BYDSeagull#.”
At the Chengdu Auto Show last month, Zhou revealed the new model will be named the “Great Seagull” and confirmed it will go on sale by the end of 2026.
No other details were revealed, but the Great Seagull appeared in the batch of new energy vehicles approved for sale by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (
) last month, giving us a better idea of what to expect.
BYD’s new Great Seagull measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm tall, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase, according to the filing. In comparison, the current Seagull is just 3,780 mm long.
It will also use a more powerful 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor, up from 55 kW (75 hp) in the current Seagull.
BYD will reveal final specs soon, but the Great Seagull is expected to feature its latest Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, enabling it to recharge from 10% to 70% in 5 minutes.
The larger upgraded model has a roof-mounted LiDAR, suggesting it will be available with BYD’s God’s Eye B advanced driver assistance system.
A few images surfaced online, revealing the new BYD Great Seagull undisguised for the first time in public. In the images posted by
BYD Fans Club
, you can see the new front-end design and LiDAR on the roof.
We also caught a glimpse of the interior last month with a revamped cabin design. The new interior features a larger infotainment screen, a redesigned center console with more space, and a two-spoke steering wheel.
Following the Great Han sedan and Great Tang SUV, the “Great” Seagull aligns with BYD’s latest naming scheme.
BYD has yet to confirm it, but the new larger model is expected to launch overseas as some variant of the Dolphin Surf or Dolphin Mini.
As such, the electric hatch will likely get a bigger battery and added power to compete with new EVs such as the Volkswagen ID. 3 Neo and Renault Megane.
BYD’s current Dolphin Surf starts at about €22,900 ($26,500) in Europe, so the larger variant is expected to cost slightly more. It will likely still start at under €30,000 ($35,000), as a smaller sibling to the Dolphin.

title: Musk pitches 200-mph Austin-San Antonio ‘Hyperloop’ tunnel, again
content:
Hyperloop
The Boring Company
Fred Lambert
| Sep 21 2026 - 7:06 am PT
Elon Musk says the Boring Company is working on a 200-mph “Hyperloop” tunnel between Austin and San Antonio that would cut the drive to under 30 minutes. He posted the claim on X this weekend with no route, no timeline, and no cost.
It’s a version of a promise Musk has been making for more than a decade. So far, he hasn’t built any of them.
“Boring Company is working on a simple, precursor Hyperloop tunnel between Austin and San Antonio (>200 mph),” Musk wrote. “Due to traffic congestion, that journey can currently take up to 2.5 hours. @BoringCompany can reduce that to a consistent <30 mins.”
The Boring Company replied that it “would be excited and honored to build this massive infrastructure project.”
The two cities sit about 80 miles apart on I-35. At a sustained 200 mph, the math roughly works. The problem is the gap between the tweet and anything real. No permit. No funded route. And no sign anyone is committing to anything.
Musk has promised a hyperloop for over a decade
Musk introduced the hyperloop in a 2013 white paper: passengers riding in pods through a near-vacuum tube at 700 mph. He open-sourced the idea and moved on. In 2017, he claimed “verbal” government approval for a Boring Company hyperloop from New York to Washington, DC. It never happened. A year later, the company
got a green light for a possible hyperloop station in Washington
. That didn’t happen either.
The most recent attempt is the most telling. In late 2022, the Boring Company
began testing a “full-scale” hyperloop
at its Texas facility near Austin. The “twist”: it was a Tesla driving through a tube at normal air pressure, not a pod in a vacuum. The company still advertised “600+ mph.” Nothing came of it.
So this Austin-San Antonio pitch isn’t a new frontier. It’s the fourth or fifth time Musk has floated a hyperloop, in some cases in the exact same part of Texas.
What the Boring Company has actually built
One thing: the Las Vegas Loop. It’s a network of tunnels under the convention center and a few casinos where human-driven Teslas shuttle passengers between stations. In
Electrek’s first rides back in 2021
, the cars topped out around 35 mph. Self-driving still isn’t working in them.
Bigger projects keep getting announced and quietly dropped, from a Chicago airport express to an Ontario, California airport loop. Money isn’t the issue. The company just
raised $3 billion at a $23 billion valuation
, led by the UAE. It’s not short on cash, but it is short on delivered high-speed transit.
And no one else has cracked it. Hyperloop One, the best-funded independent effort, burned through hundreds of millions and shut down in December 2023 without moving a single paying passenger. A decade after Musk’s white paper, there isn’t one hyperloop carrying people anywhere on Earth.
Electrek’s Take
We’ll believe it when we can ride it.
The Austin-San Antonio corridor is a real problem worth solving. It’s one of the fastest-growing regions in the country, and I-35 between the two cities is miserable. But a weekend tweet with no permits and no timeline isn’t a plan. It’s a headline.
We have been here too many times to just beleive Musk when he says something like this.
Musk delivers on plenty. Reusable rockets and the best-selling EVs of the last decade are not vaporware. But hyperloop is one idea he’s pitched over and over and never once shipped. Until there’s a signed agreement with the state and a shovel in the ground, this belongs in the same folder as the New York-DC tunnel: a promise, not a project. What would change our mind? A permit. We’re not holding our breath.
Whatever becomes of Musk’s tunnels, the cheapest way to get around is on energy you make yourself, and if you drive an EV, home solar can cut your charging costs to nearly nothing. title: South Park just took on America’s e-bike problem – and surprisingly nailed a lot of it
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 21 2026 - 7:14 am PT
South Park has finally come for e-bikes. And perhaps surprisingly, underneath all the explosions, biker gangs, racist caricatures, and general South Park-ness of it all, the show actually managed to make some pretty insightful observations about the current state of e-bikes in America.
The Season 29 premiere, “South American Biker Gangs,” aired last week and revolves almost entirely around the growing popularity of e-bikes among kids – and the growing backlash against them.
As someone who has spent years covering this exact issue, I went into the episode expecting mostly cheap e-bike jokes. Instead, I found myself thinking, “Okay, they actually kind of understand this.”
But they also get plenty wrong.
Spoiler alert from here on out, but you probably knew that.
The episode begins with Cartman, a canonically 10-year-old child, convincing his mother to buy him a $2,000 Class 3 e-bike. At the bike shop, the salesman gives his mother perhaps the most responsible e-bike sales pitch ever delivered in South Park:
“That’s a very specific kind of bike, ma’am. I can sell it to you, but there are a lot of restrictions on where your son could ride it. He’d have to respect a lot of rules of the road.”
Approximately five minutes later, he’s dressed like a miniature hooligan, complete with a hoodie and face covering, blasting through red lights, terrorizing pedestrians, riding on sidewalks, and eventually launching through the front window of a Denny’s.
So far, the satire hits thick but is rooted in reality. Many young kids get their first e-bike this way, by begging their parents, and it’s often one of the faster models that parents don’t fully understand.
Obviously, most kids riding e-bikes aren’t jumping them through restaurants. But the show captures a very real problem: A relatively small number of highly visible, irresponsible riders can quickly become the public face of e-bikes.
We’ve watched versions of this play out in cities across the US. Someone riding responsibly at 20 mph (32 km/h) in a bike lane isn’t particularly memorable. Someone popping a wheelie through traffic certainly is.
The out-of-class e-bikes are perhaps just as big a problem
The episode also has fun with the increasing lengths e-bike retailers are going to offer riders higher performance, even if that pushes the bikes past legal limits.
Cartman’s bike is repeatedly described as a Class 3 e-bike. But eventually, his friends Stan, Kyle and Kenny discover a shop selling much cheaper Chinese e-bikes.
The kids pool their money to buy three e-bikes. The pre-teens then sign forms promising that they’re over 16 and won’t ride in prohibited areas, while everyone involved understands perfectly well that none of that is true. The Asian caricature of a seller even tells them aloud, “wink wink,” after each line.
It’s exaggerated, sure, but the underlying problem is very real.
The US has a reasonably clear three-class e-bike system on paper, but the marketplace has increasingly been filled with vehicles marketed as “e-bikes” that can exceed those limits considerably. Online sales make age restrictions and intended-use disclaimers especially difficult to enforce.
South Park even gets the speed-unlocking arms race right. After Cartman discovers that his friends’ cheaper bikes are faster than his expensive yet legal one, he convinces his mother to buy him a speed unlock dongle.
Anyone who follows the e-bike industry knows how familiar the concept is. Controllers, settings, apps, display menus, and aftermarket components can sometimes make regulatory speed limits feel like suggestions.
Where South Park goes way overboard: batteries
Then we get to China.
When the boys discovered those cheaper Chinese e-bikes, the seller tells them the bikes are “very dependable, there’s only a 60% chance they’ll explode in the garage.”
Obviously, that’s absurd. And while it’s satire, it plays into one of
the biggest misconceptions surrounding e-bikes.
Yes, battery fires are real. Poorly manufactured lithium-ion batteries, damaged packs, improper chargers and other unsafe equipment can create serious fire risks.
But the overwhelming majority of e-bike batteries don’t spontaneously explode, including the enormous number manufactured in China. In fact, China even has
stronger e-bike battery regulations than the US
, believe it or not.
The real distinction isn’t simply “Chinese versus non-Chinese.” It’s properly engineered and certified equipment versus questionable batteries, chargers and components without adequate quality control.
Ironically, Kenny’s bike eventually does explode – but not because its battery spontaneously combusts. A gang of middle-aged spandex cyclists literally put a bomb on it (but more on that in a moment).
And somehow the e-bike still gets blamed. It’s classic South Park-ian beating a dead horse to demonstrate victim-blaming.
The spandex cyclists might be the best joke
Perhaps my favorite part of the episode is Randy Marsh, Stan’s father, becoming radicalized against e-bikes.
Stan’s mother explains that he can’t get an e-bike because, beyond the high price and perceived danger, his father already hates e-bikers because he’s a traditional cyclist who thinks they ride too fast and take over his bike lanes.
Soon, Randy has assembled the town’s middle-aged cyclists into an actual biker gang, complete with full irony here. As their spandex-clad gang grows into a giant peloton, motorists become furious because they can’t get around them.
That’s a complaint cyclists have heard for decades. Traditional cyclists spent generations being accused of taking over roads, slowing down traffic, ignoring laws, and generally not belonging there. Now some of those same criticisms are being leveled at e-bike riders – sometimes by cyclists themselves.
South Park takes that tribalism to its logical extreme, with Randy’s cycling gang literally raiding e-bike shops to destroy their e-bikes and assault the owners. When police hear that a “biker gang” is attacking stores, they immediately assume it must be the kids on e-bikes.
The e-bikers have become such convenient villains that they get blamed even when the cyclists are causing the trouble.
But the episode also understands why kids love e-bikes
Buried underneath all the absurdity is perhaps the most accurate observation in the entire episode.
After being unable to convince their parents to buy them e-bikes, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny secretly buy e-bikes with their own money. They cruise the streets together with them and enjoy riding trails together in the woods after school.
The kids remark on how great it is and how independent they feel. Stan points out that instead of sitting inside staring at their phones, they’re outside, actually doing something.
It’s actually one of the more understated segments of the episode, touching on part of the e-bike conversation that frequently gets lost.
For teenagers who can’t drive yet – and especially in US communities where getting virtually anywhere independently otherwise requires a car – an e-bike can represent an enormous amount of freedom.
It can mean getting to school, visiting friends, going to work, or simply exploring without asking Mom or Dad for a ride.
It makes the contrast even more stark with the perfect line delivered by the spandex-clad Randy, capturing the contradiction of the resulting moral panic when the town reacts to the growing numbers of kids riding around on e-bikes: “Somebody needs to do something! We need to get these kids off the streets and back inside, on their phones.”
Sure, it’s South Park exaggeration, but there’s a real point hiding underneath it.
We complain that kids spend too much time staring at screens. Then, when they discover a form of transportation that gets them outside with their friends, we overreact and try to ban it.
And then everybody bans e-bikes
Eventually, Kenny tries to explain to the spandex cyclists’ biker gang that most e-bike riders aren’t hooligans. He and his friends ride responsibly. He wants the adults to understand what e-bikes give kids like him. He wants to explain to them the independence, the camaraderie of shared experiences, the ability to exist in a third place without bothering anyone.
Then his bike explodes.
Again, not because of its battery – because Randy’s spandex bike gang planted a bomb on it.
But that distinction quickly disappears.
Kenny’s death becomes the social proof that e-bikes are dangerous, and the entire town rallies around banning them. Police confiscate every e-bike in town, loading them in the back of lifted pickup trucks to haul the bikes away while the kids are left slowly trudging back to school on foot.
It’s ridiculous, but it’s yet another sharp piece of satire in the episode, where one spectacular incident becomes representative of an entire category of transportation. The behavior of the worst riders becomes representative of every rider. And instead of targeting dangerous behavior, inappropriate vehicles, or unsafe equipment, the easiest political solution is simply getting rid of the thing everyone has decided is the problem.
Of course, South Park isn’t an e-bike policy documentary. It’s South Park. Everything is intentionally pushed well beyond reality. But underneath the explosions and absurdity, the episode gets something surprisingly important right.
There are legitimate problems surrounding today’s e-bike boom. Kids riding high-powered machines irresponsibly is one of them. Vehicles being marketed as e-bikes despite operating outside established electric bicycle classifications is another. Battery safety deserves serious attention, too.
But none of those problems means that e-bikes themselves are inherently the problem.
For millions of riders – including plenty of teenagers – they’re simply bicycles that let people travel farther, climb hills more easily, and experience a degree of transportation independence they might not otherwise have.
So yes, South Park spent 22 minutes making fun of e-bikes. Yet somehow, by the end, it also made a pretty compelling case for them.

title: Tesla and Sunrun's virtual power plant dispatch record 580 MW to California grid
content:
Tesla Virtual Power Plant
Fred Lambert
| Sep 21 2026 - 6:03 am PT
Sunrun and Tesla pulled a record 580 megawatts of power from home batteries onto California’s grid during a heat wave on September 9, the largest residential distributed power plant event ever recorded.
The dispatch pooled more than 140,000 home batteries across the state and ran for a three-hour window in the evening, when the grid was straining under air-conditioning load.
How the 580 MW came together
Of the 140,000-plus batteries, about 110,000 were Tesla Powerwalls, and Sunrun says it owns or operates 55% of them. Those Powerwalls delivered 517 MW. Another 30,000-plus batteries from other manufacturers in Sunrun’s fleet added the remaining 63 MW.
Put together, that’s enough to power every household in Sacramento County during peak hours. Not bad for a “power plant” with no smokestack and no land of its own.
The batteries fed the grid through two existing California programs: the California Energy Commission’s Demand Side Grid Support (DSGS) program and the California Public Utilities Commission’s Emergency Load Reduction Program (ELRP). DSGS triggered automatically once the day-ahead price crossed $200 per megawatt-hour, while utilities called the ELRP event directly as the heat wave peaked.
It didn’t stop there. The next evening, September 10, Sunrun dispatched another 140-plus MW at Southern California Edison’s request.
A virtual power plant the size of a real one
“Sunrun’s distributed home batteries are operating at a scale larger than many peaker power plants combined,” said Sunrun CEO Mary Powell.
She’s not exaggerating. A typical natural gas peaker plant (the expensive, rarely-used units utilities fire up only when demand spikes) runs in the 50 to 250 MW range. Sunrun and Tesla just beat several of them at once, using hardware that was already sitting in people’s garages.
This is the model Tesla and Sunrun have been building toward for years. We covered the
original 2020 deal that made Sunrun Tesla’s biggest Powerwall installer
, and the concept goes back even further to
Tesla’s virtual power plant experiments
that turned individual Powerwalls into grid assets homeowners get paid to share.
The scale has climbed fast since then. In June,
Tesla, Sunrun, and Renew Home announced a 16.8 GW virtual power plant aimed at data centers
, pitching home batteries and smart thermostats as a way to feed AI-driven power demand without building new transmission. This week’s 580 MW dispatch is the residential version of that same bet, running live on the grid.
Why it matters for the grid
Distributed batteries solve a problem utilities keep throwing money at. Peak demand lasts a few hours a day, a handful of days a year, and covering it usually means building or firing up plants that sit idle the rest of the time.
A fleet of home batteries covers the same peak without any of that overhead. A
Brattle Group report cited by Sunrun projects up to $206 million in net savings for Californians by 2028
Electrek’s Take
This is the argument for home solar and storage that is hard to counter. A grid that leans on 140,000 garages instead of a new peaker plant is cheaper, faster to stand up, and it puts money back in homeowners’ pockets instead of a utility’s rate base. And it’s already running, at a scale that competes with real power plants.
The open question is how far this scales before it starts eating into the business case for utility-scale storage and gas peakers outright. California has the batteries, the programs, and the price signals lined up. Most states don’t yet. But 580 MW is a hard number to argue with, and every grid operator watching a heat wave this summer just got a look at what a few hundred thousand home batteries can actually do.
If you are putting solar and a battery on your roof, events like this are how that hardware pays you back — your battery can earn money feeding the grid when demand peaks. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. title: Volkswagen's new ID. Cross brings a more affordable electric SUV to the lineup
content:
Volkswagen
Peter Johnson
| Sep 21 2026 - 7:14 am PT
ID. Cross
is a “true Volkswagen,” adding a more affordable electric SUV to the lineup with prices starting at around $32,000.
Volkswagen ID. Cross enters production
Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer announced that the ID. Cross has entered series production at its Pamplona, Spain, plant.
The ID. Cross “opens its electric chapter,” Schäfer said, joining its gas-powered equivalent, the T-Cross, and the Skoda Epiq at Volkswagen Navarra.
Volkswagen invested heavily to upgrade the facility for producing electric vehicles, including the ID. Cross and Skoda Epiq.
The ID. Cross is “a true Volkswagen,” according to Schäfer, as a “modern, reliable, and above all, affordable” electric SUV. VW’s CEO said “electric mobility should not be a promise for a few. It should be a real choice for many.”
As the first SUV from its new family of smaller, entry-level EVs, and an electric equivalent to its best-selling T-Cross, the ID. Cross is expected to play a key role as Volkswagen revamps its lineup to compete with Tesla and Chinese automakers like BYD.
Volkswagen
opened orders for the ID. Cross
in July, starting at €36,525 in Germany, or around $42,000. Next month, it will launch the lower-priced Trend model, starting at €27,995 or roughly $32,000.
It’s available with two battery packs: a 37 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pack and a 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) pack, providing a WLTP range of up to 427 km (265 miles).
The electric SUV is based on the same MEB+ platform as the ID. Polo and is offered in three output levels and trims :
VW ID. Cross Trend:
standard with 85 kW (114 hp) and 37‑kWh battery
VW ID. Cross Life and ID. Cross Style:
standard with 99 kW (132 hp) and 37‑kWh battery
VW ID. Cross Life and ID. Cross Style:
optional with 155 kW (207 hp) and 52‑kWh battery
With DC fast charging up to 90 kW, the 37-kWh battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 23 minutes. The 52 kWh battery takes around 24 minutes with DC fast charging of up to 105 kW.
Inside, the ID. Cross adopts Volkswagen’s new digital cockpit. The setup includes a 10.25″ “Digital Cockpit Pro” instrument display and a 12.9″ center infotainment screen.
Volkswagen ID. Cross concept interior (Source: Volkswagen)
Like the ID. Polo, the electric SUV features a new Retro Display mode that transforms the instrument panel into a throwback theme reminiscent of the first-gen Golf 1.
Measuring 4,161 mm long, 1,794 mm wide, and 1,588 mm high, with a 2,601 mm wheelbase, the ID. Cross is about the size of the current Volkswagen T-Cross.
Volkswagen ID. Cross (Source: Volkswagen)
Thanks to a flat battery pack and floor design, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 475 liters of interior storage space, 20 liters more than the T-Cross.
, the ID. Cross starts at €36,525 ($42,000), including VAT, and sits between the T-Cross (€25,280) and Tiguan (€39,385) in price.
Volkswagen said the standard ID. Cross Trend with 85 kW output and a 37 kWh battery will go on sale in mid-October, with prices starting at €27,995 ($32,000), or slightly more than the ID. Polo (€24,995).

title: 1.25GWh！远景能源、隆基等4企海外储能业务获新进展
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，中国储能企业海外订单及项目持续落地，海辰储能、远景能源、隆基、赢科数能分别在印度、摩洛哥、澳大利亚等多个市场取得新进展。
海辰储能签1GWh储能电芯供应协议
9月18日，海辰储能与印度能源企业Advait Energy Transitions旗下Advait Battery Ecosystem签署主供应协议，计划在未来一年向其供应1GWh磷酸铁锂电芯。
根据协议，海辰储能将供应314Ah方形LFP电芯，产品主要用于Advait在印度建设的储能系统组装工厂。该工厂位于印度古吉拉特邦Gangad，规划年产能2.5GWh，主要面向电网级储能和工商业储能市场。
远景能源供货摩洛哥储能项目
近日，远景能源在摩洛哥落地的25MW/125MWh储能项目正式并网，项目位于OCP本盖里尔矿区，是摩洛哥首个大型储能项目。
该项目由摩洛哥绿色能源公司OCP Green Energy开发，远景能源提供核心储能设备，项目投资额近1700万美元，并作为OCP旗下202MW光伏项目的配套储能工程。
隆基澳大利亚项目并网投运
近日，隆基位于澳大利亚南澳州Strathalbyn的Lunio Energy储能项目完成并网，并进入澳大利亚全国电力市场（NEM）参与交易。
该项目部署4套LONGiBank 2.0储能系统，正式投运后将根据NEM实时电力供需及市场价格进行充放电，参与电力市场运行。Strathalbyn也是Lunio Energy首个投入运营的储能资产。
赢科数能海外储能签约交付超120MWh
近日，赢科数能多批次储能产品完成海外签约及交付，项目覆盖德国、奥地利、英国、巴基斯坦、菲律宾等市场，累计规模超过120MWh。
项目主要围绕Stars CL289Pro、Stars CL261系列工商业储能系统展开，应用于独立储能、电力交易、光储融合、备用电源等场景。
其中，德国市场落地250台Stars CL289Pro工商业储能柜，项目规模达31.25MW/72.25MWh，主要面向独立储能市场化运营。巴基斯坦、菲律宾项目则采用光伏+储能备用电源模式。

title: 天合光能等3企新签光伏组件订单
content:
近期，天合光能、电投新能、纤纳光电分别新签德国、泰国及国内项目订单。
天合光能签署德国74MW组件供货协议
近日，天合光能与MaxSolar达成新供货协议，将为其位于德国的5座光伏电站项目供应最新至尊3代组件。
根据协议，此次供货规模为74MW，全部采用天合光能至尊3代组件，预计于2026年第四季度完成交付。
此次合作是双方既有合作的延续，过去5年天合光能向MaxSolar累计供货规模已达1.55GW。
电投新能获泰国30MW HJT组件订单
近日，电投新能与泰国JJ Energy Company Limited签署独家合作协议。根据协议，2026年至2027年期间，JJ Energy将作为电投新能在泰国市场的独家合作伙伴，双方将围绕HJT组件在泰国及东南亚市场的应用展开合作。
此次合作首批交付容量为30MW，全部采用电投新能G12-132 HJT组件，主要用于泰国工商业屋顶光伏项目。
纤纳光电获大唐异质结组件采购订单
近日，大唐电子商务平台发布四川公司丹巴新能源公司甘孜丹巴巴底光伏发电项目示范方阵2000V及1500V异质结双玻双面单晶光伏组件谈判采购结果，纤纳光电科技（浙江）股份有限公司中标该项目。
本次采购产品为N型异质结HJT双玻光伏组件，采购数量为571.5块，税率为13%，需用日期为2026年10月31日，交货地点为四川省甘孜藏族自治州丹巴县美人谷商务中心。

title: 晶澳试水太空光伏！p-HJT产品完成太空在轨验证发射
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月17日，晶澳自主研发、封装制备的p-HJT光伏产品，搭乘快舟11号运载火箭在酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空，顺利进入预定轨道。
此次试验，是晶澳首次以大规模商业化应用为目标，开展的p-HJT产品太空在轨验证。
当前，随着商业航天产业的发展，太空经济持续推进，太阳能是卫星系统主要能源方案。在此背景下，行业正持续探索具备成本优势的太空光伏技术路线，以此适配低轨星座等各类空间场景的发展需求。
晶澳首席技术官欧阳子介绍，经过多年规模化量产与多场景应用验证，晶澳地面光伏产品的性能和长期稳定性已经得到市场的充分验证。本次太空在轨试验，是将地面成熟的晶硅光伏技术拓展应用至太空环境，同时也是晶澳布局未来空间能源的关键一步。
项目将依托在轨实测，研究p-HJT电池在低轨环境下的可靠性与衰减特性，探索晶硅路线打造高性价比空间能源方案的可行性。空间能源技术验证周期较长，仍需持续开展试验。
晶澳表示，本次卫星发射入轨后，晶澳p-HJT组件将直接暴露于太空环境，面临强辐射、高能粒子冲击以及高低温交变等极端考验。通过持续对比地面模拟数据与太空实证数据，晶澳将系统评估p-HJT产品在低轨空间场景下的长期可靠性与衰减表现。
若本次在轨实证达成预设目标，将加速成熟的晶硅产业链在低轨场景中逐步替代砷化镓，降低卫星电源系统成本，助力卫星互联网、遥感观测、空间通信、太空算力等低轨星座相关产业生态建设。
晶澳表示，将以本次实证为基础，持续精进组件研发与制造技术，推进太空光伏产品技术成熟，为商业航天与空间探索提供更具竞争力的规模化能源方案。
需要注意的是，当前太空光伏整体技术尚处于探索验证阶段，暂未实现规模化产业落地，商业化前景存在重大不确定性。
晶澳表示，截至目前，暂未取得太空光伏相关订单，该业务对公司当前经营业绩暂无实质性贡献。

title: First 250 kW AEM stacks enter commercial operation | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
The 500 kW system, built from two 250 kW stacks and delivered to the site in August 2026, is described by P2H2 as the first commercial deployment of 250 kW AEM stacks – more than ten times larger than the stacks used in conventional AEM systems, which typically range from 2 kW to 25 kW.
Now operational, the system will initially produce up to 70 tonnes of green hydrogen per year. Regional gas supplier Holthausen is named as the primary offtaker, with additional industrial and mobility customers in the area. The system’s 10–100% operating range allows it to follow Belgium’s day-ahead electricity prices, ramping up when renewable power is cheapest.
P2H2 said it plans to use operational data from the Antwerp deployment to support a move toward larger platforms, including multi-megawatt systems. A second commercial order – a 500 kW dual-250 kW stack system supporting the EU-funded PYROCO2 green-chemicals project – will be delivered to Norwegian research institute SINTEF later in 2026. The Antwerp project has received partial support from the European Regional Development Fund and the Flemish innovation and entrepreneurship fund administered by VLAIO, with total EU and Flemish investment reported at close to €900,000.
Paul Matter, Chief Executive Officer of Power to Hydrogen, said: “Bringing this system online in one of Europe’s most demanding industrial environments is how we answer the skepticism around AEM: not with claims, but with hardware on the ground. Antwerp is the first step in showing that AEM can be real, durable and repeatable, and that it can help bring down the cost of green hydrogen where it matters most.”
Carl Holthausen, Director and CTO of Holthausen, said: “We have been selling hydrogen long enough to know that the demand for zero-emission hydrogen is real. What continues to hold the market back is access to reliable supply at a price customers can plan around. A dedicated local source gives us the confidence to quote our customers against a known cost and dependable volume, rather than being exposed to changing market conditions.”

title: Velonix supports H₂ pipeline in-line inspection runs
content:
The project marked the first hydrogen-service pipeline application for Velonix®, enabling multiple in-line inspection (ILI) runs to be completed after previous attempts without the system’s control had failed.
Hydrogen can damage ILI magnets and is more compressible than natural gas or nitrogen, making PIG speed and tool velocity difficult to control. During an earlier attempt, an uncontrolled speed excursion destroyed the multi-million-dollar ILI tool and resulted in the complete loss of inspection data.
For the completed runs, the digital flow skid, valves, materials, and sealing systems were reconfigured to meet hydrogen-compatibility requirements. The system reduced and controlled flow velocity in real time while continuously monitoring flow conditions.
Velonix responded to developing speed excursions to suppress or eliminate them before they could escalate. According to Expro, this stabilized PIG velocity during the pipeline integrity operations and protected the inspection equipment from uncontrolled speed events.
Stable tool velocity also enabled the customer to obtain live integrity data through Expro’s Data-to-Desk platform. The company said the data supported faster decision-making and allowed the customer to validate the pipeline’s mechanical integrity in hydrogen service.
Expro also said stabilizing PIG speed reduced the safety and financial risks associated with uncontrolled speed excursions and turned an operation that had previously been unreliable into a controlled, repeatable process.

title: CATL’s New Batteries Target American Pickups. They Could Be Made In The U.S.
content:
The Chinese company sees an opportunity in America despite trade barriers, with local production through licensing as a possibility.
Photo by:
8:58am ET
CATL says U.S. automakers have already tested its new batteries designed specifically for American pickups.
CATL hasn’t disclosed the batteries’ specifications, production timeline, or which U.S. automakers tested them.
Licensing could allow American companies to manufacture the batteries domestically.
Chinese battery giant CATL wants in on the American electric pickup market, and it has already developed batteries specifically for the job. Getting them into trucks, however, will be tricky and likely require American companies to manufacture them locally.
Zhu Lingbo, the chief technology officer of CATL’s international business unit, told the
Financial Times
that the company has created “tall” batteries specially designed for American pickups. U.S. automakers have already tested them, he said, without naming the companies.
The CATL executive spoke Sunday at CATL’s headquarters in China, saying that America offered “huge business” despite “very intense geopolitics.” He noted that licensing the technology to U.S. manufacturers could provide a way in.
More On This
However, the FT report contains no specifics regarding the batteries’ chemistry, dimensions, performance, or production time frame. It also doesn’t point to an actual customer that has agreed to use them.
We do know that
Ford’s upcoming Fathom electric pickup
will use Michigan-made
LFP cells
built with CATL technology. It’s unclear whether Ford’s cells relate to the newly disclosed design, but the arrangement shows how CATL’s technology could reach American pickups.
CATL’s American ambitions also predate this announcement. Company chairman Robin Zeng had previously expressed
willingness to build a U.S. factory
, if it were allowed. Tesla provides another licensing precedent, although its Nevada LFP plant manufactures cells for energy storage products, not cars.
Developing batteries specifically for American pickups suggests CATL still sees a market worth pursuing despite the obvious obstacles. Yet political resistance remains strong, with very high tariffs, strict localization requirements, and potential security bans constraining Chinese companies’ access to the American market, regardless of their cost and technology advantages.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The U.S. government designated CATL as having alleged military links in January 2025, which the battery company vehemently denies. Still, getting its technology into more American vehicles will be tricky. CATL said at the time that it would challenge the designation, even through legal means if necessary.
Zhu’s comments come ahead of planned talks in New York between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China’s He Lifeng, and a summit in Washington, D.C. between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. After meeting in Beijing in May, the two presidents are expected to discuss AI, rare earth supplies, and the November deadline for the trade truce between the two countries.
Ford’s experience shows both the appeal and the complications. During
our visit to Ford’s Michigan battery plant
, we learned that the automaker licensed CATL technology to build cheaper EVs and create American manufacturing jobs. But the arrangement still
drew opposition from the Trump administration
. CATL’s pickup batteries could follow a similar path, but making them in America won’t necessarily settle the argument over where the technology comes from and whether it’s acceptable to use it.

title: Hyundai Recalls Ioniq 9 EV Because Rear Seats Could Trap Children
content:
The carmaker has received five consumer complaints, including two about alleged minor injuries.
Photo by:
Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
8:59am ET
Hyundai is recalling certain 2026 Ioniq 9 EVs in the United States.
The big electric family SUV’s rear seats could trap children when the power-folding function is activated.
A software update fixes the problem, but over 5,000 cars are affected.
Hyundai Ioniq 9
electric SUV is one of the best family cars out there, but it’s now affected by a potential issue that can put a dent in its family-friendly character.
A total of 5,360 2026-model-year Ioniq 9s sold in the United States may trap children in their second-row seats when the power-folding feature is activated because the cars can’t properly detect if there’s someone sitting in them.
Photo by: Suvrat Kothari
The automaker has launched a
safety recall
that affects
EVs with the Limited, Calligraphy, or Calligraphy Design trim packages, and the fix is just a software update away. However, until the fix is applied, Hyundai is urging owners of potentially affected cars to “exercise caution when operating the second-row power-folding seat functions.”
During a three-month investigation, the South Korean company found that the anti-pinch behavior in the second row of seating in the Ioniq 9 was not up to par, so it decided to roll out a safety recall to address the issue. While investigating the problem, five complaints were filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), including two for alleged minor injuries.
The remedy is a revised logic for the software that controls the anti-pinch protection for the rear seats. Hyundai said that dealers will inspect the seats and install the updated Seat Controller software for free. Owners who have opted to get over-the-air software updates through Hyundai Bluelink will get the fix as a wireless update to their car’s brain.
Hyundai is not alone in this problem, though it seems to have figured out a solution from the get-go. Earlier this year,
General Motors
recalled over
14,000 Vistiq electric SUVs
because their third-row seats could trap kids, but GM’s fix included a new seat control module that wasn’t available yet when the recall campaign started. The temporary solution was to disable the power-folding seats altogether, which didn’t look great on an $80,000+ luxury SUV.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
This is the third and biggest recall by far for the Hyundai Ioniq 9, which has proven to be quite problem-free. The first recall, affecting just 27 vehicles, was related to the high-voltage battery, while the second recall, with 172 cars, was over potentially loose rear suspension fasteners.
But even with such a relatively clean record, Hyundai is having a pretty hard time selling its biggest EV. Through the first eight months of 2026, the electric SUV sold 6,147 units in the U.S., with only 589 cars going to new owners in August.

title: Nissan's New Rogue Is A Different Kind Of Hybrid. Here's How Much It Costs.
content:
Nissan's New Rogue Is A Different Kind Of Hybrid. Here's How Much It Costs.
The 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid gets a unique hybrid powertrain that’s different from its rivals.
- Nissan's long-awaited Rogue Hybrid goes on sale in America.
- Its starting price is nearly the same as the Honda CR-V Hybrid.
- The Rogue Hybrid gets a unique drivetrain that makes it drive like an EV most of the time.
Nissan has revealed the pricing of the all-new fourth-generation Rogue in the U.S. The Japanese automaker previously called it the Rogue e:Power, but has now rebadged it simply as the Rogue Hybrid.
The 2027 Rogue Hybrid will start at $37,065 including $1,575 in destination charges. That makes its starting price nearly identical to the Honda CR-V, but well over the Toyota RAV4, which starts at $33,495 and is now hybrid-only. The Rogue will also come in non-hybrid versions later. The Rogue Hybrid’s top Platinum AWD trim will set you back by $45,065.
"Hybrids are increasingly becoming the powertrain of choice for U.S. customers, and we believe that trend will only accelerate," Christian Meunier, the chairman of Nissan Americas, said in a press release.
Gallery: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid
The Rogue Hybrid arrives at a time when hybrid sales are on a tear in the U.S., boosted even more by the high gas prices due to the U.S. war in Iran. It’s late to the market compared to its rivals, but the timing couldn’t have been better.
Unlike its rivals, though, it gets a unique hybrid drivetrain. The Rogue Hybrid drives more like an electric vehicle, with only the electric motors driving the wheels. The combustion engine does not have a mechanical connection to the wheels—it’s only there as a generator, charging the 2.0 kilowatt-hour battery, which powers the motors. This is a non-plug-in hybrid, so the battery is only charged by the gas engine and energy recovered from regenerative braking.
Nissan said the Rogue Hybrid will deliver north of 40 miles per gallon of fuel economy. If true, that would put it right up there with the new RAV4 and better than the Honda CR-V.
2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid
Other than that, the Rogue packs all the latest technology and features you’d expect in this price range. It gets a 14.3-inch infotainment screen that will be standard on the Platinum trim and optional on the SR. This larger screen also gets Google built-in with Gemini support. A 12.3-inch screen will be standard on the rest of the trims with wireless Carplay and Android Auto. It will also get the ProPilot Assist advanced driver assistance system with automatic lane changes and supervised hands-off driving in traffic jams.
Only the SR AWD with SR Technology Package will be available this fall. The rest of the trims will be available by early 2027.
Here's the full price list for the 2027 Rogue Hybrid:

| Rogue Hybrid SV AWD | $37,065 |
| Rogue Hybrid SV AWD with SV Premium Package | $39,165 |
| Rogue Hybrid SR AWD | $39,065 |
| Rogue Hybrid SR AWD with SR Technology Package | $43,065 |
| Rogue Hybrid Platinum AWD | $45,065 |

title: Scania's New EV Truck Has 447 Miles Of Range
content:
Scania's New EV Truck Has 447 Miles Of Range
A new battery system and an aerodynamically optimized cab give Scania’s electric big rig an edge over the Tesla Semi.
- Sweden’s Scania found a way to boost the range of its electric big rigs.
- By placing additional batteries behind the cab, Scania can increase the energy capacity by up to 356 kWh.
- MCS charging at up to 750 kW completes the picture.
Scania, the Swedish truck maker owned by the Volkswagen Group, is now offering a battery solution that boosts the driving range of its electric big rigs up to 447 miles (720 kilometers). That’s more than most truck drivers in Europe will ever have to experience between mandatory breaks, but Scania has done it anyway.
Scania electric truck with additional behind-the-cab batteries
To enable the impressive driving range, which is 106 miles longer than what the European-spec Tesla Semi is capable of, Scania also introduced a slightly more aerodynamic design, dubbed the protruding Increased Vehicle Dimension (IVD) cab. Catchy, I know.
Weird name aside, the truck maker claims the more slippery cab can reduce energy consumption by up to 3% compared to the conventional design, which can add up quickly on long trips. With the additional batteries and slightly longer cab, Scania said its 6x2 tractor can comfortably tow a dual-axle European trailer even if the total vehicle length exceeds 54.1 feet (16.5 meters).
“This is not only about placing batteries in a new position on the vehicle. The larger point is what it enables: electric transport over distances that have traditionally been among the hardest to electrify, with range, payload and charging considered together from the start,” said Lars Gustafsson, Senior Vice President, Head of Solutions Management, Scania.
It’s an impressive achievement that gives Scania—and the Volkswagen Group—bragging rights in the trucking industry. Besides the new long-range Scania EV trucks, the latest-generation MAN eTGX, which is also built by the VW Group, delivers an identical 447-mile range on a full charge, courtesy of a 6x2 chassis and 616 kWh of usable energy.
Gallery: Scania Long-Range Electric Truck With Behind-The-Cab Batteries
MCS charging at up to 750 kW is also part of the package, though CCS charging at up to 375 kW is also an option.
However, it’s worth noting that the larger batteries add quite a bit of weight to the vehicle, which in turn means the payload capacity has to suffer. Scania didn’t disclose how much stuff its new long-range truck can haul, but it’s clear that it will be less than a shorter-range model with a lighter battery.

title: This VW ID. Buzz Finished A 62,000-Mile World Trip With Nearly 96% Battery Health
content:
The electric van visited 92 countries in 445 days, and Volkswagen says it completed the entire trip without a single technical breakdown.
Photo by:
Volkswagen
4:40am ET
A VW ID. Buzz traveled around the world for 445 days, through 92 countries without a technical breakdown.
Its battery health was measured at 95.75% after the trip.
The VW-backed expedition shows what an EV can do with careful planning—even where public chargers are scarce.
Automakers have realized that nostalgia can really help sell EVs. The
Volkswagen ID. Buzz
cashes in on that with lots of retro-inspired charm, but it also needs to handle long-distance travel. Rainer Zietlow took that to the extreme with an around-the-world trip in an ID. Buzz, complete with a battery-health check at the end.
Zietlow is a German long-distance driver and founder of expedition company Challenge4. With support from Volkswagen and other partners, he covered 61,992 miles (99,767 kilometers), driving the Buzz through 92 countries across six continents. The van needed 16 container ship crossings to complete the route.
The journey began at Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles’ Hanover customer center in July 2025 and finished at the city’s IAA Transportation show in September 2026. At the end, a Guinness representative presented the award for the most countries visited during a continuous journey in an electric vehicle.
Gallery: VW ID. Buzz World Tour
Volkswagen says the trip took 445 days, involved more than 300 charging stops, and concluded without a single breakdown.
As you can imagine, charging the Buzz in countries with less developed EV infrastructure was a challenge. In Zambia and Tanzania, for instance, Zietlow says he had to plug directly into national electrical substations under supervision because he couldn’t find any dedicated EV chargers.
South Africa
, Morocco, and Rwanda were easier. He even notes that at a Rwandan airport located at an altitude of around 6,600 feet (2,000 meters), he encountered a fleet of ID. Buzz vans being used as shuttle taxis.
He describes Saudi Arabia’s network as approaching Germany’s, praises progress in Brazil and Chile, and puts China in a league of its own. With planning, he argues,
long-distance EV travel
avoids problems including contaminated or low-quality fuel, oil changes, and typical combustion engine problems such as overheating.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
TÜV Nord tested the Buzz’s battery both before and after the trip. We don’t know the exact battery health reading at the start—presumably it was brand new and in perfect condition—but it was 95.75% when the van was tested upon its return to Germany.
Overall, this is a very encouraging result for both the ID. Buzz and EVs in general. VW’s electric retro van still has its limitations like any EV, such as
a significant range drop in cold weather
. When we took one on a road trip from Ohio to Michigan, it proved it could handle sustained highway driving just fine, delivering
around 230 miles of real-world range
at an average speed of 64 mph (103 km/h), almost matching its EPA rating.

title: Volvo’s CEO Is Out. Again.
content:
Volvo’s CEO Is Out. Again.
Håkan Samuelsson came out of retirement less than two years ago to steer the brand in the right direction.
- Volvo Cars is replacing its chief executive officer yet again.
- The Swedish brand poached one of the biggest Volkswagen Group executives to replace Håkan Samuelsson.
- Last year, the company’s board voted to bring back Samuelsson, who led the automaker when it was developing the SPA architecture.
Volvo Cars is getting a new CEO, again. The company’s board of directors has appointed Klaus Zellmer as President and chief executive officer of the brand, less than two years after bringing back Håkan Samuelsson to steer the marque in the right direction.
It’s a big win for the Swedish automaker, which has been struggling to keep its sales figures in the green and profitability high in the past few quarters. Zellmer, who will take over from Samuelsson no later than October 1, 2027, has over three decades of experience in the automotive industry, with two decades spent at the Volkswagen Group, where he’s currently the CEO of Skoda.
Klaus Zellmer, the new CEO of Volvo Cars, will take over from Samuelsson in 2027.
In his current position, Zellmer transformed Skoda into Europe’s third-largest automaker, with an operating margin of 8.5% in the first half of 2026. That number is especially important for Volvo, which is aiming for a similar figure by 2030 as part of the biggest product push in its history. But getting there won’t be easy, as the Geely-owned premium marque was at 3.5% last year, and manufacturing costs in Sweden are much higher than in Czechia.
No fewer than 13 new models are scheduled to debut until the end of 2030, with six launches slated for Europe and the United States, and an additional seven developed specifically for China. During the strategy update, Volvo emphasized that the key to its success is regionalization, with each region getting bespoke cars built locally.
Thankfully, Zellmer, Volvo’s upcoming boss, has a lot of experience managing an ever-changing auto industry with a knack for electrification. Last year, the Skoda Elroq was Europe’s second-best-selling EV, after the Tesla Model Y, while the larger Enyaq crossover ranked fifth, according to Dataforce.
Zellmer took over the Czech automaker in 2022 and has plenty of experience in Europe, but he also made his presence felt in the United States, where he led Porsche’s North American division between 2015 and 2020. During his tenure here, the automaker’s U.S. sales rose to a record 61,568 units in 2019 from 51,756 in 2015.
“Klaus Zellmer combines deep automotive expertise with broad international leadership experience and a strong record of guiding organisations through transformation and changing market conditions,” says Eric Li, Chairman of Volvo Cars. “His experience from both the high-end premium segment and high-volume brands is an excellent fit for Volvo Cars. The Board is confident that, under Klaus Zellmer’s leadership, Volvo Cars will build on its strong foundations and enter its next chapter with a clear ambition to strengthen its position as a leading premium car company.”
When Samuelsson came back in 2025, Volvo said that his tenure would only last two years, while it looked for a long-term successor. Now, that successor has been found.

title: CMF 将脱离 Nothing 独立运营，成为一家印度本土企业
content:
IT之家 9 月 21 日消息，瑞典华裔企业家裴宇（Carl Pei）计划将 Nothing 旗下的平价手机与消费电子业务板块分拆出来，组建一家由印度资本控股的独立新公司。裴宇押注印度即将成长为下一个全球消费电子产业中心。
当地时间周一，Nothing 联合创始人兼首席执行官裴宇在 X 平台发布题为《印度是大势所趋》（India Is Inevitable）的文章表示，CMF 将会作为独立企业运营，在印度设立专属的管理团队与研发团队。总部位于伦敦的 Nothing 仍会保留该业务的部分股份，他称：“我们正将 CMF 从 Nothing 中拆分出来，打造一家独立的印度公司：由印度人控股，总部设在印度，拥有本土团队和研发中心。Nothing 仍将作为股东和合作伙伴，而 CMF 将成为印度本土企业。”
市场调研机构 Counterpoint 的数据显示，在截至 6 月的季度当中，Nothing 是印度增长速度最快的手机品牌，出货量较去年同期实现翻倍。在全球手机市场基本由苹果、三星以及中国头部手机厂商把持的格局之下，印度已经成为 Nothing 至关重要的市场。
曾联合创立一加（OnePlus）的裴宇提出，印度有望继日本、韩国、中国之后，诞生具备全球影响力的消费电子企业。他认为印度已经搭建起可以参与全球竞争的制造业基础，但产品工程能力以及研发实力仍有待补强。“目前印度尚且缺少属于自己的全球性消费电子品牌。但这一局面终将改变。”
IT之家注意到，早在今年 2 月，Nothing 就在班加罗尔开出了自家第一家旗舰门店，以此推进在印度市场的整体扩张。CMF 主打平价智能手机以及周边配件，帮助品牌触达更多对价格敏感的消费者群体。

content:
感谢IT之家网友
9 月 21 日消息，华为 Mate 60、Mate X5、Pura 70 等系列老机型已在 9 月 17 日提前开启了
HarmonyOS
7 系统的花粉 Beta 版升级活动。用户可前往设置 → 软件更新处报名尝鲜。报名成功的用户点击系统更新后就可以获得新版本推送。

官方更新日志显示，此次新版本升级了沉浸光感、3D 空间壁纸、华为分享等功能，同时还下放了超空间存储、超空间内存技术等，整机性能提升。然而，更新日志并未公开全部升级亮点，IT之家盘点老机型升级鸿蒙 7 后的“隐藏”新功能如下：
沉浸光感粒子动效实装：支持滑动消除通知消息通知栏化作光感粒子飘散、卡片移除 / App 卸载如星光消散、音量 / 亮度条调节伴随光感粒子等效果（沉浸光感处于“均衡”可触发）。
锁屏新增可调时钟样式：支持手动拉伸 / 缩短时钟大小、开关景深效果。

状态栏优化：时钟内收，跳转应用后会提供前一个应用快捷回跳按钮。
超级省电模式回归：进入黑色省电桌面、限制使用应用范围、降低系统运行性能、减弱显示视觉效果、限制应用后台活动、加严后台同步机制、电量低于 10% 后，关闭小艺语音唤醒。
新增户外探索模式：集户外导航、长续航、应急通信等为一体的户外专用模式。预置电话、信息、指南针、地图、相机等户外常用应用，还可根据需要添加其他应用；提供户外应急知识，例如户外辨别方向、搭建庇护所、扭伤冻伤等应急内容；支持摩斯码手电筒（默认预置常亮、SOS 两种模式）。

新增内存清理功能（游戏助手）：点击内存清理，实时清理后台内存，减少游戏卡顿。需系统版本 7.0 及以上、应用助手版本 16.4.1.300 及以上。
新增智能稳帧功能（游戏助手）：智能稳帧可提高流畅度，降低功耗发热。老机型暂未发现支持超级帧率档位。
设置-设备缩略图优化：告别清一色的“诗野千里”，会展示所使用设备型号。值得一提的是，Mate 60 系列手机依然显示“诗野千里”，但缩略图经过优化后，会展示前摄模组，符合机型外观特征。

畅连新增共享屏幕功能：可共享自己的屏幕，也可邀请对方共享屏幕。

title: 天文学家新发现：超大质量黑洞并非只搞破坏，其激波可驱动恒星形成
content:
IT之家 9 月 21 日消息，天文学家对 9 个近域星系开展了观测研究，试图弄清星系中心超大质量黑洞产生的激波是如何塑造恒星形成过程的。
该研究团队选取了核心拥有活动星系核（AGN）的星系作为观测对象。活动星系核是明亮且动荡的区域；其动力来自星系中央的超大质量黑洞。这类黑洞质量可达太阳的数百万乃至数十亿倍，正在吞噬大量气体与尘埃。当能量从核心向外涌出、撞击周围被称作星际介质的气体云时，就会生成高速、强劲的激波。
这类激波也被叫做活动星系核反馈（AGN 反馈）。它们向周边环境注入巨量能量，搅动作为恒星形成原料的气体和尘埃。过去人们普遍认为，这类反馈作用会终止星系内部的恒星形成；但科学界很早就猜想，该过程同样也可以反过来触发恒星诞生，进而推动星系的成长与演化。这项新研究就详细还原了该现象发生的机制。
“我们由此看到，黑洞并不只是在星系中心吞噬物质；它们还在主动改造周遭环境。”哈佛‑史密森尼天体物理中心的研究成员莉萨 · 丘利（Lisa Kewley）在一份声明中表示，“这项研究帮助我们理解一套复杂的反馈循环，它在星系演化当中扮演十分关键的角色。”
超大质量黑洞：恒星的雕刻者
天文学家认为，所有大型星系的中心都存在超大质量黑洞，但并非全部都处于活跃状态。例如银河系核心的人马座 A*（Sgr A*）就相对沉寂。它吞噬物质的速率，差不多相当于一个人类每一百万年吃下一粒米。
另一些超大质量黑洞外围环绕着海量气体尘埃，还有扁平旋转的吸积盘持续向黑洞供给物质。黑洞极强的引力会在吸积盘内部制造巨大摩擦力，使得整个区域焕发出耀眼光芒，也就是活动星系核。
这类活动星系核向外释放辐射；而黑洞“进食”的过程本身并不高效，大量没有被吞噬的物质会沿着两极向外排出。物质以两股等离子体喷流的形式向外猛烈喷发，就如同黑洞打了一个响亮的“嗝”；喷流可以延伸数千光年之远。由此可见，超大质量黑洞与活动星系核对周边星际环境具备极强的影响力。
研究团队借助甚大望远镜（VLT）以及多单元光谱探测器（MUSE），观测那些正在吸积物质的活动星系核。
“当我们把观测分辨率提升之后就可以发现，黑洞除了吸积物质之外，同时还向外抛射物质。”来自该天体物理中心的朱培新（Peixin Zhu）在声明当中指出，物质向内吸积与向外喷射，二者是互相关联的。
科研人员开展三维分析，同时解析活动星系核及其周遭环境的三项要素：来自活动星系核的辐射；激波引发的星际介质激发；以及恒星形成活动。
观测结果显示，成弧形以及环状分布的新生恒星，大多出现在距离星系核心 2600‑20000 光年的范围。研究人员同时看到从吸积盘向外延展的辐射锥；高速激波既扫过星系中心区域，同时还会沿着垂直于辐射锥的方向传播出去。
该激波特征和喷流与星际介质相互作用的理论模型相吻合。团队提出，在喷流强度偏弱的星系当中，黑洞风同样也能够催生激波。
“激波最有意思的特点在于，它传播的方向总是垂直于黑洞向外流出物质的方向。”朱培新表示，该现象十分普遍，在被观测的 9 个星系里面都稳定出现。
该研究证实，正在活跃吸积的黑洞运行着一套复杂的吸积‑外流循环机制，并以此和宿主星系发生相互作用。科学家拆分解析该过程的各个环节之后，比以往更加清晰地还原了这套循环以及它如何影响恒星形成。
IT之家注意到，该团队的论文已于 9 月 14 日正式发表于《天体物理学杂志》（The Astrophysical Journal）。

title: 工信部将优化无线电频谱资源布局，支撑先进制造业发展
content:
IT之家 9 月 21 日消息，据新华社今日报道，工业和信息化部将优化无线电频谱资源布局，充分发挥频谱资源引领无线电技术创新应用、支撑无线电产业发展的作用，夯实产业发展根基。
报道称，发展先进制造业，加快推进新型工业化，离不开稀缺的无线电频谱资源的支撑保障和安全有序的电磁环境。2026 中国无线电大会 21 日在河北雄安新区开幕，工业和信息化部有关负责人在会上说，要做好频谱资源科学规划、精准供给、合理开发、高效利用，让无形的频谱资源释放出有形的巨大能量，为加快构建以先进制造业为骨干的现代化产业体系注入澎湃动能。
上述负责人表示，接下来要建强创新平台，推进无线电科技创新和产业创新融合发展；要提升无线电治理效能，持续健全无线电管理法律法规和制度标准体系，加强无线电监测干扰查处，依法严厉打击非法用频设台行为；要深化开放合作，办好国际电信联盟 2027 年世界无线电通信大会等。
2026 中国无线电大会以“无线创新谱绘未来”为主题，围绕战略前瞻、技术突破和产业实践等举办 1 场主论坛，聚焦频谱高效开发利用等举办 10 场专题研讨会，围绕《中华人民共和国无线电管理条例》修订发布 10 周年等举办 3 场专题交流会。
IT之家查询获悉，2027 年世界无线电通信全会（WRC-27）将于 2027 年 10 月 11 日至 11 月 12 日在中国上海举行。
世界无线电通信大会是国际无线电通信领域立法缔约的最高级别会议，每 3 至 4 年召开一次，主要任务是修订对全球具有普遍法律约束力的《无线电规则》，调整国际无线电频率和卫星轨道资源使用和管理规则，确定未来 5 至 10 年频轨资源开发利用的优先方向，会议成果将对全球 5G / 6G、商业航天等发展产生重要影响。

谷歌将 Googlebook 的目标用户锁定为安卓用户和程序员，力图让自家的 Gemini AI 成为笔记本电脑体验中不可或缺的一环。谷歌并不亲自生产这些设备，而是与五家厂商合作，由它们生产运行类安卓操作系统的笔记本。各机型在价格、设计以及处理器、存储等规格上各有差异，但也有些共同特征：相似的键盘布局，以及一条可显示电量和自定义动画的“Glowbar”灯带。
谷歌的收入主要来自广告和服务业务。负责谷歌安卓（Android）生态的总裁萨米尔 · 萨马特（Sameer Samat）上周在纽约的一场媒体活动上表示，推笔记本的目的在于提供能与安卓手机无缝协作、并搭载“真正实用”的 AI 功能的机器。
在发布前的采访中，萨马特说：“如今人们的工作方式对笔记本体验而言并不够优化。我们看到人们开始在手机上处理工作，然后转到笔记本上继续，反之亦然。”他指出，各平台之间的应用缺乏连贯性。“我们想把笔记本为当下、也为人们未来的使用方式重新造一遍。”
他表示，至少在初期，瞄准安卓爱好者是合理的。“我们决定从安卓社区入手，因为我们确实看到了缺口，”萨马特说，“如果一个人用着安卓设备，那么问题是：以你今天的工作方式，什么样的笔记本才合适？”
当被问及 Googlebook 相对于 MacBook Neo 的定位时，萨马特表示：“我们认为这属于市场中不同的细分领域。”他说，拥有三星电子 Galaxy S26 或谷歌 Pixel 11 Pro 等高端手机的用户，“希望有一台像他们的手机一样精致、高端且性能强劲的笔记本”。他提到的底气包括整机的做工品质，以及谷歌在触控板尺寸、芯片和最低内存配置等方面设定的标准。
萨马特预计，此次发布将激发更多笔记本厂商的兴趣。“随着人们热情高涨，会有更多厂商推出 Googlebook，会有很多不同的参与者想要加入。”他还补充说，未来也可能推出配置更强的机型。
Googlebook 的操作系统与安卓有明显相似之处：预装或可自定义的桌面小组件、类似安卓的应用列表、下拉式设置菜单。同时，它还融合了 ChromeOS 的元素 ——ChromeOS 是 Chromebook 所依托的软件，而 Chromebook 是一类在课堂上随处可见的平价笔记本。谷歌表示，Googlebook 的软件将获得长达 10 年的定期功能更新。
以下是这套混合操作系统的主要能力：
在笔记本上运行手机应用：Mac 和 iPhone 用户早已能够在手机和电脑之间轻松切换处理各项任务。Googlebook 区别于现有 AI PC 的地方在于其同步能力 —— 用户可以在安卓设备上开始某项操作，然后在笔记本上继续，反之亦然。用户还能在笔记本上直接运行安卓手机上的单个应用和游戏，并访问手机中的文件和照片。谷歌表示，希望最终也能实现 Googlebook 与 iPhone 之间的类似互联功能，但这需要时间。
AI 驱动的文件搜索：笔记本采用一个小型 Gemini Nano v3 AI 模型，为设备上的文件和照片生成摘要，让用户能更快地通过关键词和描述搜索文件。该模型“在设备端”运行，意味着文件摘要和搜索查询不会通过互联网处理，以确保隐私。
情境感知：借助名为“Magic Pointer”的新功能，用户可以让 Gemini 聊天机器人回答与屏幕内容相关的问题。用户晃动光标即可激活该功能，它利用设备端 AI 模型理解屏幕上的各类文本和组件，并根据光标指向的内容提供建议查询。用户发出指令后，会弹出 Gemini 聊天窗口，通过互联网给出回答。
借助 Googlebook，谷歌希望为 AI 在笔记本上找到超越噱头的用途。萨马特说：“如今人们觉得 AI 功能能让人更高效，但还没有人能在笔记本上把这件事做对。这些功能要么根本不到位，要么碍手碍脚，纯粹是为 AI 而 AI。我们想要的是 —— 你需要的时候它在那里，不需要的时候它就不打扰你。”

title: Regenwassernutzung in Haushalten und Betrieben: Studie zeigt Potenziale und Herausforderungen für Trinkwassereinsparung
content:
Regenwassernutzung in Haushalten und Betrieben: Studie zeigt Potenziale und Herausforderungen für Trinkwassereinsparung
Durch den Klimawandel werden Trockenphasen häufiger und Wasser muss sparsamer als bisher verwendet werden. Die Nutzung von Regenwasser in Haushalten und Industrie kann wertvolles Süßwasser einsparen. Allerdings gibt es in Deutschland große regionale Unterschiede beim Potenzial der Regenwassernutzung. Unter welchen Bedingungen Regenwasser finanziell und ökologisch gewinnbringend genutzt werden kann, hat das Fraunhofer-Institut für System- und Innovationsforschung ISI im Auftrag des Umweltbundesamts untersucht.
Der Klimawandel verschärft Nutzungskonflikte um die begrenzte Ressource Wasser: Auch in Deutschland sinken regional während Hitzewellen immer häufiger die Grundwasserpegel. Gleichzeitig steigt in solchen Phasen der Wasserbedarf von Haushalten und Landwirtschaft, die beide vorrangig Grundwasser nutzen.
Vor diesem Hintergrund rückt Regen als alternative Wasserressource zunehmend in den Fokus. So benennt die 2023 verabschiedete Nationale Wasserstrategie die Nutzung von Regenwasser als mögliche Maßnahme zur Schonung des Süßwassers. Im Auftrag des Umweltbundesamts haben Forschende des Fraunhofer ISI nun die Potenziale und Herausforderungen der Regenwassernutzung in Deutschland untersucht und bewertet.
In ihrer Studie analysieren die Forschenden die ökologischen, hygienischen, wirtschaftlichen, sozialen und technischen Voraussetzungen und Auswirkungen der Regenwassernutzung anhand verschiedener Szenarien. Um das Einsparpotenzial unter unterschiedlichen Bedingungen zu bewerten, wurden Langzeitsimulationen für drei Regionen mit Berücksichtigung der jeweiligen Bebauungsstruktur und der klimatischen Bedingungen erstellt. Berlin, Köln und München stehen in der Studie beispielhaft für Regionen mit vergleichsweise niedrigen, mittleren und hohen Regenmengen.
Einsparpotenzial und Wirtschaftlichkeit der Regenwassernutzung
Die Simulationen zeigen, dass das Einsparpotenzial für Trinkwasser stark von der Bebauungsdichte und den regionalen Regenmengen abhängt. Auch die Verteilung der Niederschläge über das Jahr und die Größe der verfügbaren Wasserspeicher beeinflussen, wie viel des Bedarfs an Betriebswasser (etwa für Toilettenspülungen oder Waschmaschinen) in verschiedenen Siedlungstypen durch Regenwasser ersetzt werden kann.
Bei Einfamilienhäusern könnte ein großer Teil des Betriebswasserbedarfs mit Regenwasser gedeckt werden, jedoch zumeist nicht kostendeckend. In dicht bebauten Wohnquartieren lässt sich pro Hektar am meisten Trinkwasser einsparen, weil große Dachflächen für die Sammlung von Regenwasser genutzt werden können. Allerdings reicht die Menge des Regenwassers bei dichter Besiedelung nicht aus, um den Betriebswasserbedarf der Bewohner:innen zu decken.
In Berlin könnten in dicht bebauten Siedlungen aktuell rund 40 Prozent der benötigten Betriebswassermenge durch Regenwasser abgedeckt werden, was ungefähr 17 Prozent der derzeitigen Trinkwassernutzung einsparen könnte. In München könnte der Betriebswasserbedarf von dicht bebauten Quartieren sogar zu 70 Prozent durch Regenwasser gedeckt werden, was 24 Prozent des Trinkwassers sparen könnte. Bei Berücksichtigung zukünftiger Trockenperioden könnte diese Bedarfsdeckung jeweils um 10 bis 20 Prozentpunkte sinken. Auch größere Regenwasserspeicher könnten das nicht ausgleichen.
In der Industrie kann dank der großen Dachflächen von Gewerbebetrieben mehr Regenwasser gesammelt werden, als die Belegschaft benötigt. Dadurch gibt es im Gewerbe große Nutzungspotenziale für Regenwasser, etwa zur Kühlung, für die Bewässerung von Grünanlagen oder als Produktionswasser. Unter bestimmten Bedingungen kann sich die Nutzung von Regenwasser für die Betriebe finanziell lohnen. Die Zwischenspeicherung von anfallendem Regenwasser zur späteren Nutzung kann außerdem Abflussspitzen abfedern und so zur Entlastung des Kanalsystems beitragen.
Insgesamt variiert die Wirtschaftlichkeit der Regenwassernutzung stark je nach Region, vor allem wegen unterschiedlicher Wasserpreise, Abwassergebühren und möglicher Vergünstigungen beim Niederschlagswasserentgelt.
Fazit und Empfehlungen für naturnahe Wasserhaushalte in Gemeinden
Kleinere Anlagen für die Regenwassernutzung werden der Untersuchung zufolge zumeist aus ökologischen und idealistischen Motiven betrieben. Im größeren Maßstab, etwa durch die Ausweitung auf Quartiersebene und die Verbindung mit blau-grünen Infrastrukturen in den Städten, könnten die Wirtschaftlichkeit und die ökologischen Vorteile steigen. Wichtige Akteure sind Kommunen mit ihren öffentlichen Gebäuden. Im Rahmen eines integrierten Wassermanagements wäre aber auch die Förderung privater Investitionen geeignet, um Trinkwasserressourcen zu schonen, das Mikroklima zu verbessern und Leitungen zu entlasten.
Kommunen und Länder können hier informieren und einen rechtlichen Rahmen schaffen, um die Umsetzung eines naturnahen Wasserhaushalts voranzutreiben. Insbesondere bei Neubauten sollte die Regenwassernutzung zu Beginn der Planungen einbezogen und in Kombination mit anderen Maßnahmen wie Rückhalt, Versickerung, Verdunstung und der Nutzung weiterer Wasserressourcen (z. B. aufbereitetes Grauwasser aus der Dusche) mitgedacht werden.
»In deutschen Städten werden Abwasser und Niederschläge derzeit zentral und möglichst schnell aus den Wohn- und Industriegebieten abgeleitet«, sagt Dr. Jan Greiwe, wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter am Fraunhofer ISI. »Die Sammlung und Nutzung dieses Wassers könnte den Trinkwasserbedarf reduzieren. Sie wirkt damit auch, aber nicht gezielt, zur Abfederung von Bedarfsspitzen, beispielsweise während Hitzewellen und Trockenphasen. Im Rahmen eines ganzheitlichen naturnahen Wassersystems könnte die Regenwassernutzung mehr Lebensqualität in die Quartiere bringen und die Versorgungssicherheit steigern.«

title: Röntgenlicht ist wie Gitarrenmusik
content:
Röntgenlicht ist wie Gitarrenmusik
