title: Designing Layered Drone Defenses for Data Centers
content:
Drone activity around critical infrastructure is rising, and data centers are not immune. Until recently, few operators considered drones a serious risk. That’s changing fast.
The threat is no longer theoretical. In spring 2026, drone strikes
disrupted operations at AWS facilities
in the Persian Gulf. While that incident occurred months ago, it continues to underscore an evolving risk landscape for operators.
How should the industry respond? The most effective response favors resilience, lawful defensive measures, and operational readiness over attempts at interdiction.
Why Drone Risks Are Increasing for Data Centers
Consumer-grade drones are inexpensive, widely available, and increasingly capable. Their accessibility means more devices in the sky near more facilities on the ground, elevating both intentional and accidental risks. Even small drones can damage exposed mechanical systems or interfere with critical cooling and power infrastructure. While military-grade platforms pose the highest risk in conflict zones, non-state actors and lone individuals could still cause localized disruption.
Related:
Data Centers Under Fire: Industry Faces Systemic Security Risks
Layered Physical and Detection Controls
A layered defense blends
practical hardening
with multi-sensor detection and clear operational workflows.
1. Physical Drone Defenses
Physical hardening should prioritize airflow-safe protection and impact mitigation:
Install protective cages or netting on roofs or around critical components to create a physical buffer against drones.
Deploy radar or other detection systems that trigger physical protection measures.
Where feasible, relocate vulnerable components, such as cooling towers, from prominent rooftops to ground-level areas behind barriers and fencing.
Apply materials for thermal and infrared signature management to help reduce long-range target identification.
Any such treatments must remain compliant with building codes and equipment performance requirements.
2. Redundancy and Resilience Planning
Even the best defenses can’t guarantee prevention. Treat drones like any other external disruption and design to limit the blast radius.
Intra-site redundancy.
Within a site, build multiple cooling and power subsystems so the facility can continue running if one is damaged.
Inter-site failover.
Across sites, maintain tested failover runbooks to quickly and safely shift workloads or traffic to other data centers.
Recovery procedures.
Include maintaining and regularly rehearsing incident response and disaster recovery plans that specifically account for drone-related disruptions.
Related:
Electromagnetic Interference: The Invisible Threat to Data Center Uptime
3. Location Strategy and Regulatory Environment
Site selection should now explicitly consider drone risks alongside traditional criteria.
Conflict-prone regions.
Areas vulnerable to military activity carry elevated risks of military-grade threats and may warrant additional protective measures.
Local sentiment and governance.
Jurisdictions with strong support for critical infrastructure protections and effective law enforcement coordination can reduce non-military threats.
Regulatory maturity.
Regulatory maturity is increasingly important: consider the availability of
U-space/UTM services
, prevalence of
Remote ID compliance
, and responsiveness of aviation and public safety agencies.
Terrain and concealment.
Hilly, vegetated sites can limit sightlines and complicate the low-altitude approach path, while still preserving necessary detection coverage. Reduce nearby public vantage points and easy launch locations that have clear sightlines to exposed plant, and ensure property boundaries discourage unauthorized drone operations.
Airspace Restrictions and Community Coordination
Only national aviation authorities can establish enforceable airspace restrictions. Rather than seeking informal “no-fly zones,” operators should collaborate with authorities to raise awareness of critical infrastructure and improve response coordination. Publish site advisories, update perimeter signage, and engage with drone service providers and UTM platforms to increase geofencing awareness around sensitive areas. Build local relationships so that law enforcement and emergency management teams understand the facility’s risk profile.
Related:
Bunkers, Mines, and Caverns: The World of Underground Data Centers
Conclusion
Drones introduce low-cost, high-disruption risks that data center operators must plan for as part of business-as-usual resilience. The strongest posture is layered: harden exposed infrastructure, deploy multi-sensor detection, formalize detection-to-response operations, and
design for redundancy
and failover. Combine these measures with location awareness and regulatory coordination.
The industry has clear evidence that drone disruptions are not hypothetical. By focusing on resilience, operators can reduce both the likelihood and impact of drone-related incidents.

title: Enterprises Adopt Colocation for AI and Hybrid Cloud Initiatives
content:
Enterprises are increasingly choosing colocation data centers to host AI inference computing, which performs best using higher cabinet densities than are supported in most legacy corporate data centers. Modern colocation facilities support 35 kW cabinets with air cooling and 70-150 kW cabinets using optional liquid-cooling solutions. Because liquid cooling can be added once higher-density cabinets are needed, enterprise users with uncertain densification timelines can avoid stranding capital expenditures on infrastructure, making this “pay-as-you-go” model attractive.
AI inference computing
is highly iterative, requiring rapid, continuous interaction with large volumes of corporate financial, operational, and research data. Enterprises optimize AI inference computing performance by placing it near their other data centers to enjoy ultra-low round-trip telecom latencies. Enterprises can also install AI applications in edge colocation data centers near specialized data sources and use cases, such as factories, financial market feeds, and research labs. Colocation is available near almost every major city, but most public cloud regions operate from only a few major data center markets in each country.
Related:
The Role of Brokers in Accelerating Data Center Construction
Colocation also offers cybersecurity advantages for AI applications. Because AI inference computing accesses valuable, confidential corporate data, many enterprises in highly regulated industries like financial services and healthcare prefer to perform inference internally in private colocation suites with dedicated network circuits and self-operated firewalls rather than sending that data off-site to third-party AI startups.
Hybrid Cloud Adoption and Rebalancing
Public cloud adoption remains strong: 74% of enterprises accelerated cloud migrations last year, according to Foundry’s 2026 Cloud Computing Study, seeking the flexibility, agility, and low capital investment offered by the cloud.
However, prompted by rapidly escalating cloud costs and several highly publicized cloud outages, many enterprises are rethinking “cloud only” strategies by shifting to a hybrid cloud plus colocation or on-premises model. VMware’s Private Cloud Outlook 2026 indicates that 83% of enterprises have completed or are planning to repatriate workloads back from the public cloud, driven by security, cost, compliance, and performance concerns.
In the push toward hybrid cloud, many enterprises now tailor workload placement to whichever delivery path works best for each specific application and data set. Enterprises often choose public cloud for dynamic capacity and cloud-native applications, but colocation and on-premises for predictable workloads and those that underperform technically or are cost-prohibitive in public cloud. Colocation also effectively hosts private clouds seeking the advantages of public cloud in a more controlled computing and security environment.
Related:
Federal Colocation Readiness: What Data Center Operators Must Prove
Capacity Expansion Without Long Build Cycles
Enterprises seek scalable data center capacity for both AI and traditional corporate computing (research, accounting, finance, sales, and legal), which is vital to all businesses.
AFCOM’s 2026 State of the Data Center Report
indicates that 75% of enterprises expect AI workloads to increase overall capacity requirements.
Colocation offers incremental capacity expansion, allowing enterprises to increase or decrease capacity as needs change. Enterprises often prefer colocation to expanding on-premises capacity because on-premises data center construction can be expensive, time-consuming, and, in some cases, impossible due to the age of legacy facilities or physical limitations.
Cost Predictability and Governance
Colocation typically offers lower occupancy costs than public cloud for stable, predictable workloads. Most new colocation campuses are massive – often 50+ MW – delivering economies of scale in both upfront construction costs and operating expenses unavailable at smaller on-premises data centers. An enterprise seeking 2 MW of new capacity can occupy it at much lower cost in colocation than in a new on-premises data center.
Related:
Wholesale vs. Retail Colocation: How to Choose a Data Center Lease
Colocation also avoids unpredictable, unbudgeted cost overages in public cloud deployments, often driven by unforeseen variable usage, opaque fees, and
weak monitoring tools or practices
. Enterprise users in Flexera’s 2026 State of the Cloud Report estimate that 29% of their cloud spending is wasted.
Application Performance and Networking Enhancement
Colocation supports legacy applications not written to be cloud-native, which often perform poorly in public cloud environments, while other corporate applications require lower telecom latency than is available from public cloud placements when corporate data centers aren’t located near cloud campuses.
Some enterprises enhance connectivity for their computing portfolio using dedicated networking cabinets in interconnection-focused colocation facilities near their primary data centers. In this topology, enterprises secure competitively priced metro-area circuits from 20+ telecom carriers and cloud direct-connect circuits available in urban carrier hotels.
International Operations and Data Sovereignty
Many US-based multinational corporations operate their domestic data centers in-house but turn to international colocation suites for worldwide operations where data sovereignty, low-latency access to foreign operations and customers, or audit and compliance requirements necessitate local computing. International colocation providers also usually offer à la carte managed services that are valuable to enterprises without local IT staff.
Test and Development Labs
Colocation supports internal test/dev labs by offering technologies unavailable at legacy on-premises data centers. Many colocation facilities offer liquid coolants for direct liquid-to-chip testing, large telecom network connections for data-intensive application development, and AI-driven data center management tools and digital twin software. Some cutting-edge colocation facilities offer 800-volt DC electrical distribution and
immersion cooling
. These technology-forward features are available for “try it before you buy it” enterprise projects.
Audit and Compliance Controls
Colocation provides a secure, non-shared hardware placement, enabling audit and compliance procedures favored by corporate users. Many colocation data centers also offer extensive facility and provider certifications, enhancing regulatory approvals.
Meeting Multiple Objectives with Colocation
Enterprises can pursue various goals simultaneously using colocation – delivery paths are not “either/or” between cloud and colocation. For example, a large bank might use an affordable private colocation suite to supplement other computing capacity and reduce public cloud costs; multiple international colocation facilities to support worldwide operations; several interconnection nodes to improve telecom networking; and a density-focused colocation cabinet pod for AI inference rollouts.

title: Australian state mandates storage for new data centers - Energy Storage
content: The Australian state of Victoria, home to the city of Melbourne, has announced rigorous new limitations on data centers being built, with full restrictions on providing their own renewable power and energy storage, along with siting restrictions away from residential areas. Victorian Premier Ben Carroll said that data centers will need to bring their own renewable energy supply and storage. An associated 20-page report titled “The Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan” [sic] said that Melbourne has become Australia’s second‑largest market for data centers, with AUD $5.8 billion spent in capital expenditure in 2025. More than 50 operate across the state. The new rules don’t apply retroactively to built data centers or to applications already under assessment. It also doesn’t state a firm deadline but details a staged plan throughout 2027 to implement separate elements while also gathering feedback from stakeholders. The state is already targeting renewable energy targets of 65% by 2030 and 95% by 2035, which includes energy storage targets of 2.6 GW by 2030 and 6.3 GW by 2035. Rules not quantified, but off-grid not allowed The action plan covers both what government bodies must do to implement the new ideas for data centers, but doesn’t make detailed specifications. For now, the most detailed elements are found in a table below, where developers will need to “bring your own supply” and “maintain system security”. This involves, quote: “Offset actual operational electricity use by investing in new renewable energy generation and storage. Detailed compliance, verification and firming requirements to be finalized in step with Commonwealth standards,” indicating some ongoing work required to fully regulate this requirement in line with Australian standards. One note is that data centers will not be allowed to operate off-grid, with a requirement that data centers participate in demand flexibility services “to the maximum extent commercially and technically possible,” without further detail. Another requirement says a “high levels of power usage effectiveness” must be achieved, for example, to reduce grid draw when renewables are in short supply. title: GridStor wins financing for 400 MWh BESS in Arizona, tolling secured with state utility - Energy Storage
content: Developer and operator GridStor, backed by Goldman Sachs, has announced it has secured financing for its White Tank BESS in Arizona, with $220 million agreed across a range of financial instruments. The 100 MW / 400 MWh White Tank facility will be operated under a 20-year tolling agreement with the local utility, Arizona Public Service (APS), and is located in Maricopa County, where most of Phoenix is located. EcoStor said it is expected to be placed in service “in the first half of 2027.” Arizona’s state utilities continue to break all-time records for power demand, with APS notching a peak electricity demand on August 2 that was 5% higher than the previous record set in 2025, driven by population growth, manufacturing, especially in chip fabs, and data center expansion. The White Tank battery storage project will reinforce APS’ system reliability. In terms of financing, the company said its three banking partners on the deal, ING Capital, KeyBank N.A., and Zions Capital Markets, structured a $220 million tax equity bridge, construction, and term debt financing agreement. The financial close of the project marks GridStor’s fourth financing move within the past twelve months as it builds out or acquires more than 3 GW of BESS. What they said: “We are proud to work with three distinguished financial partners to complete the financing of the White Tank Reliability Project,” said Chris Taylor, CEO, GridStor. “Trusted partnerships like these are critical for advancing large-scale power supply and infrastructure to meet surging demand for new power capacity. We thank ING, KeyBanc Capital Markets, and Zions for placing their trust in us.” “We are pleased to complete the financing of the White Tank battery energy storage project with GridStor,” said Filipe Barreto, Director, ING. “This transaction reflects ING’s confidence in the sector and our commitment to financing energy infrastructure that enhances grid reliability and supports the transition to a lower-carbon energy future. We look forward to building on this success with GridStor.” “Battery storage has become an essential part of how utilities address growing load, reliability requirements and changing grid conditions,” said Greg Berman, Managing Director, Utilities, Power & Renewable Energy, KeyBanc Capital Markets. “We’re proud to have arranged this financing for GridStor’s White Tank project and support the development of infrastructure that can be deployed quickly and at scale to help address the nation’s evolving energy needs.” “We are pleased to provide this strategic financing to support the continued growth of Arizona’s energy capacity,” said Robert Park, Head of Power and Project Finance, Zions. “This transaction underscores our Power and Project Finance team’s expertise in structuring tailored financial solutions in the power sector, and we are proud to have supported GridStor in this project transaction.” The post GridStor wins financing for 400 MWh BESS in Arizona, tolling secured with state utility appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Italy authorizes 2.3 GW in September so far, including 110 MW BESS despite local opposition - Energy Storage
content: Italy’s Ministry of Environment and Energy Security (MASE) has published two single authorization decrees for a pair of 55 MW battery energy storage systems (BESS), totaling 110 MW, both located in the municipality of Ittiri in Sardinia. The authorizations were issued to the London-based fund Bluefield Partners despite pushback via negative opinions from the municipality itself and regional landscape protection offices. Under decree 264/2026, subsidiary BSD042024 Srl obtained the single authorization to build the plant dubbed “Ittiri A.” Through decree 263/2026, BSD052024 Srl secured the authorization for “Ittiri B.” The two storage systems are identical, right down to their components. Each project will feature 48 containerized plant units comprising batteries and inverters, each with a capacity of 1,255 kW and four hours of storage duration. The submitted timeline estimates that construction will take approximately 26 months for Ittiri B and 27 months for Ittiri A. Despite the negative opinions from local and regional offices, the ministry deemed the objections to be overcome. In Ittiri, the debate surrounding the energy transition—and energy storage systems in particular—remains an ongoing issue. Last July, the regional government denied approval for a 470.4 MW / 1,408 MWh BESS proposed by Thiesi Solar, an Enerside subsidiary. The region deemed the project incompatible with the area’s agricultural vocation and territorial governance model, asking the ministry to declare the application inadmissible. With these two new authorizations, the total capacity approved by MASE since the beginning of September rises to 2,374 MW. Yesterday, the ministry issued eight AUs for 907.4 MW, on September 11th another six for 753.4 MW, and on September 7th , five more for 603 MW. title: TrueRE Oriana Power wins 900 MW/1.8 GWh BESS contracts in India - Energy Storage
content: TrueRE Oriana Power has secured two contracts from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd.(MSEDCL) to set up a combined 900 MW/1,800 MWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity across the Indian state of Maharashtra. The projects carry an aggregate consideration of around INR 3,870 crore over a 15-year term, excluding GST. The awarded capacity includes a standalone 500 MW/1,000 MWh BESS project at MSETCL substations, at a tariff of INR 2,38,000/MW/month, and a 400 MW/800 MWh BESS at MSEDCL substations, at a tariff of INR 2,40,000/MW/month, under the Mukhyamantri Saur Krushi Vahini Yojana 2.0 (MSKVY 2.0) – Maharashtra’s flagship scheme for decentralized solarization of agricultural feeders. TrueRE Oriana Power secured the capacity through a tariff-based global competitive bidding process followed by e-reverse auction. The projects are eligible for Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF) scheme. The company expects VGF of approximately INR 3.24 billion, based on the current estimated project cost. The projects will operate under battery energy storage purchase agreements (BESPAs) for 15 years from their respective commercial operation dates. The scheduled commissioning dates will be determined in accordance with the respective BESPAs, which are yet to be executed. title: BYD offers a closer look at the new Seagull EV [Images]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:12 am PT
revealed the second-generation Seagull design in a series of sketches: a bigger, smarter version of its most affordable EV.
When is BYD launching the new Seagull EV?
The Seagull, sold as the Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini in markets outside China, is BYD’s entry-level electric hatch.
In China, the Seagull starts at just 69,900 yuan, or about $10,000. That’s much cheaper than any new vehicle in the US. To give you a better idea, the
most affordable new car in the US
is the 2026 Hyundai Venue, which starts at just over $20,500.
Even in overseas markets, BYD’s electric hatch is among the most affordable EVs. In Europe, the Dolphin Surf starts at about €22,900 ($26,500).
It’s no wonder the low-cost electric hatch is among the world’s top-selling electric vehicles. According to Cleantechnica, the Seagull (including the Dolphin Surf and Mini) was the sixth best-selling EV globally through the first half of 2026, with over 27,500 units sold.
BYD is now preparing to launch the second-generation model. Zhang Zhuo, the general manager of BYD’s Ocean series sales division, offered a closer look at the new Seagull on Monday night.
Zhou revealed several design sketches of the updated version with the caption: “Preserving the classic design while embracing new expression, the lines have been reshaped and the surface refreshed #BYD Second Generation Seagull# More surprises are coming soon!”
When translated into English, the first image reads: “Brand new layout” and “Space size expands together.”
Another reads: “Clean appearance” and “The driving posture is even more extreme.” The other sketches reveal new “Trident-shaped” front and rear lights and the second-generation Seagull’s “Dynamic new look.”
No other details were mentioned, but Zhuo revealed at the Chengdu Auto Show last month that the new model will be named the “Great Seagull” and will go on sale by the end of 2026.
The new Seagull also appeared in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) regulatory filing last month, revealing a few key specs.
The filing revealed that the Great Seagull measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. That’s considerably bigger than the current Seagull, which is just 3,780 mm long.
It will also gain a more powerful 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor. In comparison, the current Seagull uses a 55 kW (75 hp) motor.
We will learn more soon, with its official debut just around the corner, but you can expect the updated version to feature BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology.
Earlier this week,
several spy images
of the new Seagull undisguised surfaced online, revealing a roof-mounted LiDAR. As such, the new version will likely get an upgraded ADAS system with BYD’s God’s Eye B.
We also caught a sneak peek of the interior last month with several updates, including a larger infotainment screen, redesigned center console, and a two-spoke steering wheel.
BYD Dolphin Surf EV (Source: BYD)
Will BYD release the second-gen model in overseas markets, like Europe and the UK? It hasn’t been confirmed, but the larger updated electric hatch is expected to launch overseas, likely as the second-gen Dolphin Surf.
The current Dolphin Surf starts at around €22,900 ($26,500) in Europe, so the larger variant will likely cost a bit more. It will likely still start at under €30,000 ($35,000), as a smaller, more affordable option than the Dolphin.

title: Honda just unveiled an electric mountain bike, and it looks serious
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 22 2026 - 6:02 am PT
Honda is best known for motorcycles, cars, generators, lawnmowers, robots, jets… basically anything with a motor attached to it. But now the Japanese giant appears ready to add another two-wheeler to that list: an electric mountain bike.
Honda recently showed off its new e-MTB project at Sea Otter Europe in Girona, Spain, marking a surprisingly serious return to the mountain bike world after an absence of roughly two decades.
And this doesn’t appear to be merely a styling exercise. Honda’s German website is
already inviting
riders to register their interest in the upcoming e-MTB, declaring, “New terrain, same dream,” and describing the bike as “almost here.”
The prototype itself combines Honda’s
motorcycle-inspired design
with some decidedly familiar bicycle hardware. The carbon monocoque frame was developed with German premium e-bike manufacturer Rotwild through its ADP Engineering division, and features a massive rear swingarm that Honda calls the “Gullarm.”
The suspension uses a single-pivot arrangement with several linkages driving the rear shock, while a Fox 36 fork, mullet 29-inch front and 27.5-inch rear wheel setup, and aggressive geometry make it pretty clear Honda isn’t designing this thing for leisurely rides to the farmers market.
The display bike also uses a Shimano EP8-series mid-drive motor, though there may be another surprise lurking there. Footage
released
alongside the bike appears to show a slightly different motor casing than Shimano’s current EP801.
That’s hardly enough evidence to declare that a new Shimano motor is coming, but it certainly gives us something interesting to squint at until Honda provides more details.
Honda’s involvement in mountain biking actually goes back more than 20 years. Its motorcycle R&D division famously developed the RN01 downhill bike in the early 2000s, complete with an unusual enclosed, frame-mounted transmission. Honda raced the radical machine internationally before eventually pulling out of the sport.
That makes this return particularly interesting. Honda isn’t simply slapping its logo on a generic e-bike as many other automotive and motorcycle companies have done. The company even displayed the new machine alongside the old RN01 and its latest electric motorcycles and off-road prototypes.
Honda hasn’t announced the battery capacity, final motor, weight, price, production name, or launch markets yet.
But considering Honda is already collecting registrations for what it calls its “new E-Mountainbike,” this looks less like Honda wondering whether it should build an e-bike and more like the company preparing to actually sell one.

title: Massive UK study finds high-mileage electric cars more durable than petrol
content:
Electric Vehicles
reliability
Jameson Dow
| Sep 22 2026 - 5:00 am PT
A study of millions of UK vehicles shows that electric cars stay on the road longer than petrol cars, and the gap widens as mileage increases.
With electric cars being a
relatively
new technology, many people have been skeptical of what their long-term reliability would look like. Despite EVs having fewer moving parts which suggests less opportunity for failure, fear of the new still keeps people worrying.
But electric cars aren’t really
new anymore. The oldest EVs of the modern era have now been on the road for nearly two decades, so we’ve got some data now. And it turns out EVs look pretty good, according to a
new study
The study was conducted using
data from millions of annual British MOT tests
, the standard test of roadworthiness for cars on British roads. These tests focus on a car’s suspension, brakes, tires, exhaust, and emissions.
It checked how likely cars were to come back for another MOT test – if they didn’t, then that meant the car was no longer on the road (whether it be for an issue with those five categories above, or another issue).
In the beginning of their operational life, there’s little difference between roadworthiness of petrol and electric vehicles. EVs actually experience slightly
problems in the early years of ownership, but that’s because EVs tend to put on more miles early than petrol cars do.
When comparing on a mileage basis, EVs have very similar failure rates in the early years, differing by less than a percentage point. But that changes once you get to higher mileage numbers – past 40,000 miles lifetime.
At that point, petrol cars are less reliable, and the reliability only gets worse over time. By the time a petrol car reaches 120,000 miles, it’s
more likely to have failed than an EV (16% failure rate vs. 23.5% failure rate).
The same goes for age, as cars get older the EVs remain more reliable. That’s despite higher annual mileage from EVs no matter where they are in their age bracket.
The study also compared vehicles that have an electric and a petrol version side by side. In every case
the VW Golf, it was either a tie or a reliability win by BEVs.
This is despite the compromised BEV design of these multi-powertrain vehicles. Most of them were designed with limited chassis modifications, simply adding a large battery, making the BEV versions heavier than their chassis was designed for.
This weight discrepancy led to higher tire wear for BEVs. Across the board, BEVs did have significantly higher tire wear than petrol vehicles. But multi-powertrain vehicles like the VW Golf had much higher tire wear rates than purpose-built BEVs like the BMW i3.
While weight did have an effect on tire wear, it didn’t have an effect on suspension. The study found that BEVs suffered fewer suspension problems than petrol vehicles, no matter the mileage.
And brakes were obviously responsible for far fewer problems on BEVs, given that most braking happens via regenerative braking on electric cars. However, very old EVs (over 10 years old) ended up having more brake problems than petrol cars, likely due to persistent underuse of brakes and corrosion.
So, for EV drivers out there, be sure to hit those friction brakes every once in a while, EV drivers, even if you use regen most of the time. And keep an eye on your tires.
Not only is all of this true of light duty vehicles, but of light commercial vans like the Nissan NV200. The BEV version outperformed the diesel version, except on tire wear.
One limitation of the study is that it doesn’t track battery health, since that isn’t captured in British MOT tests. But we did recently see
the largest-ever study of battery health
that showed EV batteries last longer than many people would expect, generally retaining 90% of capacity even after 90,000 miles of operation.

title: Mercedes-Benz signs deal to put Wayve AI Driver in cars within 2 years
content:
Mercedes-Benz
autonomous driving
Fred Lambert
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:49 am PT
Mercedes-Benz has signed a definitive production agreement with British self-driving startup Wayve to build its “AI Driver” into future Mercedes vehicles, with integration starting within the next two years.
It’s the first time Wayve’s end-to-end driving AI is going into a production car in the premium segment, and it deepens a relationship that already includes Mercedes investing in Wayve’s $1.5 billion Series D round earlier this year.
What Mercedes is actually buying
Wayve doesn’t build cars. It builds the software that drives them, using what it calls an “AV2.0” approach: an embodied-AI system that learns to drive from data instead of following hand-coded rules and HD maps.
The company says its AI Driver runs without HD maps, geofences, or city-specific retraining, and can generalize to cities it hasn’t seen before. That’s the same “learned,” end-to-end philosophy Tesla uses for Full Self-Driving, and the opposite of the heavily mapped, geofenced approach Waymo built its robotaxis on.
However, unlike Tesla, which removed the radar from its sensor suite, Wayve added radar in its latest system.
Photo: Wayve
For this deal, Wayve integrated its AI Driver into Mercedes’ own production system architecture: the automaker’s hardware, its MB.OS operating system, and its map interfaces. The system was trained on Nvidia infrastructure running on Microsoft Azure. Mercedes describes what customers will get as “advanced urban and highway point-to-point driving assistance.”
And notice what the announcement leaves out. There’s no SAE automation level, no named models, and no firmer date than “within the next two years.”
“This partnership marks the world’s first integration of the Wayve AI Driver in the premium segment,” said Jörg Burzer, Mercedes-Benz’s chief technology officer.
Mercedes is now running three autonomy stacks
Mercedes isn’t betting on one self-driving system. It’s running several at once.
It already sells Drive Pilot, its own hands-off, eyes-off Level 3 system for highway traffic jams. That was the first Level 3 system certified for US roads. In January, we covered
Nvidia’s open-source Alpamayo model shipping in the Mercedes CLA
as a Level 2+ assistance system. Now Wayve’s AI Driver is coming too.
So Mercedes is hedging: a rules-based L3 system for a narrow highway case, Nvidia’s stack for L2+ point-to-point, and Wayve’s embodied AI as a scalable path toward higher automation. It’s the strategy of a company that wants autonomy, but it isn’t sure which path will suceed yet.
That’s the bigger story for the industry. While Tesla insists on writing every line of its self-driving software in-house, legacy automakers are increasingly buying the “AI driver” from specialists like Wayve, Nvidia, and Mobileye. Wayve now counts Mercedes, Nissan, and Stellantis among the investors in its
$1.5 billion Series D
, which valued the company at $8.6 billion in February.
“The pace and depth of our development work together reflect a deep technical alignment between our teams,” said Wayve co-founder and CEO Alex Kendall.
Electrek’s Take
I think it’s clear that other automakers will work with these ADAS/ADS system integrators rather than Tesla.
Not only do they avoid working with a competitor, but Tesla has also shown real difficulty maintaining FSD across several vehicle programs and different hardware versions (HW3). It would be hard for an automaker to trust Tesla with deploying and maintaining a system in other automakers’ vehicles.
Wayve’s entire business is built around that. It’s a way safer bet, especially with Mercedes’ ownership stake.

title: Tesla Full Self-Driving bug falsely flags dirty cameras, demands service
content:
Full Self-Driving (FSD)
Fred Lambert
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:26 am PT
Tesla’s newest Full Self-Driving update, v14.3.9, is telling owners their cameras are dirty when they aren’t — and sending them to service to fix a problem that doesn’t exist.
Tesla has confirmed the bug and is canceling the service appointments it triggered. A fix is expected in a coming update.
The alert owners are seeing
Drivers who installed v14.3.9 started getting a message on the center screen: “Poor camera visibility detected. Interior windshield residue cleaning is required.”
The cameras are clean. The alert fires anyway, often in bright sun or glare, with the software reading normal optical conditions as an obstructed forward camera.
Tesla owner
posted a screenshot of Tesla Support confirming the software fault and said Tesla is proactively canceling service visits that owners booked because of it. Owners on Reddit reported the same message on clean cars.
What triggered it, and what to do
v14.3.9 (software builds 2026.27.5 and 2026.27.6) rolled out around September 12. It’s the same update that brought
Automatic Collision Evasion to HW4 cars
, letting FSD take over manual driving to avoid a crash.
If you got the camera alert, don’t book a service appointment. Owners who already paid for a cleaning or inspection can contact Tesla Support for a refund.
A follow-up build, v14.3.10, is expected to address the alerts. So far, its release notes are identical to v14.3.9’s, so there’s no confirmation of what changed.
Electrek’s Take
Vision-only for the win. It’s a two-step forward, one-step back process.
The newest build is so twitchy about camera visibility that it’s flagging perfectly clean lenses and shipping owners off to service. It looks a lot like Tesla turned up the sensitivity on visibility detection and overshot.
A false “clean your camera” popup is an annoyance, not a danger. But it points at the real problem with a camera-only system: getting it to catch genuine degradation from sun, fog, and dust without crying wolf on a clean windshield is hard, and Tesla still hasn’t nailed it.
Tesla is likely to run into a thousand more of these issues before it can actually achive unsupervised self-driving at scale, which require redundancy – something you can’t achieve if your only way to see, cameras, fail.

title: Tesla's active robotaxi fleet in Austin crashes back to 8 vehicles after Cybercab pump
content:
Tesla’s active robotaxi fleet in Austin has fallen back to just 8 vehicles over the past seven days, according to data from community tracker Robotaxi Tracker.
That’s about the same number Tesla had on the road when it launched the service in June 2025. Fifteen months of promises, and no net growth. A surge following the “launch of the Cybercab” quickly dissipated.
Tesla’s “launch” spiked the numbers for about a week
Tesla held a Cybercab launch event in Austin on September 3 and invited a wave of supporters and Tesla influencers to ride the steering-wheel-free vehicle. For a few days, X was full of first-ride videos.
The tracker data shows exactly what that looked like. The number of unique Tesla robotaxis actually seen carrying riders in Austin spiked past 100 in early September, up from the 20-to-40 range it had been stuck in for most of the year.
Then it collapsed. By September 22, the seven-day active count is back to 8.
And the ride videos dried up with it. One of those early Cybercab rides turned a 10-minute trip into a 70-minute detour, and the flood of posts Tesla engineered for launch week has slowed to a trickle after Tesla “influencers” left the city.
Registered vehicles aren’t the same as active ones
Here’s the gap Tesla’s boosters keep glossing over.
Tesla registers its autonomous vehicles with the Texas DMV under the state’s new AV rules, and that registered fleet now sits at 476 VINs (409 Model Ys and 67 Cybercabs), up 285 in the last 30 days alone. TSLA pumpers point to that growing number, and to the rising Cybercab count in particular, as proof the fleet is scaling.
But a registration is a VIN in a database, not a car giving rides. Of those 476 registered vehicles, trackers have matched only 265 to license plates actually spotted on the road, and just 179 were seen at all in the last 30 days. Over the last 7 days, only 8 were caught carrying passengers.
Tesla keeps “adding” vehicles to its Texas robotaxi fleet on paper. That count has never reflected how many cars are actually operating at the same time.
Electrek’s Take
This is what a marketing launch looks like when there’s no product ramp behind it. And by product ramp, I mean useful Cybercabs. I do beleieve that Tesla can ramp up production and we have seen plenty of Cybercabs sitting in parking lots, but it currently has no way to translate that into autonomous ride-hailing at scale due to the same safety concerns we have been talking about for more than a year.
Top comment by Volvo Guy
What's interesting is that there is a spike about 2 weeks before the "launch" and then another spike at "launch". I'd bet good money that:
--The first spike was a test to make sure they were ready for the "launch" spike
--Both of these events are spikes rather than new plateaus because during both events, Tesla was remote monitoring every car and that is not sustainable. If they had truly autonomous operations, there would be no reason to scale back after ramping up. The cars would just keep running and the line would go up and to the right. The spike pattern demonstrates that these were tests, not actual scaling of ongoing operations
Tesla needed a moment, and it got one on September 3. It invited the usual crowd of supporters, and generated a week of glowing ride videos. The active-fleet chart shows the whole thing: a clean spike past 100 vehicles, then a cliff straight back down to 8. Once the influencers went home, so did the cars.
And 8 is rough. That’s essentially where the service started in June 2025. Fifteen months later, after a “launch,” a Cybercab reveal, and hundreds of new registrations, the number of Tesla robotaxis actually carrying people in Austin in a given week hasn’t moved.
That’s entirely because if Tesla deploys the system at scale, it would face too many accidents. Therefore, it is preferable to only run a few vehicles at a time, in geo-fenced areas, and at lower speeds.
There would be nothing wrong about that if Tesla wasn’t trying to convince the public, and mostly the stock market, that it is “leading the autonomous market with no close second behind” when in fact, it is mostly an act.

title: Waymo riders can now get $2.85 back when pairing a ride with public transit
content:
Robotaxi
Public Transit
Jameson Dow
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:00 am PT
Photo: Waymo
Waymo is now offering a $2.85 credit to any rider who pairs their ride with public transit, expanding a pilot program it previously ran in two cities – but it’s only available for Visa users, for now.
One of the great things about living in a city is that you can get around without a car. Higher housing density makes public transit possible, which then serves as a cheap way to move lots of people quickly.
But, every once in a while, you’ll still need some other solution to get where you’re going – especially in American cities where public transit
isn’t nearly as expansive as it ought to be
. Maybe you take a train into town because it’s cheaper and you can skip traffic, but the only stop is a couple miles from your destination.
For these situations, there are taxis. Instead of owning a car and finding a place to park it, you can just borrow a ride for a fee.
Of course in the modern age, we have robotaxis, driven by computers rather than humans, and Waymo is the leading provider of this service in the US.
So to assist with this symbiotic relationship between transit and taxis, Waymo is now offering a deal: anyone who takes a transit ride and a Waymo ride back to back gets a $2.85 reward back from Waymo.
The program is only available on Visa cards for the time being. Waymo would like to expand it to other payment processors, but has not yet done so. To use it, you link your Visa card to your Waymo app, and when you use the same card for both a Waymo and public transit ride within 2 hours of each other, you get $2.85 in “Waymo Cash,” which can be used for future Waymo rides.
Waymo initially ran a similar trial program in Los Angeles and San Francisco, and designed the program to mirror a
$2.85 discount
given to riders who use both BART and SF Muni, two regional transit systems, in the SF Bay Area.
The company says that in its most mature markets (SF/LA/Phoenix), over half of its riders also use public transit, so it expects to see high use of the
new program
. But the new program will be available initially to all riders in San Francisco, with the idea of expanding out from there.

title: 东方日升首批pHJT CIC电池下线

集邦光储观察获悉，8月29日，东方日升首批pHJT CIC（Coverglass-Interconnected Space Solar Cell）电池下线，产品为RisenFlex Nova系列。
RisenFlex Nova采用p型异质结（pHJT）技术，电池厚度为70μm，尺寸可根据需求进行调整，目前覆盖30×40mm至210×105mm。产品主要用于特殊环境场景，目前已向客户开放定制验证。
今年6月SNEC展会期间，东方日升对外发布Risen Flex Nova新星产品。公开资料显示，该产品采用70μm厚p型异质结电池，尺寸为210mm×105mm，BOL效率21%，在AM0空间标准光谱下最高效率可达22.2%。
公司半年报显示，70μm超薄HJT电池已实现小批量交付，厚度低于70μm的产品也在开发中。按照公司规划，超薄HJT电池预计于2027年形成GW级量产能力。后续团队将持续优化良率、效率与可靠性，推进产品迭代升级。

title: 又一企588Ah、601Ah大容量储能电芯量产下线
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月21日，派能科技在合肥基地举行588Ah、601Ah大容量储能电芯量产下线仪式，其大容量储能电芯正式进入规模化量产阶段。
据了解，588Ah、601Ah大容量储能电芯为派能科技自主研发产品，主打高安全、长寿命、高能效特性。依托合肥基地智能制造体系，该系列电芯已完成超100MWh批量产出。
在产线智能化方面，该大电芯产线核心工序自动化率达100%，部署120余台工业机器人、180余套智能设备。通过MES系统采集全链路生产数据，实现单颗电芯100%全流程追溯，支撑电芯全生命周期质量管控。
目前，该大容量电芯已应用于派能科技新一代PyOcean系列6.25MWh、8MWh大型储能系统，对应的储能系统已拿到订单并正式发货。
在市场落地层面，公开资料显示，派能科技近年持续落地海内外大型储能项目，包括江苏扬州仪征120MW/240MWh储能电站、宁夏200MW/400MWh储能电站，以及欧洲百兆瓦时级的储能项目，持续积累大型储能项目交付经验。

title: 宁德时代拟募资45亿元，用于4大电池基地
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月20日，宁德时代发布2026年度第七期绿色科技创新债券申购说明，债券发行总规模为45亿元。
根据发行文件，本期债务融资工具的发行规模为人民币45亿元，其中，品种一期限为3+2年期，初始发行规模人民币40亿元；品种二期限为5年期，初始发行规模人民币5亿元。
本次募集资金扣除发行费用后，将用于宁德时代下属锂离子电池生产项目日常运营，资金投向包含锂电原材料采购、生产设备维护更新，以及兑付原材料采购对应的银行承兑汇票、商业承兑汇票。
据悉，本期债券募集资金拟投福鼎时代锂电池生产基地项目、江苏时代动力及储能锂离子电池研发与生产项目、四川时代动力电池项目和山东时代新能源电池产业基地项目，上述基地合计规划产能约460GWh。
需要明确的是，本次募资为补充现有投产基地营运资金，并非用于新建产能，460GWh为四座基地已披露规划总产能，不属于本次债券新增扩产规模。

title: 思格南通智慧能源中心二期建设再提速
content:
9月21日，思格新能源南通智慧能源中心二期项目顺利完成主体结构封顶。从6月29日正式开工到主体封顶，仅用时84天，再次展现“思格速度”与“苏锡通服务”的高效协同，也标志着思格在完善全球产能布局、提升制造与交付能力方面迈出重要一步。
作为思格新能源全球核心生产基地之一，南通智慧能源中心在公司全球化战略布局中具有重要地位。一期项目以百天封顶、8个月建成投产的建设速度，建成全球最大的单体分布式储能工厂之一，并于今年3月正式启用。
本次封顶的二期项目总投资10亿元，将重点布局大型地面电站储能设备。二期投产后，将与一期已建成的户用及工商业储能产能形成强力协同，推动思格全面覆盖“户用—工商业—大型地面电站”的全场景产品矩阵，有效承接创新产品量产，为全球订单的快速响应与规模化交付提供坚实保障。
在扩大产能的同时，二期项目将进一步推进制造体系的智能化与数字化升级，打造贯通“计划—生产—设备”的数字化管理闭环。此外，基地将全面落实“全生命周期质量追踪体系”，实现从“供应来料—生产制造—物流配送—产品安装—实际使用”全链路数据的贯通与可视、可溯、可控，以高标准品质服务全球客户。
在建设过程中，项目持续得到南通市政府与苏锡通科技产业园区的全方位保障。从前期沟通、审批办理到配套完善、施工协调，相关部门通过专班服务与高效协同，及时回应建设需求、解决推进难题，为一期建设与二期扩产的有序衔接创造了良好条件。“苏锡通服务”与“思格速度”同向发力，推动项目建设不断取得新进展。
此次主体封顶后，二期项目将进入后续建设与投产筹备阶段，计划于2027年一季度举行二期开园仪式。随着南通智慧能源中心产能与制造体系的持续完善，思格将进一步强化技术创新、规模化生产与全球交付的协同能力，以先进制造支撑创新落地，为全球能源转型提供更高品质的光储产品与解决方案。

title: 远景能源、星源材质等8企锂电储能项目进展更新
content:
近期，锂电及储能产业链项目持续推进，涉及钠电正极材料、铝箔、锂电隔膜及储能系统等环节，部分项目已投产或产品下线，部分项目进入开工、签约及建设推进阶段。
珈钠能源钠电材料项目投产
9月21日，珈钠能源2万吨钠电聚阴离子材料扩建项目在四川自贡正式投产。
该项目主要依托铁基聚阴离子技术生产钠离子电池正极材料，产品涵盖大规模储能、轻型动力等应用场景。此前，企业已于2024年在自贡基地建成投产一期万吨级产线。此次二期2万吨扩建项目的投产，使该企业聚阴离子钠电正极材料产能规模实现翻倍。
拓芯安储能系统项目落户
9月21日，拓芯安新能源（广东）有限公司储能系统供应链和智能制造项目签约仪式在广东乐昌举行。
该项目拟选址乐昌经开区城东片区，总投资约5亿元。项目将成立专业化供应链管理及新能源智能制造公司，聚焦电池包（PACK）辅件赛道，整合结构件、连接器件、热管理材料等供应链资源，打造移动储能一站式供应链服务平台。
远景江门智慧储能基地产品下线
9月20日上午，远景江门智慧储能基地首套产品正式发运，同时基地400MWh储能产品成功下线。
该基地位于江门台山市广海湾，主要生产储能装箱集成产品、柜式产品与交流侧产品等，具备年产50万千瓦时储能设备的生产能力。项目于2024年11月动工建设，并于2026年5月进入试生产阶段。
一锂电池隔膜项目环评获受理
9月17日，丽水市生态环境局遂昌分局发布公告，正式受理浙江圣墨西科技有限公司年产3000万平方米锂电池隔膜项目的环评文件。
该项目位于浙江省丽水市遂昌县龙板山东城智造园，由浙江圣墨西科技有限公司租用园区厂房实施。项目拟购置高速隔膜涂覆线、高精度分切机等主要设备，建成后将形成年产3000万平方米锂电池隔膜的生产能力。
5万吨钠离子电池铝箔项目开工
9月16日上午，神火集团年产5万吨钠离子高性能电池铝箔项目在商丘市示范区正式开工。
该项目建设周期为24个月，规划建设约4万平方米生产车间及智能仓储系统，主要生产1070、1100等合金牌号、厚度为8至20μm的钠离子正负极用电池铝箔。

该项目由星源材质全资子公司投资建设，总投资约64亿令吉（约合人民币100亿元），总建筑面积超20万平方米。项目分为两期建设，其中一期已于2025年6月正式投产运营。
项目全部建成后，将具备年产40亿平方米锂离子电池湿法基膜及配套涂覆隔膜的加工能力。

title: EWE awards Bilfinger hydrogen treatment contract for Huntorf
content:
The project will repurpose one of seven underground salt caverns at EWE’s Huntorf storage site in Germany’s Wesermarsch region for hydrogen storage. Once commissioned, the facility will provide approximately 16 million standard cubic meters (Nm³) of working gas capacity and will be connected to Germany’s hydrogen core network.
Bilfinger will be responsible for the engineering, installation, and commissioning of the hydrogen drying system. The project will mark the first commercial-scale use of Bilfinger’s H2Dry technology.
Peter Schmidt, Managing Director of EWE GASSPEICHER, said: “Hydrogen storage facilities are essential for a secure and reliable energy supply. They create a buffer between production, import and consumption, ensuring that hydrogen is available whenever it is needed – no matter when it is produced or supplied. With our storage project in Huntorf, we are creating vital infrastructure and, through this contract award to Bilfinger, taking another important step forward.”
Ulrich Trebbe, Product Manager Hydrogen at Bilfinger, said: “Hydrogen storage requires efficient and cost-effective treatment solutions. With H2Dry, we provide exactly that while helping our customers bring green hydrogen to market competitively.”
The Huntorf facility forms part of EWE’s Clean Hydrogen Coastline initiative, which integrates renewable hydrogen production, storage, transport, and utilization across north-west Germany. The four-part project received funding approvals from the German federal government and the State of Lower Saxony in summer 2024 under the European Important Project of Common European Interest program.

title: A $25,000 EV Conversion Can Give Classic Cars a New Life—This 1970 Scout Shows How
content:
Canada’s Beachman says EV conversions start at $25,000.
Photo by:
Beachman Bikes
4:34am ET
Canada’s Beachman, known for e-bikes, is now converting classic cars into EVs.
Its latest creation is a 1970 International Harvester Scout 800A, which sat unused in a field for years.
The startup says it can convert a classic motorcycle into an EV for as little as $7,000. Cars start at $25,000.
Converting classic cars into EVs isn’t anything new, but now there’s a new player that promises to keep costs relatively low for an industry that has been inundated with six-figure projects.
Canada’s Beachman,
known for its e-bikes
, has opened its Special Vehicles Division, which handles EV conversions starting at $7,000. The startup’s latest creation is a 1970 International Harvester Scout 800A that got an electric transplant after sitting unloved in a field for years.
The classic American SUV went through a minor restoration process that included cutting out the rust from the driver’s floor, freshening up the original white steel wheels, reupholstering the seats, and rebuilding the dash.
Photo by: Beachman Bikes
The original gas engine was removed from under the hood, but the rest of the Scout’s drivetrain was left untouched. A bog-standard 147-horsepower (110-kilowatt) electric motor sourced from a 2019
Nissan Leaf
was bolted to the original four-speed manual transmission through a custom-made adapter plate. As a result, this EV still has a clutch pedal, a gear stick, low range, and four-wheel drive.
A 40-kilowatt-hour battery pack lifted from the same 2019 Leaf powers it all and provides between 93 and 124 miles (150-200 kilometers) of range on a full charge. That’s not exactly record-setting, but the car’s owner only uses the converted Scout to deliver beer from his brewery on warm summer days in Toronto. As an urban delivery vehicle with plenty of character, the boxy Scout does the job just right.
A full charge takes about eight hours on a Level 2 charger, but that’s perfectly adequate for the car’s purpose.
Gallery: 1970 International Harvester Scout 800A EV conversion by Beachman
Swapping a gas engine with an electric powertrain comes with a few strings attached, so it’s not exactly a plug-and-play deal. Because the electric motor doesn’t idle, it can’t be used to produce vacuum for the old brake booster, so an independent brake pump needed to be fitted. The steering also needed a rethink, and the original dash had to be modded to display information about the EV system.
Beachman says car conversions start at $25,000 for vehicles with a manual transmission. Automatics cost more because the gearbox has to come out, but the basic pack is the same: proven off-the-shelf components from mass-made cars that make ownership easier in the long run.

title: Rivian R3 Will Be Priced 'Materially Lower' Than R2, CEO Says
content:
Rivian R3 Will Be Priced 'Materially Lower' Than R2, CEO Says
The R4 is coming after that, he told The New York Times, at an even lower price than the R3.
- The Rivian R3 will be priced "materially lower" than the R2, CEO RJ Scaringe said in an interview.
- The R2 will eventually start at $45,000, so it sounds like the R3 will cost significantly less than that.
- Scaringe said the R4, which we know next to nothing about, will be even cheaper than the R3.
The Rivian R2 arrived to rave reviews this year, including from us at InsideEVs. But plenty of the startup's fans and EV buyers at large are already eyeing Rivian's next car, the R3. The hatchback, presented as a "one more thing" surprise at the R2 reveal event, kind of stole the show from its big brother. Now we know a (little) bit more about what it'll cost you.
"The next product, which we creatively call R3, is going to take the price point down. We haven’t announced pricing yet, but it will move materially lower," Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe told The New York Times in a recent interview. "There’s a product beyond that, called R4, which again moves that further."
Rivian's product roadmap.
Today the R2 starts at close to $60,000 for debut trim, which is the Performance edition with Launch Package. By late 2027, Rivian says, it'll release a version for $45,000. That R2 Standard will have rear-wheel drive and a Rivian-estimated "275+" miles of range.
If the R3 brings the price for a Rivian "materially lower," that indicates that the hatchback could start somewhere below $40,000. While that segment now has more options than ever, like the newly discounted Hyundai Ioniq 5, the Subaru Uncharted, and the Toyota bZ, there are far more EVs on sale that are more expensive.
Rivian hasn't revealed much in the way of detail about the R3. We know it will be produced at the startup's upcoming Georgia factory, which is supposed to kick off production in 2028. Scaringe has said R3 sales will start with the high-performance, off-road-oriented R3X.
The company has said even less about what comes after that. The R4 Scaringe mentioned will apparently cost even less than the R3, suggesting it could be a true budget EV. But what form factor it will take is still very much unknown. When Scaringe came on the Plugged-In Podcast in 2025, he said the R4 and R5 will be "a sibling set, where you have two very different vehicles that share the same platform."
The vagueness is understandable. For now, the R2 is the company's top focus, and that needs to go off without a hitch for the rest of its roadmap to come into focus. Deliveries started in June, and the automaker expects the new model will let it sell up to 70,000 EVs this year, bringing it more scale than ever before. As Scaringe told me last year on the podcast: "It must go well."

title: Rolls-Royce Wants Its Ultra-Exclusive Project Nightingale EV’s Cashmere Roof To Survive 176°F Heat
content:
The British marque will also slam Project Nightingale’s unique side-opening trunk 15,000 times as part of its testing process.
Photo by:
Rolls-Royce
3:21am ET
Rolls-Royce’s low-volume Project Nightingale convertible is hitting the road for extensive testing.
The coachbuilt EV features a cashmere-lined roof and a side-opening Piano Boot.
As part of the endurance testing process, the exclusive two-door Rolls-Royce will go through extreme temperatures and extensive stress testing.
While some car manufacturers are scratching their heads, trying to come up with new ways to make their electric models more efficient and cheaper to build,
Rolls-Royce
has unlocked a new first-world problem.
The British marque has officially kicked off the real-world testing program for its upcoming Project Nightingale electric convertible, and one of the challenges of developing an ultra-exclusive coachbuilt car is making sure that all the components can survive scorching heat and freezing winters.
Photo by: Rolls-Royce
Sure, all automakers do the same, but I haven’t heard of many EVs with a cashmere-lined retractable roof that needs to survive temperatures of up to 176°F (80°C). But that’s not all, as the roof will go through 10 separate procedures that will put the fabrics, closing mechanism, and performance to the test.
The side-opening Piano Boot, a first for Rolls-Royce, will also be opened and closed 15,000 times to ensure that it “never interrupts the perfect theater and effortless operation of this hallmark gesture for generations to come.” The company’s words, not mine.
With just 100 cars scheduled to be assembled, the first working prototypes are now driving in Southern Europe, where the company originally started testing its luxury cars over 100 years ago. As part of the endurance testing program, several Project Nightingale EVs will spend a total of 350 weeks driving on Mediterranean roads to the Arctic Circle and the deserts of the Arabian Peninsula.
Gallery: Rolls-Royce Project Nightingale
Along the way, the prototypes will have to endure extreme temperatures and climb as high as 9,022 feet (2,750 meters). Separately, a collective 1,430 hours will be spent on aerodynamic modelling and wind tunnel testing to ensure that air won’t become a nuisance. With a practically silent powertrain, Rolls-Royce wants its exclusive EV to eliminate all unwanted sounds, enabling occupants to enjoy the sounds of nature from the comfort of their battery-powered Rolls.
Speed testing at up to 155 miles per hour is also part of the whole process, during which a specially designed electric wind deflector will go through its paces to minimize wind turbulence in the cabin.
Unveiled earlier this year, the Rolls-Royce Project Nightingale is the company’s first Coachbuild Collection model. Based on the same Architecture of Luxury aluminium spaceframe that underpins the electric two-door
, the 100 Nightingale EVs are expected to be powered by a dual-motor setup with over 600 horsepower and 800 pound-feet of torque.
Pricing is being kept under wraps, but rumors suggest that every unit will cost anywhere between $5 and $10 million. Deliveries are scheduled to start in 2028.

title: Tesla Cybercab Inherited One Of The Most Annoying Things About Owning A Tesla
content:
Riders report that Tesla's robotaxis are taking strange routes, something that Teslas owners have been highlighting for years
Photo by:
2:40pm ET
The Tesla Cybercab seems to have inherited a problem that owners have complained about for years: navigation.
One rider says that a simple 10-minute drive took them over an hour to complete.
Navigation issues have plagued Tesla owners for some time, but the robotaxi's issues may be compounded by tighter safety constraints.
Tesla owners have complained about their cars' navigation systems for years, and now, the cars operating on
Tesla's robotaxi network
seem to be experiencing similar problems.
Normally, this is just something that's annoying. The navigation points you right when you should go left, only for you to figure out that it just put you on a 5-mile detour for seemingly no good reason. If you catch it early enough, just flip a U-turn, and you're golden. Unfortunately,
's driverless cars don't have that option.
One rider in Austin, Texas recently experienced this firsthand when they hopped in a Cybercab expecting a ten-minute trip to their destination. The Cybercab had other plans:
"Was supposed to be a quick 10 minute hop from 99 Ranch to the Domain. The car had other plans and took me on a massive south detour through East Austin," wrote one user on
. "Guess the Cybercab wanted the scenic route today. Total ride time was 70 minutes."
One issue likely responsible for this rider's hour-long trip in the robotaxi is the restriction on highway travel. Tesla's fleet sticks to surface-level, low-speed roads. Another,
as one report from 2025 points out
, could be at-grade railroad crossings
across Austin
. Put the two together, and now the Cybercab has to do some routing magic to make the trip possible. The user said that upon booking the ride, the Robotaxi app didn't indicate how long the trip would take.
Other Tesla Robotaxi riders have reported odd routes. An Axios reporter said the Cybercab
dropped him off
at the business next door to where he wanted to go. It's unclear how frequently these problems occur across the service as a whole.
It's common for robotaxis to have restrictions on which kinds of roads they can handle. Waymo operating in the San Francisco Bay Area for well over a year before its cars began venturing onto highways with paying passengers. Tesla did not respond to questions about whether this detour had to do with a mapping error, operational design domain constraints, or both.
However, it's hard to ignore that Tesla has had an ongoing mapping problem for ages. Users have been
complaining
Tesla's navigation
has made
illogical decisions
, including on Full Self-Driving (Supervised). The only difference in this case is that there's no driver behind the wheel to nudge the car in the right direction if that occurs.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
If the fleet's restrictions on highway use or railroad crossings change in the future, it could help to cut down on some of the issues that early robotaxi riders are seeing today. However, CEO Elon Musk did say that Tesla was going to be "
super paranoid
" about safety in its rollout. So the expansion to more types of road conditions may happen gradually.
Either way, whether it's the tight boundaries that Tesla's driverless cars have today, or generalized navigation issues, it seems that the robotaxi fleet itself isn't immune to the same types of problems that owners have been complaining about online for years.

title: Tesla Wants $50,000 Deposits For A Roadster Nobody Has Seen Yet
content:
Tesla Wants $50,000 Deposits For A Roadster Nobody Has Seen Yet
The Roadster will be revealed in two weeks. Is $50,000 too much to ask to reserve something sight unseen?
- Tesla reopened reservations for the Roadster, and they cost $50,000 a pop.
- The company plans to unveil the new supercar on October 1.
- Elon Musk has made bold promises about what the Roadster will be like.
The last time Elon Musk asked people for $50,000 deposits on the Tesla Roadster was in 2017. Those reservation holders were told they'd get their car in 2020. That did not happen. In fact, it still hasn't. Now, those same reservation holders must be getting déjà vu, because Tesla is once again asking for $50,000 deposits to get in line for a Roadster. Insert that Bernie Sanders meme here.
Tesla's reservation page went live last week, and the company is asking for a $5,000 initial payment due immediately, plus another $45,000 wired within 10 days. The initial $5,000 is fully refundable, though.
Thankfully for the people dropping fifty grand now, the production car actually has a reveal date. Tesla says we're going to see the Roadster (again) on October 1. So new reservation holders won't have to wait long to see what they've spent brand-new 3 Series money reserving. Both Marques Brownlee and Sam Altman were among the high-profile customers who plunked down the cash to reserve a Roadster after it was revealed nearly a decade ago. But they got tired of waiting and asked for refunds not too long ago.
Tesla first opened up reservations for the Roadster in November 2017, after the vehicle was unveiled as a "one more thing" surprise at an event showcasing the Tesla Semi truck. For a limited time, Tesla took $250,000 deposits for a special Founders Series. For several years, it allowed customers to plunk down $50,000 to snag a standard Roadster. Now that Tesla is unveiling the production Roadster within a couple of weeks, reservations are open once more.
No one knows what exactly the Roadster is going to be like when it's unveiled at SpaceX's Waco, Texas, rocket-testing facility next week.
The automaker originally promised a top speed of over 250 mph, a 0-60 time under two seconds, and 620-plus miles of range. Since then, Musk has claimed the sports car would be able to fly (thanks to SpaceX technology) and that it would hit 60 mph in an unfathomable 1 second. He's also since cast doubt on the value of having over 600 miles of range in an EV, due to the weight of the battery. Another potential change has to do with the design; the teaser image on Tesla's website indicates a "cyber" refresh that would make the Roadster look more like Tesla's modern lineup. (The Semi, too, got a facelift before actually going on sale.)
Tesla has reportedly cleared the airspace near the event, suggesting that we might see this rocket idea in action. The Information reported that Tesla will show off a street legal car, plus one that flies. Hopefully for Tesla, that goes better than throwing a steel ball at the Cybertruck did.
"It'll be a banger," Musk said recently about the upcoming demonstration on the All In Podcast. "Excitement guaranteed. Success is not guaranteed, but excitement is."
I know what I—and I'm sure the reservation holders new and old—will be looking out for: a production-ready model with a price and a release date, or at least a production timeline. After keeping reservation holders on the hook for close to a decade, it seems like that's the least Tesla could do.

title: The Tesla Semi Had This Reviewer Skeptical. Now He Thinks It’s A Game Changer
content:
Top Gear’s Jack Scarlett thought the electric truck had missed its moment. A factory tour and a passenger ride changed his mind.
Photo by:
8:00am ET
Top Gear’s Jack Scarlett went from doubting the Tesla Semi to calling it a potential game changer.
Tesla’s focus on efficiency extends from the Semi’s powertrain to how it’s built and repaired.
Rivals already haul freight on electricity. Tesla now has to prove its truck makes better business sense.
Tesla took so long to get the Semi ready for production that it needed to give the truck
a facelift
along the way.
Top Gear’s
Jack Scarlett arrived in Nevada wondering whether the world had moved on, but after getting a ride in a Semi, he now thinks it may be Tesla’s most significant new vehicle since the Model S or Model 3.
His skepticism is reasonable. While Tesla kept pushing back the Semi's launch date, other manufacturers beat it to market. In Europe, Volvo began series production of its heavy-duty FH Electric range in September 2022. In the U.S., the Freightliner eCascadia entered production that same year and had already covered more than six million miles across over 50 customer fleets by May 2024.
Mercedes-Benz joined the long-haul fight with customer deliveries of the eActros 600 in December 2024 (I saw one at work while on an EV tour of Europe last year). By April 2025,
Volvo had sold 5,000 electric trucks
worldwide while Tesla was still working toward mass production. Volvo’s total includes different truck types, not just Semi rivals, but it still shows how late Tesla is to the heavy-duty EV market.
An impressive and unique machine, the Semi may have been worth the wait. After years of pilot manufacturing, it's nearing volume production. Scarlett rode shotgun with Semi program chief Dan Priestley, toured the factory, and discovered that some of this truck’s cleverest features have nothing to do with going fast or far.
The central argument is efficiency. Batteries are heavy, and every unnecessary pound eats into a truck’s earning potential. Tesla designed the Semi’s battery structure and chassis to support each other, reducing redundant structural material. It says designing the Semi as an EV from the outset saves weight, because its battery and chassis share structural duties instead of duplicating them.
Its three-motor setup also disconnects the two-motor axle during cruising, leaving one efficiency-focused motor to handle constant-speed cruising, even when loaded up.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The Semi packs
548 kilowatt-hours in Standard Range form
and 822 kWh in the Long Range. Tesla quotes U.S. ranges of 325 and 500 miles, with electricity consumption around 1.7 kWh per mile. It also notes that roughly 60% of range can be replenished in 30 minutes when hooked up to
a Megacharger
As with passenger cars, the idea is to replenish range while the driver is already taking a break, not turn charging into a separate trip with extra downtime, and Tesla thinks the Semi’s charging speed makes that possible.
That philosophy extends to the Nevada factory that builds it, designed to churn out up to 50,000 trucks annually. Body panels are powder-coated,
Top Gear
learned, eliminating the need for a conventional paint shop. Workers install cabin components through the open rear before closing it up. The nose comes in three sections, so if it gets damaged, you don’t have to replace the whole thing.
More On This
But what's it like on the road? Riding shotgun, Scarlett says he briefly forgets there’s a fully loaded trailer behind them, like Jay Leno did when he
tried the truck earlier this year
. Overall, the video is a fascinating look into the work Tesla did to get this truck to market in its current form—even if it's years late. As Tesla opens up deliveries and offers the truck in new markets like Europe, we'll start to see if the trucking world bites.

title: These Absolutely Wild-Looking EVs Are Saudi Arabia's First Homegrown Cars
content:
These Absolutely Wild-Looking EVs Are Saudi Arabia's First Homegrown Cars
The Ceer Exobot SUV and sedan have yoke steering, 850 horsepower, and radical wedge designs.
- Saudi Arabia's first homegrown car company, Ceer, unveiled its first cars on Monday.
- The Exobot SUV and sedan are wild-looking, wedge-shaped EVs with gullwing doors.
- Ceer is a joint venture between the Saudi Public Investment fund and Foxconn, the contract manufacturing giant that assembles iPhones.
Saudi Arabia's first automaker just revealed what it's been working on since it was founded in 2022. Ceer, the car startup created by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Taiwanese contract-manufacturing giant Foxconn, will hit the EV market with two vehicles from the same "Exobot" platform, a sedan and an SUV.
Spy shots hinted at it and the official photos from Monday's reveal confirm: These extreme-looking EVs make the Cybertruck look about as tame as a Honda Civic. The Saudis are swinging for the fences with Ceer, which is a key pillar of the Kingdom's strategy to diversify its business away from fossil fuels.
Gallery: Ceer Exobot EVs
The automaker plans to launch five more models over the next five years, making for a seven-car portfolio that spans propulsion types. But it starts with these otherworldly Exobot siblings, which were designed by Rob Melville, McLaren's former design director.
While the two cars have drastically different body styles, they have the same basic DNA. Both feature super-low noses and get taller at the back, lending them look that evokes the wedge-shaped cars of the 1970s.
Ceer Exobot SUV
But they're distinctly futuristic, incorporating gullwing doors, copious amounts of glass, concept car-like bodywork, and light bars in front and back. I can't help but think of how much the sedan reminds me of the Herrera Riptide Terrier from Cyberpunk 2077. If photos of that game's cars weren't all over Melville's inspiration board, I'll be shocked.
Those light bars, by the way, are fitted with 32 different lighting elements, as a way to honor Saudi Arabia's unification in 1932. According to Autocar, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had a big say in what the final products looked like.
Ceer Exobot Sedan
“His Royal Highness really pushed us hard,” Ceer boss James DeLuca told Autocar. “I’ve been in this industry for 47 years and our head of design, Rob Melville, came from McLaren. We thought we had done a pretty good job and the board said ‘don’t show us what the rest of the world is doing' we want something new, unique and different."
Inside, the cars feature sharp edges and a yoke-shaped steering wheel that's missing its top bit. There's a massive 8K screen that spans the width of the windshield, plus a vertical touchscreen ahead of the center console and a ton of Lamborghini-like hexagonal shapes. Look closely and you'll also spot windows below the sedan's belt line, by the front passengers' outer knees. Other than that, the sparse, screen-heavy interior doesn't look nearly as original as these cars' exteriors.
Under that wild-looking skin is an 800-volt platform three motors, a 112 kilowatt-hour battery, and a claimed 850 horsepower. DC fast-charging from a 10-80% state-of-charge takes 30 minutes and peaks at 250 kW, according to Ceer. That's about middle of the road these days. All of that goes for both the sedan and SUV.
Where they differ are in range and acceleration. The sedan is quicker, hitting 62 mph in 2.6 seconds, while the SUV takes 2.9 seconds. The sedan has 416 miles of range, while the SUV has 348 miles. Both estimates are based on the NEDC cycle, so they're a bit more generous than EPA ratings. Last year, Ceer announced that Croatia's Rimac will supply its electric drive systems.
Saudi Arabia wants Ceer to help turn it into a real manufacturing presence, and it joins Lucid Motors, which already manufactures cars in the country. But it doesn't seem like customers in the States will be able to buy one anytime soon—even if they're taken by the outlandish designs. (My eight-year-old thought the sedan looked "super cool.") According to its website, Ceer vehicles are "tailor-made" for Saudi Arabia and some neighboring countries.

title: This Chinese SUV Has Built-In Propellers So It Can Drive Across Water
content:
This Chinese SUV Has Built-In Propellers So It Can Drive Across Water
The Geely Battleship 700 can float and even traverse water thanks to its built-in propellers.
- The Geely Battleship 700 can drive short distances in the water thanks to two propellers at the rear.
- The vehicle can swim in water for 40 minutes, or float for up to two hours.
- It starts at just under $30,000 in China.
China’s car market is full of fun tech. Whether that's cars with karaoke machines or suspension systems that danc e, it’s not hard to find a Chinese EV or PHEV that does something completely fantastical. Yet, despite the abundance of futuristic (if sometimes gimmicky) tech, Chinese brands are still finding ways to one-up each other.
Case in point: Geely's latest SUV can act as a boat.
Believe it or not, the Battleship 700 isn't the only EV designed to float. Elon Musk famously wanted the Cybertruck to serve "briefly" as a boat in emergency situations. Chinese brands have made good on that promise.
BYD designed the Yangwang U8 SUV to float and actually move around should an owner find themselves in deep water. BYD bills this as an "emergency floating mode" that works for 30 minutes. The SUV's front wheels act as rudders, while the motors spin the wheels and give it a bit of locomotion. As nifty as that sounds, forward propulsion in the water isn’t so good, partially because wheels designed for the road can only do so much.
Geely has an answer to that in the Battleship 700, its own Land Rover Defender-like big SUV that competes with the YangWang. The SUV has a full-blown propeller system, turning this off-road plug-in hybrid into something like a boat.
Geely calls this feature an emergency flotation and escape mode, meaning it's meant to protect occupants in a worst-case scenario and not a party trick for cruising across a lake. Here's how it works. In the water, two 11.5 horsepower propellers on the back of the vehicle—they look a lot like exhaust tips—can propel the vehicle to a little over 4 mph. The Battleship 700 also has sonar so you don’t run into anything in the water. On speed, it has the Yangwang U9 beat; that rival can reportedly churn through the water at about 2 mph.
As impressive as this is, the experience isn't unlimited. The Battleship 700 can “swim” in water for about 40 minutes, or float for up to two hours. Remember, this is less of a car-as-a-boat feature, but a safety feature meant to save the occupants in case the vehicle finds itself in a deep body of water.
For the rest of the time, when the Battleship 700 is on land, power comes from a 2.0-liter turbocharged engine that works alongside three motors (two in the back, one in front). The SUV boasts a combined peak output of 1,113 horsepower. Those motors are fed by a 47.14 kWh battery. The combined range of the battery and gas engine is 1,100 miles, according to China’s CLTC cycle. Pricing for this model starts at just under $30,000, but can reach as high as $58,000 in China’s market.
The Battleship 700 has already gone on sale in China, but Geely has plans to export it to other markets, including Australia.
The ability to be a boat sometimes isn't the only strange feature Geely added. There’s also an oxygen-delivery system, which Geely claims can be used via a mask or in the cabin when traveling in high-altitude locations. It just goes to show: In China's cutthroat car market, features like AI assistants and in-car fridges can only dazzle buyers for so long before something better comes along.
