title: 刷视频也能教会机器人干活！1200亿tokens人类动作预训练，误差按幂律下降
content:
刷视频也能教会机器人干活！1200亿tokens人类动作预训练，误差按幂律下降
押注互联网里的人类经验
允中 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
9月17日，Figure把Helix 2.5带进了旧金山湾区30个陌生家庭。它要收拾散落在客厅里的玩具、叠毛巾、铺床。机器人到达现场后，不再采集新数据，不更新模型权重，也不根据现场执行结果重新选择模型。
视频很容易被概括成“人形机器人‘零样本’做家务”。严格来说却并非如此。三个任务此前都在其他环境中用专门数据做过适配。Figure所说的“零样本（zero-shot）”，是指机器人第一次进入这些家庭，面对新的布局和操作对象时，不再针对当地环境和物体重新训练。
注：Figure Helix 2.5在30个此前未采集任务训练数据的湾区家庭中执行整理客厅、叠毛巾和铺床任务。这里的“零样本”指机器人面对新的家庭环境、空间布局和操作对象实例时无需现场重新训练，并不意味着模型此前未学习过这些任务；相关任务此前已使用其他环境采集的数据完成适配。来源：Figure
视频之外，Figure还公布了两组更容易被忽略的实验。
第一组直接比较是否经过Index预训练。
Figure用同一批任务专属数据训练了两套策略模型，架构、优化方式、超参数、下游数据和评估方法保持一致。一套随机初始化，另一套从Index预训练模型开始。前者在30个陌生家庭中的完整任务成功率为9%，后者达到56%。
这个56%要求完整完成任务，部分完成任务的情况不得分。以收拾客厅为例，所有玩具都必须进入篮子；如果出于安全原因需要人工干预，整个执行回合直接记为失败。按照Figure披露的实验协议，两组模型之间的主要差异是——是否经过Index预训练。
另一组实验转向离线评测，专门考察预训练数据规模。
Figure用Index的四档嵌套数据（nested data）子集训练模型，预训练数据总跨度为8倍；模型大小不变，下游训练方式也保持一致。每个模型再使用相同的任务数据进行微调，比较留出测试集上的机器人动作预测损失。
随着Index数据规模翻倍，损失规律下降。Figure还用较小规模实验拟合趋势，再预测最大规模模型的测试结果；官方称，预测误差只相当于整个8倍数据范围内损失变化的0.54%。
这两组实验结果很容易被囫囵理解为“Figure发现了机器人规模定律（Scaling Law）”，但它们本质上是对不同问题的回答。
第一组实验中的9%到56%说明，有没有大规模的人类行为预训练，会显著影响机器人在陌生环境中的闭环泛化。
第二组中的四档数据的损失曲线说明，当人类数据预训练规模继续扩大后，这种收益在下游机器人动作预测上呈现出可测量的随规模变化的曲线。
Figure目前没有公布1倍、2倍、4倍、8倍Index预训练分别对应多少真实家庭成功率。也就是说，预训练规模持续扩大，对闭环机器人表现会产生怎样的连续变化，这条曲线还没有公开。
上：Figure在真实机器人闭环评测中，对比了未经Index预训练与经过Index预训练的模型。在其公开的多项未见任务中，Index预训练模型的成功率均明显更高；Figure在正文中将总体结果概括为完整任务成功率从9%提升至56%。这组实验回答的是：“有没有大规模人类行为预训练，会不会影响真实机器人执行结果？”
下：Figure进一步使用4档严格嵌套的Index数据，将预训练规模从1倍扩大到8倍，并在模型规模、下游训练和评估流程保持一致的情况下，观察到适配后的机器人动作预测验证损失持续下降。这组实验回答的是：“当人类数据预训练规模继续扩大，离线迁移指标是否呈现可预测的规模效应？”
两组实验并非同一条曲线。Figure目前尚未公开1倍、2倍、4倍、8倍Index预训练规模分别对应的真实机器人闭环成功率，因此不能据此推导“预训练规模扩大后，真实任务成功率按相同规律连续提升”。
恰恰是这里，让2026年的机器人预训练出现了一个比“Human Data有没有用”更具体的问题：
人类经验能不能像文本之于大模型那样，成为机器人预训练中一种可以持续扩展、并能预测下游收益的数据来源？
Dyna：人类数据的规模效应已经进入真机闭环
Figure并不是第一个观察到“人类数据越多，机器人越受益”的团队。
8月，Dyna Robotics发布Dyna-2。它把第一视角人类视频构成1000小时、1万小时、10万小时和100万小时四个严格嵌套的数据规模。更大的数据集只是在较小集合上继续增加数据，而且各来源比例保持一致，尽量排除数据分布变化对结果的干扰。
随后，Dyna把四档模型用同一套机器人后训练方法适配到14个真实机器人任务。四档模型的平均归一化得分，依次达到任务可达上限的20%、28%、45%和53%。也就是说，人类视频预训练时的规模差异，经过同样的机器人后训练以后，最终延伸到了真机闭环表现。
注：Dyna分别使用1000小时、1万小时、10万小时和100万小时第一视角人类视频进行预训练，再将四档模型用相同的机器人后训练方案适配到14个真实机器人任务。随着人类视频预训练规模扩大，14项任务的平均归一化表现依次达到任务可达上限的20%、28%、45%和53%，说明预训练阶段的规模差异在经过相同机器人后训练后，仍然延伸到了真实机器人闭环表现。这里的20%—53%是Dyna为了汇总不同任务原生指标而定义的平均归一化表现，并非任务成功率，也不能与Figure在30个陌生家庭中报告的56%完整任务成功率直接比较。
因此，更准确的技术时间线不是“Figure第一次发现人类到机器人的规模定律”。Dyna此前已经展示了更完整的跨本体、从预训练规模一路延伸到闭环真机表现的证据；Figure则把可预测的迁移规模效应明确延伸到了全身人形机器人系统上，并用30个陌生家庭让人类预训练的现实价值变得更加直观。
百万小时之外，Dyna还通过一组消融实验追问：这种规模效应究竟从哪里来？
单独预测动作时，模型随着数据增加出现严重而不稳定的过拟合。加入未来视频预测以后，39个机器人任务上的迁移表现整体改善；而当研究者进一步增加不带动作标签、只用于视频预测的人类视频时，跨本体表现才随着数据规模呈现出稳定的单调提升。
因此，单纯说“扩大人类数据规模就会持续获益”，仍然不够准确。
数据是什么，以及模型被要求从中学什么，共同决定了规模效应会不会出现。
一旦人类经验开始成为机器人预训练资产，追问自然就落到了数据来源本身：这些经验应该从哪里来？
Figure：建立一套可控的人类数据供应链
Figure在Index发布稿中把自己的判断写得很直白：
“要规模化训练真正通用的机器人，所需要的数据并不存在于来源广泛的互联网视频。”
于是它搭建了一套自己的Human Data供应链。
Index通过Creator创作者网络，让人们在真实家庭和工作场所记录任务。到8月底，Figure称平台已经收到超过1600万条视频，并累计向创作者支付1500万美元；Helix 2.5发布时，新的人类视频数据正以约35分钟/秒的速度进入Index。数据随后还要经过质量过滤、反作弊、去重、重新平衡和文本标注。
注：Figure将Creator贡献者上传的真实世界视频依次经过质量过滤与标注、反作弊审查、去重和数据再平衡，最终形成用于训练Helix的数据集。与直接使用互联网公开视频不同，Index代表的是一条“主动建设人类行为数据基础设施”的路线：通过持续采集、筛选和整理，更系统地获得适合Physical AI训练的大规模Human Experience。
算力也在同步扩张。
9月初，Figure宣布与英国AI云厂商Nscale达成战略合作。该合作涉及一份初始价值35亿美元的算力承诺，未来合作规模或将扩大至60亿美元以上；双方计划基于英伟达Vera Rubin平台部署最高10万颗GPU。Figure创始人兼CEO Brett Adcock直言不讳，Helix下一阶段越来越受制于数据和算力。
这是一条资本密集，但对数据分布拥有更强控制力的路线。
某类任务不够，可以定向补；某种环境过多，可以重新平衡；长尾里缺什么，就继续组织人在现实世界里生产。
Index不只是一个不断扩大的数据集，更像是一套可以主动改变训练数据分布的基础设施。
但Figure目前尚未在Helix 2.5相关材料中披露Index全量数据统一的拍摄视角构成，也没有公开完整的人类动作监督机制。现在能够确认的是，它正在以极大的规模采集、筛选和组织真实人类行为数据，而Index预训练已经显著改善了Figure自己的完整人形机器人系统。
Figure的解法，是通过专门采集和数据治理，主动塑造自己需要的训练分布。
行业同时在尝试另一种办法：不重新生产全部数据，而是提高模型从互联网公开视频中提取可迁移信号的能力。
另一条路线：让模型理解互联网中的人类经验
互联网公开视频不是天然的机器人数据（Robot Data）。
视频中的镜头位置多样，人体会被遮挡，动作也没有关节控制标签，更没有机器人的本体感知、力反馈和接触状态。视频里一个人伸出手打开橱柜的几十帧，距离一台人形机器人真正需要输出的控制信号还很远。
另外一些团队没有像Figure那样采集更多专门为机器人而生的数据，而是尝试通过模型学习和表示转换，从已有视频中提取可迁移信息。
CoMo从互联网视频中学习连续的潜在运动表示，并为此前没见过的视频生成伪动作（pseudo-action），再与有限的机器人数据共同训练策略模型。“互联网视频能否转成与动作相关的监督信号”，并不是一个全新的命题。
HuRo做得更直接。它把来源和视角各异的人类视频 “机器人化”，转化成更接近机器人观察和动作分布的数据；随着这类预训练数据扩大，真实操作任务的完成度和分布外（OOD）表现继续改善。
Rhoda则绕开了显式的人类动作。它用来源广泛的互联网视频训练因果视频模型，让模型先预测世界接下来如何变化，再通过逆动力学模型把这种预测转换成机器人动作。近期的真实工业任务实验显示，更大的预训练模型和更多训练算力都能改善机器人策略，而且当机器人数据较少时，更强预训练带来的收益更明显。
这些方法虽然机制不同，却都在检验另一种可能：当原始数据离机器人分布较远时，能否通过表示学习（representation learning）、动作恢复或世界建模来弥补其中的差距。
互联网视频的确没有现成的机器人动作轨迹。但其中的人类行为、物体交互和物理世界规律，究竟有多少能够被重新编码成物理AI真正能用的经验，仍然没有定论。
亮源新创（Light Origins）则大胆地把问题又往前推了一步：数据源直接来自普遍存在的互联网人类行为视频。
亮源新创：把预训练数据源推向互联网规模
亮源新创选择的不是专门为机器人训练采集的数据，也不是主要依赖第一人称人类视频，而是尝试从互联网中的第三视角人类行为视频中提取可迁移经验。
互联网上已经积累了海量人类行为视频。这类数据更容易实现规模化和多样性，代价则是更大的人机域差异（domain gap）：镜头并不跟随视频中的人类身体，动作可能被遮挡或剪辑，人类和机器人身体结构不同，视频里没有可以直接执行的动作标签。
根据9月21日亮源新创官网正式发布的技术博客来看，Light-O1先从视频中恢复结构化人类动作，再编码成统一的人形动作表示，与视觉、语言信息一起进行自回归预训练，最终得到一个人类动作先验（Human Action Prior）。
注：从机器人遥操作、UMI等机器人数据，到第一视角人类视频，再到互联网规模的第三视角人类行为视频，数据来源覆盖范围逐步扩大，同时也伴随着视角、本体和动作表示差异的增加。本图用于说明亮源新创选择的人类动作预训练数据来源位置，不代表不同数据来源之间的性能比较。
此次技术博客披露的人类动作预训练规模，从37.5亿扩展到1200亿词元（token），最大规模约对应10万小时人类动作。
Light-O1分别在第一视角人类数据、公开机器人数据和亮源新创自研人形机器人数据上进行目标域适配。随着人类动作预训练规模扩大，适配后的动作预测误差、全身姿态误差和腕部位置误差均持续下降，并呈幂律趋势。亮源新创将这一现象称为“迁移缩放定律”（Transfer Scaling Law）。
注：亮源新创将人类动作预训练规模从37.5亿tokens扩展至1200亿tokens，并在第一视角人类数据、Unitree G1机器人以及亮源自研人形机器人数据等目标域上进行评估。实验显示，随着预训练规模扩大，动作预测误差和身体姿态预测误差在不同目标域上持续下降，呈现幂律缩放趋势。该结果基于目标域适配后的预测指标，用于衡量预训练规模与迁移效果之间的关系，并不等同于真实机器人闭环任务成功率。
人类动作先验并不是亮源新创首创；从公开的互联网视频中提取与动作相关的信号，也已经有CoMo、HuRo等近邻工作。
Light-O1这次更值得关注的，并不是“用了互联网视频”本身，而是把几件此前通常分开研究的问题放进了同一组规模实验：互联网规模的人类动作视频、结构化动作恢复、持续扩大的预训练规模，以及这些规模收益在不同机器人和人形机器人目标域适配后仍然保留下来。
至此，亮源新创首次验证了互联网规模的人类动作预训练对多本体人形机器人的迁移缩放定律。
注：视频展示Light-O1当前模型在机器人平台上的任务执行能力，用于说明预训练和后续适配后的模型具备真实可执行行为。本文讨论的“迁移缩放定律”仍以留出数据上的开环评测为依据。来源：亮源新创
更值得追踪的是：如果模型真的能从距离机器人更远的数据里持续获得可迁移的动作先验，这条“Scaling”（规模效应）之路最终能走到闭环真机的哪一步？
从离线迁移到闭环表现，不同“规模效应”不是一回事
当把Figure、Dyna和亮源新创放在一起，很容易把不同层级的“Scaling”混为一谈。
注：不同团队正在探索Human Experience如何转化为机器人能力。目前公开研究已经分别展示了从人类经验规模化、跨本体迁移、真实机器人闭环表现等不同层面的证据。由于不同研究采用的数据、模型和评测协议不同，本图用于展示公开证据所在层级，不代表企业能力排名或横向比较。制图：原文作者
最基础的一层，是预训练本身能不能随着数据增加持续改善。
再往下一层，是这种改善离开人类数据域以后，能不能在机器人或人形机器人目标域中继续存在。
Figure的四档Index实验和亮源当前的核心结果，主要落在这里：更大规模的人类预训练，对应更好的下游机器人动作相关离线指标。
然后才进入真实机器人的闭环表现。
Figure用Index预训练和随机初始化的9%对56%，证明“有没有预训练”会显著改变机器人在陌生家庭里的实际执行结果；但它尚未公开Index规模每翻倍、闭环成功率如何连续变化。
Dyna则已经用四档人类视频预训练，在相同机器人后训练条件下得到20%、28%、45%、53%的平均归一化闭环得分。两套数字定义完全不同，不能横向比较。
再往下一步，才是最接近产业经济的问题：
达到相同能力时，更强的预训练究竟能少用多少新的机器人真实经验？
Figure给出了一个值得关注的信号：Helix 2.5在一个同任务比较中，只使用此前Helix 02约一半的任务专属数据，就达到相近成功水平，同时把部署范围扩展到了30个陌生家庭。
但这组比较跨了模型代际和评估条件，并不是严格控制的等性能实验，因此不能直接推导“Index普遍把机器人数据需求减半”。
Dyna用大约10分钟机器人示范就完成Bottle Cap Untwisting的实验同样有吸引力，而且表现随着人类视频预训练规模继续提升；但它依然不是一条可以直接换算“多少小时人类数据等于多少小时机器人数据”的曲线。
就目前公开证据而言，亮源新创验证到的仍主要是适配后的离线迁移。
因此，它下一步最有信息量的实验其实很明确：固定机器人适配方案，让不同人类动作预训练规模的模型逐一进入闭环；再改变机器人数据预算，看能否形成等性能曲线。
到那一步，才有条件真正讨论“互联网级人类动作”的数据经济性。
计算最终着眼处：整条数据成本链
机器人行业习惯用“小时数”描述数据规模。
一小时遥操作数据多少钱，一小时Human Video多少钱，现有的互联网视频则几乎不需要重新去采。按照这种算法，Figure看起来昂贵，互联网原生路线似乎天然便宜。
实际账本远没有这么简单。
Figure愿意为Creator创作者、采集体系、质量控制和主动数据再平衡付钱，换来的是更可控的数据分布：缺什么，就能继续生产什么。35亿美元级别的算力合作，则继续把这套数据基础设施推向更大的模型。
从互联网公开视频出发，确实省掉了重新让人执行一次任务的物理采集成本。
新的账单会出现在别处：哪些视频值得留下，人体动作能恢复到什么精度，镜头运动和遮挡如何处理，怎样把人类动作转成机器人可用的表示，以及需要多少训练算力，才能把这些嘈杂经验真正压进模型。
Dyna提供了第三种可能：并非所有视频都必须恢复出高质量动作标签，世界建模本身也可以让大量只有视觉经验的视频参与规模化学习。
所以，这场数据战未必会以“谁拥有更多视频”决胜，更不能只比较两种路线的原始采集成本。
真正要算的是整条链路。
从得到一段经验，到它最终变成机器人可以迁移、可以执行的能力，需要支付的不只有采集成本，还有表示、对齐、算力，以及最后仍然难以完全省掉的真实机器人经验。
Helix 2.5让人类经验成为一条更难忽视的规模化轴线；Dyna已经证明，这条轴有机会一路穿到真实机器人闭环；亮源新创则把实验继续推向距离机器人数据分布更远但却最为丰富的互联网级人类行为。
接下来值得比较的，也许不再只是哪个公司拥有最多“小时数”。
而是机器人获得下一项能力时，整条链路还要向真实世界支付多少成本。

title: 华为全新智驾上车，全域L3架构，岚图最强旗舰MPV 42万开卖
content:
华为全新智驾上车，全域L3架构，岚图最强旗舰MPV 42万开卖
纯电120kWh大电池，18.1吨压着照样开
杰西卡 发自 ROBO-车
量子位ROBO | 公众号 AI4ROBO
车圈现在恐怕没人能比岚图更能整活了吧……
上个月岚图追光S刚完成了360°隧道大回环挑战，更早之前泰山X8还无安全绳爬过45°的天梯，现在新MPV又出新花样了：
先是6台MPV摞成车塔，上方5台合计18.1吨，压着最底下一台车完成起步、行驶和刹停；随后还有双车叠加一字马演示，两组车辆上下叠放，同步驶过减速带。
各种极限挑战的传播效果确实很足，但岚图真正想推到台前的其实是车身、底盘、控制，及其集大成之作——
全新旗舰MPV岚图梦想家9。
这款车刚刚上市，推出了三个版本，售价41.99万～52.99万元，比预售便宜了1万元。
在梦想家9身上，岚图基本把当前高端MPV能拿出来的头部技术装到了一起：
华为乾崑智驾ADS 5、896线激光雷达、鸿蒙座舱HarmonySpace 6、三腔空气悬架、双阀EDC、双向10°后轮转向、全系800V……
也就是说，梦想家9瞄准的，已经不只是传统豪华MPV擅长的空间和第二排舒适性，智能化、底盘、三电、安全和整车控制，通通被岚图拉到了旗舰规格。
华为ADS 5上车，5米3大MPV也上后轮转向
还是先看智能化。
岚图称，梦想家9基于全域L3级架构开发，全系搭载华为乾崑智驾ADS 5。
感知硬件共有37个，其中包括一颗896线双光路图像级主激光雷达、3颗固态补盲激光雷达，组成四激光雷达方案，覆盖城区、高速、泊车等主要驾驶场景。
896线主激光雷达也是华为今年高阶智驾方案的一项重点升级。
相比此前主流车载激光雷达，更高线数主要服务于更细密的点云感知，配合周围3颗固态补盲雷达，进一步扩大车辆近场和侧向感知范围。
而且放到一辆大型MPV上，其价值会更加明显——
梦想家9车长5325mm、宽1998mm，轴距达到3200mm。城市窄路、地库、泊车乃至高速长途，都比尺寸更小的轿车更考验驾驶者。
高阶智驾承担一部分操作压力，底盘则负责处理大尺寸本身带来的物理负担。
梦想家9首搭岚图虎踞P智能底盘。悬架结构为前双叉臂、后五连杆，配备三腔空气弹簧和双阀EDC减振器。
三腔空簧支持4档刚度调节，调节范围达到150%；双阀EDC分别控制压缩与回弹，再交给VMC智能底盘控制系统统筹悬架、动力、制动和转向。
另一个关键配置是双向10°后轮转向。
低速时，后轮与前轮反向偏转，帮助5米3车身缩小转弯和掉头所需空间；高速状态下则可以通过同向偏转辅助车身稳定。
大型MPV天然有几个很难绕开的工程问题：车长、轴距大，城市灵活性差；整车重、满载频率高，对俯仰、侧倾和制动控制要求也更高。
三腔空悬、双阀EDC、后轮转向，解决的都是同一组问题。岚图近期一连串极限挑战，也一直强调底盘和整车控制。
追光S完成360°隧道大回环，需要车辆以约130km/h速度进入回环，对动力持续输出、转向精度、车身刚度和底盘控制同时提出要求。
梦想家9则是进行了6车叠放挑战，上方5台车合计18.1吨，最底层车辆还要完成负重移动，车塔起步、行驶、刹停后，底层车辆车门仍可正常开启，动力、转向、制动和悬架系统保持正常。
随后进行的双车叠加通过减速带，则是为了验证三腔空悬、双阀EDC和VMC控制两组车辆车身起伏的可靠性。
极限项目本身和用户日常驾驶有明显距离，能展示出的底层能力却很明确：
悬架负责承载，电驱负责精确输出，制动负责稳住重心，VMC再把几套系统放到一起协同控制。
安全也沿着同一思路继续强化。
梦想家9采用全域L3级冗余架构设计，岚图称感知、计算、电源等八大核心系统均设置冗余备份。
需要说明的是，L3级架构设计描述的是硬件和系统冗余基础，车辆实际开放到什么驾驶能力，仍要以法规及交付后的软件功能为准。
被动安全方面，前舱采用七重防碰撞结构，二排B柱区域使用2200MPa超高强度钢，车尾设置五层碰撞防护，第三排座椅靠背也加入钢板。
对于MPV，第三排安全尤其重要。
相比不少七座SUV把第三排更多作为临时座位，MPV三排乘坐频率更高，满载又是常见工况，安全结构需要真正覆盖前中后三排。
智能化的另一部分，则交给了鸿蒙座舱HarmonySpace 6。
梦想家9采用MoLA 2.0架构，引入新一代多模态大模型，SystemAgent端到端大模型参数达到千亿级，较上一代百亿级继续提高。核心方向也从执行简单语音指令，向理解更复杂的自然语言、调用不同座舱功能延伸。
车内前排配备两块15.6英寸华为智慧屏，同时提供29英寸AR-HUD，二排还有21.4英寸吸顶娱乐屏。
更有意思的是跨系统联动。
用户靠近车辆后，智慧大灯点亮、升降立标升起、侧滑门打开，空气悬架同步降低车身，二排座椅向车门方向旋转45°。
座舱、车门、底盘和座椅不再各自工作，开始围绕同一个上下车场景联动。
对于高端智能车，软件能力继续往前发展之后，体验差异也越来越取决于车辆不同系统能否真正协同起来。
120kWh大电池上车，三排补齐舒适配置
三电方面，梦想家9同时保留插混和纯电，并且全系采用800V高压平台。
先看插混版。其动力系统由1.5T发动机和前后双电机组成，综合功率约560kW、综合扭矩910N·m，匹配65kWh三元锂电池。
CLTC纯电续航达到340km，综合续航1500km，同时支持5C快充，20%～80%充电只需要12分钟。
对于MPV用户，插混大电池路线的逻辑相对比较清楚：
日常通勤可以尽可能依靠纯电，340km纯电续航进一步降低发动机介入频率；长途多人出行保留燃油补能，65kWh电池再配合5C快充，也让插混车型获得了接近纯电车的补电能力。
不过，大型MPV车身迎风面积更大、整备质量更高，还经常面对满员和大量行李工况。如果纯电路线要覆盖长途出行，单靠优化电耗很难解决全部问题。
所以，更大的电池容量仍然是直接办法。纯电版前后双电机峰值功率分别达到175kW和300kW，综合功率475kW，电池容量直接提到了120kWh，CLTC续航701km。
座舱空间则回到了MPV熟悉的领域。
梦想家9采用2+2+3七座布局，第二排座椅支持横向滑动、多角度旋转、零重力和机械按摩。
座椅可以向外旋转45°，配合空气悬架降低车身高度，方便老人和孩子上下车；停车之后继续旋转，可以和第三排形成面对面的布局。
零重力模式最大躺角达到147°。二排除了座椅加热，扶手和腿托也支持加热。
车顶采用了左右分布式天幕，两侧光线可以分别调节。
扶手上控制屏还能拆下来拿在手里操作。
Ultra+版进一步把通风、加热和按摩配备到了第三排。
二排座椅转过来后，前后对坐空间可以达到1.6米，既服务商务会客，也给家庭出行留出了更多空间组合方式。
车内配备13L双门冷暖冰箱，温度覆盖-6℃至50℃；二、三排提供LC调光玻璃和分段式全景穹顶，辅以遮阳帘和氛围灯。
外观上最显眼的，也是礼尊版配备的可升降发光水晶立标，车辆解锁时升起，锁车后可以收回。
这个翅膀，这个升降功能，怎么感觉好像有点“劳里劳气”【doge】：
旁边还有一套华为HUAWEI XPIXEL双百万像素智慧投影大灯，左右总像素约260万，可以投射导航箭头、车道提示和迎宾图案。
最终价格也正式落地：
- Ultra版插混41.99万元，纯电42.99万元；
- Ultra+版插混45.99万元，纯电46.99万元；
- 礼尊版插混51.99万元，纯电52.99万元。
整体价格覆盖41.99万～52.99万元，相比此前42.99万元起的预售价，正式起售价降低1万元。
另外，梦想家9右舵版计划从11月开始进入海外市场。
随着梦想家9上市，岚图梦想家系列也从30万元级一路延伸到70万元级。
高端MPV开考整车基本功
对于岚图而言，梦想家的重要性不言而喻。
这一系列累计销量已经超过20万辆，也是岚图目前用户基础和市场认知都相对成熟的一条产品线。
岚图切入50万元级MPV时，也没有重新建立一个车型名称，依然沿用了梦想家。
目前来看，普通梦想家承担30万～40万元级市场，梦想家9继续向40万～50万元级延伸，更高端还有四座版本，最终形成了30万～70万元MPV矩阵。
这背后是一条明确的商业逻辑：
一款车卖得多，解决的是规模；同一个产品名称可以持续向更高价位延展，则开始影响品牌的价格能力。
梦想家帮助岚图在高端MPV市场站住一个相对稳定的位置，梦想家9接下来承担的就是把已有的用户基础、车型认知继续向50万元级传递。
但这也是梦想家9要直面的难点。
如今的高端新能源MPV赛道不可谓不拥挤：
腾势D9、魏牌高山、极氪009、智界V9、别克GL8新能源，再加上原有的赛那、格瑞维亚等产品……在40万～50万元上下已经聚集了多条技术路线和多个品牌。
但市场规模本身，并没有随着产品数量同步快速扩大。
所以不同车型接下来的竞争，更接近一场存量市场里的产品替换和价格带争夺。
新能源MPV早期的确很容易建立感知差异。
电机带来了更好的平顺性和静谧性，大电池降低短途用油频率；随后冰箱、大屏、零重力座椅、电动侧滑门快速普及，又进一步拉高了传统MPV的舒适体验。
然而，配置普及速度太快，40万元以上产品现在几乎都能把冰箱、娱乐屏、座椅按摩摆上配置表，单点舒适功能形成的领先周期越来越短。
由此，各品牌开始向车辆更底层的能力集中。
同时，智能化也成为了新的变量。随着华为合作伙伴的增多，具备华为最新能力的车型，也会在中国高端汽车市场越来越常见。
这也正在成为50万元级新能源MPV新的门槛。
智驾越来越容易成为高端车的共同能力后，真正难复制的部分，依然会重新回到整车工程。
One More Thing
梦想家9这次正式上市之前，其实原本还计划过一场预售发布会。
结果发布会前一天的9月4日，岚图临时把发布会取消了，第二天直接开始预售，车辆同步进店。
岚图董事长、CEO卢放当时给出的说法，是希望减少冗余的营销造势，先让用户去体验产品。
预售48小时，小订突破3万辆。
所以这么看，一辆车开几场发布会或许真是次要的，产品能不能打，才是更要紧的……

title: 它石智航顶尖团队引领中国具身智能率先迈入规模化落地阶段
content:
它石智航顶尖团队引领中国具身智能率先迈入规模化落地阶段
它石智航将继续扩大研发团队，加快布局生产基地，全面提升机器人交付能力
近日，2026“跨国企业上海行”推介会在上海举行。在“中外企业分享”环节，它石智航创始人兼CEO陈亦伦作为现场唯一获邀发言的上海本土企业代表，与来自24个国家和地区的220余位企业家、行业组织和投资机构代表，分享了它石以具身智能技术赋能全球工业转型的实践与思考。
当前，全球工业正在经历从传统自动化向物理AI的智能跃迁。受制于劳动力结构变化与工艺复杂度，汽车总装、精密线束装配及精细零件上料等工序仍高度依赖人工，成为自动化升级难以越过的“最后一公里”。与此同时，制造业海量的真实作业数据与严苛的工程标准，为具身智能切入实体经济提供了坚实基础。
陈亦伦表示，具身智能不能停留在实验室，一定要到真实产线经受最严苛的检验。中国具有全球最丰富的制造业场景和应用需求，这为机器人模型的训练、验证和迭代提供了不可替代的土壤。凭借长期产业生态积淀所释放的系统性能力，中国正推动本土具身智能率先进入规模化落地阶段。兼具顶尖复合型AI人才、精密供应链与开放合作生态的上海，正成为承载并放大这一产业优势的重要高地。
作为生于上海、面向全球的具身智能企业，它石智航已迅速完成了基座模型突破、硬件迭代优化、规模化落地的三级跃迁。
首先，它石首创了“以人为中心”的数据范式，采集了超百万小时高质量真实人类操作数据，自主研发AWE具身智能基座大模型，成功攻克精细操作、柔性物体处理、长程任务规划和泛化能力等工业难题，为给机器人装上了“通用大脑”；其次，依托长三角强大的“一小时产业圈”，打造“为AI而生”的硬件和本体，包括自研的A系列轮式机器人、T系列双足机器人和21自由度准直驱DexHand灵巧手；在上海专项政策的大力支持下，快速推进具身智能技术的规模化产线验证，让机器人实现了“真干活”。
上海领先的人工智能人才优势，为它石智航的快速成长提供了核心支撑。据介绍，目前，它石智航已经组建起了一支硕博占比超80%的顶尖研发团队。创始团队由五人组成，分别是：创始人兼CEO陈亦伦、董事长李震宇、联合创始人兼首席科学家丁文超、联合创始人兼首席架构师陈同庆、联合创始人兼首席战略官Vincent。团队成员普遍拥有自动驾驶和人工智能相关领域丰富经验，不仅拥有业界领先的具身大模型构建能力、本体研发能力、软硬一体产品量产能力和超大复杂系统的工程化落地能力，而且对目标行业痛点有深度洞察，能够精准锚定高价值应用场景，交付完整解决方案。
陈亦伦表示，未来，它石智航将继续扩大研发团队，加快布局生产基地，全面提升机器人交付能力，同时积极构建“中国研发、面向全球”的业务布局，与海内外合作伙伴共建行业生态，为全球工业转型升级贡献更多的“具身智能方案”，努力成长为“全球工业智能化转型的重要赋能者”。
本文由它石智航提供，量子位获授权转载，观点归原作者所有。

title: 实时世界模型进入“全科生”阶段，PixVerse R2先交卷！
content:
实时世界模型进入“全科生”阶段，PixVerse R2先交卷！
实时性和通用能力，世界模型可以全都要
梦瑶 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
这年头，实时生成的世界模型越来越会「造世界」了。
画面更夯，控制更细，但一旦走到实时生成这一步，继续往上做能力，就会有个很难绕开的坎：
能力越强，实时越难守，整个行业也因此苦既要又要的增长难题久矣。
更麻烦的是，实时世界模型还得面对世界模型的共性难题，相比LLM，能力想沿着稳定路径持续增长也没那么容易。
然而，这个困扰行业多年的实时世界模型的老bug，如今，已经有厂商用实际模型完成验证并跑出了答案——
实时性和通用能力，世界模型可以全都要。
这个玩家的名字大家应该不陌生：爱诗科技。
其实今年1月的时候，爱诗就发布了首个通用实时世界模型R1，主打持续生成能力，当时直接在网上火出圈了一波。
就在这两天，全新的实时世界模型PixVerse R2，也上线了。
甚至一经上线，模型就直接冲到了X平台的热度总榜——
这回，R2直接把LLM里那套规模继续加、能力继续涨的Scaling逻辑，真正搬进实时世界模型里。
基于统一可扩展的世界模型框架，R2把完整的时空关系压进模型，让场景能够沿着时间持续演化，前后状态保持一致，让这个世界真正「记得住」。
不仅如此，R2还把文字、图像、声音、动作统一进模型，边生成边响应、音画同步，让世界真正「控得动」。
比如下面这个探险世界，用户不仅可以控制方向，还能基于Prompt控制场景角色，而且画面是实时生成的内种：
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/h-YfJ-3Vd1rKuwgsZtbhQA
当然，脑洞完全可以再大一点，比如游戏剧情也能DIY，一句指令就能改变眼前世界，世界剧情真·随意拿捏了：
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/h-YfJ-3Vd1rKuwgsZtbhQA
过去实时世界模型最大的难题之一，就是能力一旦往上堆，速度、稳定性和交互性往往也开始彼此拉扯。
当实时和通用能力同时成立，世界模型的能力边界和使用边界也会一起外扩，逐渐进入游戏、虚拟交互等场景。
一种新的数字世界底座，这回，开始有了成形的可能。
从Scaling到能力预算，实时世界模型连撞两堵工程墙
说实话，还真不能怪实时世界模型这么多年一直卡在能力增长这件事上。
主要在于，实时世界模型想把能力继续往上做，前面先横着技术工程上的两道「硬门槛」。
其中第一道门槛，便是整个视觉世界建模都绕不开的一道表征难题：「信息」到底该怎么被统一表示和建模？
虽同样都隶属模型大类，世界模型在这件事上的先天条件，其实真没LLM那么友好。。。
LLM里的第二个L，就是Language（语言）。
好巧不巧的是，语言其实在信息形态上天然就占了便宜，因为它可以被压缩成一套离散、序列化的符号系统。
在这套体系下，每个Token都是边界清晰的语义单元，海量文本都可以被统一成有限符号的排列组合，训练任务也被高度归一为「预测下一个Token」。
于是，数据、参数和算力都能沿着同一套框架持续扩展，资源投入也更容易稳定转化为能力增长，这正是LLM能够充分释放Scaling潜力的底层前提。
但扎心的是，到了世界模型这里，这套逻辑就没那么顺了。（doge）
因为图像和视频是一种连续、高维且高度冗余的信息形态，色彩、光影连续变化，单个画面就包含海量视觉变量，相邻像素和视频帧之间又存在大量重复。
此外，模型还得从这些原始信号中进一步抽取语义、状态变化乃至物理关系，信息结构远比文本复杂。
也因此，视觉领域长期缺少一套像文本Token那样紧凑、统一、可持续扩展的表征体系，视频模型想沿着同一条路径持续增长，天然要难得多。
当然了，这还只是第一层难题。
因为一旦再加上实时两个字，难度还会再高一档，这也是实时世界模型面对的第二层门槛：
模型容量和实时计算预算天然互相拉扯。
想维持稳定实时生成，每一帧留给模型的计算窗口可能只有几十毫秒，可世界模型想理解更多场景、更复杂的物理关系和更长程的时空变化，又需要更大的模型容量、更复杂的建模，以及更多计算。
这也解释了为什么，过去世界模型的扩展更多停留在局部能力上——
画质、时长、场景各自往前猛堆，却很难汇成一条稳定、统一的增长曲线。
这个两难问题，甚至早已被头部模型反复验证。
2024年，Google DeepMind 11B参数的Genie已经能生成可交互环境，但到了Genie 2，场景和物理能力继续增强，实时性却更难兼顾，想跑到实时往往需要以蒸馏为代价，同时还要牺牲部分画质。
换句话说，对实时世界模型而言，真正难的从来都不是单独把模型做大，或者单独把速度做快，而是让通用能力和实时运行能够同时成立。
△Google DeepMind Genie 2报告
PixVerse R2：实时世界模型终于有了自己的增长曲线
所以说到这儿，实时世界模型碰到的难题就很清楚了。
想把实时性和通用能力一起做上去，先得解决一个底层问题——更多数据、任务和交互信号，怎么持续进入同一套能力体系。
前面我们说过，LLM能够持续Scaling，一个重要前提，就是语言本身拥有相对统一的Token表示和序列建模方式。
但对于实时世界模型来说，模型面对的不只有视觉，还包括动作、音频、长短不一的时间尺度，以及不断进入的各种控制信号！！
这些信息的数据形态、时间粒度和作用方式都不一样，想让这些能力继续一起增长，首先就得把它们收进一条统一的建模主线里。
而PixVerse R2这次做的一件关键的事——
便是把视觉、动作、音频、时序以及不同控制信号，放进同一套可持续扩展的因果建模框架。
需要提一嘴的是，这里的Scaling可不单单指的是模型大小，还包括世界复杂度、控制力，以及怎么稳定运行～
更关键的是，当这些原本异构的信号开始被放进同一种表示体系里，复杂动态的世界也就有机会拥有一套类似语言Token的统一计算坐标系。
而这触及的也是Scaling最底层的问题——
新增的数据、任务和交互经验，能不能持续沉淀进同一个能力体系，并形成复利。
具体来说，R2把Scaling拆成了模型、数据、任务、控制信号和时间尺度五个彼此「协同增长」的维度。
模型规模决定容量，数据拓宽世界分布，任务强化跨场景迁移，控制信号增加交互精度，时间尺度则决定模型能把多长、多复杂的动态过程纳入建模。
任意一个维度增加资源，都能反过来增益其他维度，模型的整体能力就会上涨，不依赖单纯扩大参数量。
这也就意味着R2真正扩展的，已经开始从参数规模进入世界状态空间本身。
其实传统Scaling走到后期，一个越来越现实的问题，就是资源继续往上堆积，能力增益却未必还能同比例增长，新增算力和数据的边际收益开始变薄。
反观R2做的事情，更像是在世界模型身上重做投入产出逻辑，让每一份新增资源都拥有更多能力出口，最终更充分地沉淀为整体模型能力。
落到咱用户真实体验上，就是生成质量更高、长程一致性更稳、跨场景泛化更强，多模态控制也更细～
当然了，多说无益，这实时世界模型R2到底能不能打，我们直接看实际效果～
先插一句，这次R2相比上一代R1，能玩的东西明显更多了。
就比如我们不仅能在赛博世界中玩耍，甚至还能体验互动影游和实时数字人。
先来个小试牛刀，前阵子刚看完《奥德赛》，于是我索性一头扎进了一个奥德赛草原风格的世界里，现场勇闯一下：
真别说，多少有点玩家、导演、编剧三权合一内味儿了～（doge）
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/h-YfJ-3Vd1rKuwgsZtbhQA
WASD一按，视角和方向随便转动，Prompt一敲，角色动作、剧情走向也能直接改，可控性确实不错。
最重要的是，实际体验下来，几乎没有卡顿和延时问题，实际在场感确实强，实时性也确实丝滑。
接下来我们再上一波难度，直接玩一把互动影游，体验一把在魔法学院里魔法大乱斗：
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/h-YfJ-3Vd1rKuwgsZtbhQA
说实话，光看画面，还真有种穿越哈利波特电影里的感觉，确实蛮有大片感，画面质量过关～
但我最想说的，还不是画质，大家有没有发现，在这个互动影游里，眼前的世界是可以被你临时改写的。
比如直接在Prompt框里输入想使出的攻击魔法，下一秒画面就会顺着你的指令继续往下演，确实有点爽。。。
一段内容生成出来，实时性、画面、交互、记忆这些能力都能同时在线。
省下来的时间和精力，终于可以花在一件更重要的事上——到底想创造一个什么样的世界。
能力先拉满，实时再追回来
当然，问题也来了，R2到底是如何做到「实时」和「通用」能力既要又要的？
核心的答案，其实藏在其对底层技术路径的重新拆分上。
过去行业做实时生成底层技术设计，其实大多是在一笔固定的计算预算里「做减法」。
帧率和延迟一旦锁定，单帧算力预算也基本见顶。行业往往只能靠缩模型、减采样、压计算，把重模型塞进毫秒级窗口，生成质量、复杂运动和长程一致性也会随之受损。
但R2的一个关键技术设计思路是：让能力和实时分头强化。
先把基础模型的能力上限做高，再解决实时化，这样实时世界模型的天花板就不会过早被单帧计算预算锁死，而更多取决于底层模型本身能学到多少世界规律。
这也是R2整个技术体系里，Omni Causal AR和Real-Time Acceleration两层架构真正的分工，前者管能力上限，后者管实时性。
对于想持续Scaling的实时世界模型来说，一大难题在于模态、控制信号和时间尺度越加越多，建模很容易越做越碎。
所以第一步，Omni Causal AR先把短视频、长视频、多模态参考、音频和Action控制，统一进一套因果自回归框架——
通过动态Chunk适配不同时间尺度，再用Hybrid Teacher/Diffusion Forcing、多时间尺度记忆和Error Bank解决长程生成中的误差累积、角色漂移和状态断裂问题。
这样一来，新增数据、任务、控制信号和模型规模，都可以持续转化为更强的世界建模能力～
这边能力先做高之后，Real-Time Acceleration再接手第二道题——
把这套通用能力直接蒸馏进实时加速层。
持续预训练后，Omni Causal AR先把生成质量、长程状态和因果能力做扎实，再作为Teacher和Student共同的能力底座，让后续蒸馏尽可能沿用同一套世界理解逻辑，把这套能力更完整地压进实时预算里。
先造大脑，再给大脑做实时加速器，实时世界模型，这事儿成了。
说实话，爱诗能把实时世界模型在行业里率先跑出来，算不上太偶然。
长期面对亿级用户，意味着这家公司面对的一直都是真实世界里最难处理的那部分：
需求高度分散、场景持续变化、长尾永远收不完，模型每天都在被用户用各种意想不到的方式重新「考试」。
而世界模型最终要面对的，恰恰也是同一类问题：如何在一个持续变化、充满噪声、随时会被外部输入打断的环境里，维持状态、理解变化，并继续推演下一刻。
R2这种先放大能力、再单独解决实时效率的路线，也更像是长期产品实践和技术积累自然形成的一种架构选择。
当然了，更值得注意的是，这套架构一旦成立，它的外溢价值就很难只停留在视频生成层面。
在未来，内容生产、具身智能、虚拟人、游戏实时渲染，都可能逐渐汇向同一种底层能力：
持续理解环境、维持状态，并根据外部输入实时生成下一瞬间。
甚至在互动式娱乐市场这个生态场景里，这种变化可能会更明显。
剧情、场景和角色不再只是预先写好的固定内容，其会逐渐变成可以随着用户行为持续展开、持续变化的动态系统。
到那时创作者需要亲自定义的，也许会越来越少是某一帧、某一段资产，而越来越多地转向一个世界如何运转、角色如何行动，以及规则本身。
由此，互动娱乐真正进入的，可能是一个「内容不再被完成」的时代。
我们不再只是观看故事、操控角色、通关世界。
我们开始真正生活在一个会回应你、记住你，并因为你的存在而改变的数字世界里。

title: 斑马智能发布端模型AutoOmni2.0，让元神AI更懂“我的世界”

斑马智能发布端模型AutoOmni2.0，让元神AI更懂“我的世界”
9月23日云栖大会期间，斑马智能发布新一代全模态端侧大模型AutoOmni 2.0-23B-A3B
9月23日云栖大会期间，斑马智能发布新一代全模态端侧大模型AutoOmni 2.0-23B-A3B，任务处理能力堪比10倍参数量级的云模型；基于让AI更懂“我的世界”，亮相全新AutoClaw2.0智舱协作服务实车方案。
“端智能的核心价值是开启交互新范式。”斑马智能联席CEO郝飞表示，基于端模型的全车全时免唤醒，以及上下文和记忆，是新范式的关键要素，让更加懂我的主动服务成为可能。
智驾要懂“物理世界”，智舱要懂“我的世界”
在云栖大会斑马智能展台上，腾势Z9GT、智己LS6、神行者8、红旗天工06的智驾分别是天神之眼、Momenta、华为乾崑和卓驭，但在智舱领域都选择了斑马智能元神AI。据悉，元神AI实现了对主流车企68%的服务覆盖。
“AI上车不代表赢得用户，深度使用才是真正的战场。”斑马智能首席产品官蔡明表示，AI进行复杂规划、再有效组织各方能力的前提，是对用户的理解。一方面，AI要理解物理空间、规律和轨迹构成的“表世界”；另一方面，要理解个人意图、偏好和生活场景构成的“里世界”，进而在感知、理解、执行与反馈的循环中持续进化。
据蔡明介绍，元神AI正从智舱AI迈向Personal AI，形成了“三个连通”：连通云端与车端的算力和服务；连通用户的多个终端，打通全时空场景数据；连通用户与服务，实现跨App、跨终端的服务整合。
AI数据终端公司YoooClaw创始人、CEO肖睿哲表示，联合斑马智能，在数据合规的前提下，让用户在车内1小时、车外23小时的“上下文”打通，真正发挥数据和智能的价值。
在斑马智能展台上，全新AutoClaw 2.0实车方案，以及联合YoooClaw打造的全新生态智能体实车方案，已经让“三个连通”初步落地上车。
智能汽车是具身智能最大的“中试场”
论坛上，斑马智能正式发布全模态端侧大模型AutoOmni 2.0-23B-A3B。该模型采用MoE混合专家模型架构，在智能座舱场景，普通任务能力堪比10倍参数量云模型，复杂任务处理能力相当于10倍参数量云模型的80%-90%。云栖大会现场展示了采用该模型和端云一体Agent架构的实车方案，基于模糊意图、多任务的复杂导航、车控、多媒体，以及跨域任务，AutoOmni2.0都能够低时延、保隐私、稳定流畅地执行。
AutoOmni是斑马智能行业首发的全模态端侧大模型，一年时间，端模型上车的企业中，63%选择了斑马智能。
“把端模型刻在芯上，把安全刻在心上。”斑马智能首席技术官司罗表示，AutoOmni已经合作国内外10家芯片企业，软硬协同支持8路以上多任务稳定并发，大模型推理加速5-6倍，量化保真度超过99%，少占用运行内存50%以上；而车规级端侧AI安全纵深防御体系，不止做到隐私保护和数据合规，还能够兼顾安全和性能开销。
司罗现场演示了全车全时免唤醒、主动智能迎宾、无感智能停车付费等端侧智能场景。从数十项主动智能场景开始，AutoOmni开启AI原生车主动智能新范式。
“智能汽车是具身智能最大的中试场和规模化压测平台。”司罗强调，斑马智能正从AutoOmni向EdgeOmni演进，围绕用户，从单体智能向群体智能拓展，让AI终端更懂“我的世界”。

title: 汇智智能发布Hellome：国内首个FDE直连智能体服务平台，把AI交付周期压进“周”
content:
汇智智能发布Hellome：国内首个FDE直连智能体服务平台，把AI交付周期压进“周”
企业AI服务迎来平台化交付时代
近日，南京人工智能企业汇智智能正式发布一站式AI服务平台Hellome——国内首个实现FDE（前沿部署工程师）与企业客户直接对接的应用智能体服务平台。客户在这个平台上下达智能化需求，由平台认证的FDE承接，依托统一的智能体工具完成方案设计、部署与上线，将AI落地周期压缩至周级。
需求爆发，通路补齐
大模型能力快速迭代的这两年，客户的需求同步爆发。写公文、做报表、盯舆情、管生产，每个组织都有一批“琐碎但重要”的业务等待AI化；真正的堵点不在模型，而在交付：通用AI产品无法贴合具体业务流程，传统定制项目报价高、周期以季度计，多数单位又不具备自建AI团队的条件。Hellome补上的，正是这条可规模化、可预期的交付通路。
把交付环节平台化
Hellome的解法，是把交付环节本身“平台化”。客户发布需求后，经过认证的FDE承接项目，依托汇智自研的桌面智能体Hzhermes开展工作——它直接运行在本地的电脑环境中，可操作本地软件、处理文档表格、调用浏览器与搜索等数十种工具，是一份可配置的“数字劳动力”。从需求梳理、方案设计到部署上线和后续迭代，由同一位FDE负责到底，服务过程不走转包。客户既可以先使用FDE封装好的成熟智能体，也可以随时提出定制化改造，让智能体在持续使用中越来越贴合自身业务。
与传统软件外包或标准品售卖相比，这套模式有两个关键不同。其一，智能体的开发者与后续服务者是同一个人，需求变更时响应链路更短，服务责任清晰；其二，FDE在项目中调通的方案会沉淀为平台上的“技能包”，覆盖公文写作、数据分析、舆情监测、内容创作等数十个常见场景，后续客户可直接启用，交付成本随案例积累递减。
平台的能力在发布之时已经就绪：公文写作、数据分析、舆情简报、直播脚本、短视频创作、小说写作、招聘求职等数十个场景的智能体已在平台上架，客户按需选用即可，无需从零沟通需求；对有个性化诉求的客户，FDE在既有资产上做增量改造，交付以天计而非以月计。
供给侧聚拢同步推进
Hellome上线的同时，汇智智能启动“FDE百万激励计划”，从三个方向降低工程师的入驻与成长门槛：现金激励缓解冷启动期的收入压力，流量扶持把平台需求精准导给认证FDE，技能认证为工程师建立可累积的职业信用。如今，每天都有大量AI工程师入驻平台，一个稳定的交付者网络正在Hellome上快速成形。
汇智智能的智能体服务已覆盖政企、文旅、电商、制造、金融、教育等50余个行业、超过1万家企业客户，并触达千万级个人用户；其“服务＋引擎＋算力”产品体系中的Agentsyun词元工场聚合200余个大模型，为平台交付提供模型调度支持。按照规划，未来三年Hellome将聚集10万名FDE，一张覆盖千行百业的AI交付网络正在加速成形——客户的智能化诉求，从此有了确定性极强的落地路径。

title: 稚晖君把机器人卖到2万元一台，可人可狗可开发！
content:
稚晖君把机器人卖到2万元一台，可人可狗可开发！
两万元，买到的是怎样一个机器人
henry 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
公司名字还叫上纬新材料科技股份有限公司，但发布会上，它已经开始卖机器人了。
去年最后一天，上纬新材董事长、稚晖君（彭志辉）首次公开发布个人机器人Q1。
9个月后，Q1终于正式开售，同时亮相的还有另一款能变形的机器人T1。
其中，Q1主打“可创造”，用户可以自己改外观、编动作、设计机器人的性格。T1则主打“随行”，支持在人形和四足形态之间切换，从家中陪伴到户外移动。
两款机器人均为19999元起，比1TB版本的苹果折叠屏手机iPhone Duo还便宜了1500块。
这个价格，也让人形机器人进入了高端消费电子的价格区间。
那么，你的下一台数码3C，会是一台机器人吗？
两万元，买到的是怎样一个机器人
在外观上，Q1为客制化提供了较高自由度。
除了官方提供的白、灰、粉三种配色外，用户还可以通过3D打印定制外壳，改变机器人的外观。
作为一款具身智能产品，Q1也支持用户设计互动动作，调整它的性格、语气和音色。
也就是说，同一款机器人，经过不同用户改造后，可以拥有完全不同的形态和互动方式。
在使用场景上，Q1覆盖家庭陪伴和教育。
日常，它可以通过语音和动作与用户互动；在编程和机器人教学中，用户也可以围绕它编排动作、设计互动，让代码和指令转化为真实世界中的机器人行为。
硬件方面，Q1采用启元自研QDD准直驱关节和全身力控方案。
其中，QDD关节采用高度集成化设计，体积约鸡蛋大小；全身力控则让机器人能够感知外部力量，并根据受力情况调整动作。
对于需要长期与人互动的机器人来说，关节如何输出力量、被推拉后如何恢复，都直接影响实际体验。
如果用户希望进一步开发，Q1还提供探索版，售价26999元，开放软件开发套件SDK、硬件开发套件HDK以及硬件扩展接口。
而另一款产品T1，则把重点放在了“陪伴移动”。
它最有辨识度的设计，是支持轮足人形与四足两种形态切换，让机器人可以根据不同场景改变移动方式，多少有些小时候“变形金刚”的意思。
在功能上，T1主要面向室内外跟随、家庭互动和拍摄辅助等场景。
在家里，它可以参与外语启蒙和日常陪伴；带出门后，则可以通过智能跟随、轨迹运镜等功能辅助拍摄，让“跟着你走”进一步延伸成“帮你拍”。
相比Q1强调“创造一个属于自己的机器人”，T1更关注的是机器人如何进入用户的日常移动场景。
同样的，T1也有基础版和Pro版两个版本，前者19999元，后者29999元。
其中，T1 Pro增加英伟达Orin Nano算力芯片，支持双形态360°全向避障，并加入低电量自动回充、语音召唤、跟随载物等能力，同时开放二次开发接口。
可以说，能变形的T1，把四足机器人的随行玩法和人形机器人的互动体验，放进了同一台机器里。
两款产品的侧重点也由此显现：Q1更强调动手改造和个性化创作；T1则侧重室内外随行，让机器人更多参与日常移动和互动。
除了硬件，启元还围绕外观创作和技能拓展，搭建了三个平台：
- PrimeFLOW负责机器人外观设计，让用户生成、编辑和输出自己的造型；
- PrimeHub元创工坊面向开发者，支持创作、发布和分享机器人技能；
- PrimeStore则是技能商店，让用户获取和使用更多技能。
这种二次开发友好的设计，也让机器人不再只是一次性交付的硬件产品，而更像一个可以持续更新的平台。
毕竟，如果一台机器人只能反复展示出厂时预设的几个动作，新鲜感过去，很可能就会变成家里的“摆件”。
正如稚晖君此前所说：
对我来说，机器人最有意思的地方不是它出厂时是什么样子，而是它还能被你变成什么样子。
当用户可以不断创造新动作、开发新技能，也能使用其他人分享的玩法，机器人就有机会随着内容积累，在一次次更新中找到持续使用的理由。
而这，也是启元希望探索的一条路径：
机器人不只是一个硬件，而是一个由用户、开发者共同参与构建的开放平台。
不过，玩法丰富之后，另一个问题也随之而来：
机器人能陪伴、能互动，但它能替你干活吗？
买回家的机器人，一定要帮你做家务吗？
这次发布会上，启元给Q1和T1确定了同一个定位——
简单来说，它面向的不是工厂生产线，也不是实验室验证，而是进入普通人的日常生活：陪伴、互动、随行，以及由用户自己改造。
当然，科研和开发用途仍然被保留。Q1探索版开放SDK、HDK和硬件扩展接口，方便开发者进一步开发。
但对于普通消费者来说，更现实的问题是：买回家之后，为什么还会持续使用？
这个问题，也是当前消费级机器人共同面对的挑战。
无论是官方首发预订价399美元，预售卖出1.5万台断货的机械鸭Microduck、还是国内松延的Bumi，维他动力的大头BoBo。
这些产品都在尝试回答同一个问题：当机器人进入家庭后，除了完成固定任务，它还能提供什么长期价值？
目前看下来，便宜、可爱、好玩、可开发可能是这类产品的共性。
相较之下，启元给出答案，是把创造和互动放在更核心的位置。
Q1把外观、动作、性格和音色定制作为主要卖点，强调“把机器人变成自己的”；T1则通过人形与四足切换，探索更多室内外随行场景。
但“个人机器人”并不等于“家务机器人”。
个人，强调的是机器人围绕使用者提供互动和服务；家庭，描述的是使用环境；家务，则对应清洁、整理等具体任务。
一台扫地机器人既是家庭机器人，也能完成家务；但一台陪伴机器人进入家庭，并不意味着它会洗碗、叠衣服。
事实上，启元也在推进家务方向。
本次发布会上，公司提到面向家庭场景打造的家务基座大模型PrimeMind，但这一方向仍处于研发探索阶段，不能等同于现售Q1、T1已经具备通用家务能力。
田华给出的路线是：
“先从‘有趣’起步，让机器人逐步走向‘有用’。”
对于今天准备购买一台两万元机器人的用户来说，最终决定购买的，仍然是当下能够获得的体验：
这些互动、创作和随行功能，能否让机器人度过新鲜期之后，依然留在生活里。
从收购到开售，上纬新材的机器人转型走到哪了
对关注上纬新材的人来说，这场发布会也接上了去年的另一个热门话题：智元系入主一家材料上市公司之后，究竟准备做什么？
2025年，智元恒岳通过协议转让及后续要约收购入主上纬新材，公司实际控制人变更为智元实控人——邓泰华。
同年11月25日，彭志辉当选上纬新材董事长。
于是，在智元机器人联合创始人、总裁、CTO之外，稚晖君又多了一个上市公司董事长的身份。
从去年底Q1首次亮相，到今年CES展示Q1、T1，再到开放预订、正式销售，上纬的机器人业务开始从概念走向具体产品。
围绕机器人硬件，创作平台、技能社区和应用商店也被纳入布局。
从上市公司业务结构来看，上纬原有主营仍包括耐腐蚀材料、风电叶片用材料等，同时开始发展消费级机器人新业务。
根据上纬新材半年报，今年上半年，公司机器人研发投入约1.64亿元，占整体研发投入九成左右；截至6月底，相关研发团队达到180人。
同期，公司实现营收约8.03亿元，机器人业务尚未产生营业收入；公司归母净亏损约1.67亿元，研发投入增加是业绩下降的原因之一。
从去年收购引发关注，到今年产品正式开售，上纬的机器人故事，已经有了可以被购买和体验的实物。
而对于稚晖君来说，从做出机器人，到让机器人真正走进普通人的生活，才是下一阶段更大的挑战。

content:
联想亮相阿里云栖大会：联想天禧AI把超级组织落地到端侧
联想天禧AI携全场景多端产品矩阵亮相阿里云栖大会
9月22日至24日，2026云栖大会在杭州国际博览中心举行。本届大会以”智以致用”为主题，联想天禧AI携全场景多端产品矩阵亮相，展台前观众络绎不绝，纷纷驻足体验”超能搭档”的魅力——从AI PC到AI手机、AI平板，跨端接力、语音对话、任务执行的无缝体验，让现场沉浸式感受到个人AI时代的真实温度。
从”团队”到”人+Agent”：组织的最小生产单元正在改写
联想天禧AI战略生态部负责人刘琳琳受邀出席Qoder分论坛，发表《端侧AI新范式：超级智能体落地与共创》主题演讲。围绕”Qoder助力超级组织”的论坛主题，刘琳琳从终端厂商的视角给出回答：超级组织最终会落在每个人手边的那台设备上。
AI时代，组织最大的成本不再是人力，而是协作本身。当个体产能被AI抬高一个数量级后，等待就成了唯一的瓶颈，最小生产单元也随之从团队变成”人+Agent”：人对目标负责，Agent对路径负责。联想内部的真实实践印证了这一模式：3个人、30天、零场例会，跑通了一款产品从设计到发布的全流程。
这一组织模型里，AI主机扮演着关键角色。笔记本关机、人下班，Agent的工作也就停了——这是超级组织的硬瓶颈。AI主机7×24小时在线，长耗时、高算力的任务交给它，第二天回来看结果。联想内部直接把AI主机定义为”AI执行团队”：如果说”一个人+一组Agent”是组织形态，AI主机就是这组Agent的办公室。
行业走向：比拼”人+Agent”组织方式的时代已经开始
把视野放大到整个行业，五个变化正在发生：模型趋同，Harness越来越重要，壁垒转向上下文、编排、验证与安全的工程化能力；最小单元是”人+一组Agent”，编制思维从”多少人”变成”每人驾驭多少Agent”；Agent会成为软件的第一用户，接口从GUI转向MCP、Skill、CLI；终端是超级组织的最后一公里，端云不是过渡形态，而是长期均衡；信任基础设施决定放权上限，身份、权限、审批、审计、回滚，决定企业敢把多大的事交给Agent。”比拼模型的时代在结束，比拼’人+Agent’组织方式的时代在开始，”刘琳琳表示，”下一轮拉开差距的，不是谁的模型更强，而是谁先把’人+Agent’的组织方式跑通。”
超能模式落地，生态共建提速：天禧AI 4.3让”超级组织”触手可及
从理念到实践，演讲中描绘的”超级组织”图景，在天禧AI 4.3上已变成可感知的日常体验。本次升级以”超能模式”为核心：多端入口统一、数据贯通，任务执行流程清晰可见，是”第一眼就舒服”的视觉焕新；自研全双工自然语音对话，随时打断、不抢话、精准收音，是”一开口就自然”的交互进化；首发Tianxi AgentCore端侧智能体框架，自主规划任务、执行并生成结果，支持手机、平板远程操控电脑，全程数据不出本地，是”一交代就办妥”的能力跃迁。同时，天禧AI也联合了阿里Qoder，共同提升用户体验。
产品能力的背后是天禧生态的持续繁荣。天禧生态软件矩阵月活2.8亿、年分发量40亿次，AI生态内容累计3.9万，覆盖AI PC、AI手机、AI平板、AIoT全场景。这些数字还在持续增长。面向开发者，”苍穹计划”以万亿Token、曝光位和激励基金降低创新门槛；面向内容提供方、能力共建方与战略合作联盟，联想以”总指挥、总入口、总调度”的角色全面开放——端云决策不用自己维护复杂规则，一次接入多端分发，垂类场景和应用创新留给开发者。
联想天禧AI在云栖大会的亮相，不仅是一次产品及解决方案的展示，更是联想”混合式AI”战略在端侧落地的一次系统性宣言。在Agentic AI之年，当行业还在讨论模型参数与算力竞赛时，天禧AI以”端边云协同”为技术底座、以“端侧优势”为产品抓手、以”苍穹计划”为生态纽带，给出了”超级组织如何真正落地”的答案。超级组织不是更大的团队，而是无数个超级个体的高效连接，而每一个超级个体，先要落在一台可以信任、可以托付的终端上。未来，联想天禧AI将持续深耕端侧AI，与开发者和产业伙伴一道，把”人+Agent”的超级组织，先在终端跑通。

title: 让Token生产更高效：异构混推的关键技术演进与创新实践
content:
让Token生产更高效：异构混推的关键技术演进与创新实践
商汤大装置异构混推创新实践与技术演进
Token经济加速爆发，算力需求发生结构性反转，推理需求已取代训练，成为算力增长主引擎。
随之而来的，是AI基础设施面临的全新命题与挑战：当Token调用量迈向千倍级增长，推理系统如何承接持续攀升的需求？如何通过异构算力实现高效、稳定的Token生产？
在近日举办的“2026全球AI芯片峰会·Token工厂异构混训混推技术研讨会”上，商汤大装置资深技术专家罗伟以《Token工厂：以异构算力构建新一代Al基础设施》为主题发表演讲，深入剖析规模化推理面临的系统挑战，并分享商汤大装置在异构推理架构、模型适配及关键技术演进等方面的实践与探索。
01行业挑战：Agent时代，推理负载瓶颈贯穿整套系统
Agent时代的负载特征，和传统单轮对话的推理需求有明显不同。
首先是长上下文，带来了输入计算和KV Cache占用的持续增长；其次是连续多轮的对话，意味着前缀复用和热点不断变化；再者是突发与长尾需求多，意味着流量和长度的分布会持续波动。
罗伟表示，面对这些变化，商汤大装置的底层逻辑已经转向“以Token、状态与时延预算为中心”，所有设计都围绕Token的生产效率、交付质量与单位成本，进行资源的组织和利用。
这一以Token为中心的系统设计，也支撑商汤大装置持续提升规模化Token生产与服务能力。如今，商汤大装置的日均Token服务量，已经从年初2月的0.46万亿，增长至8月4.5万亿。
02创新实践：横向串资源、纵向拉效率，系统级提高Token产能
如何把单点效率组织成系统级Token产能？罗伟分享了商汤大装置的两条主线：“横向编排”与“纵向优化”。两条主线最终指向共同目标：模型质量达标、SLO达标、有效吞吐提升、单位产能成本下降。
横向串资源：让不同算力各展所长
所谓“横向编排”，目的是资源协同，让平台知道哪些模型、哪些版本能运行在哪些算力上，哪些Prefill与Decode组合能做KV Cache交接，当前请求应该进入哪条路径，负载变化时如何自动调整。
针对不同品牌、不同规格的算力，商汤大装置构建了统一的资源画像，覆盖计算吞吐、KV Cache的容量、有效带宽、模型兼容性等，让不同算力进入同一个编排视角。
在此基础上，平台对推理请求进行全生命周期管控。从准入配对、Prefill执行、KV Cache状态交接，到Decode接管，每一个环节都有标准化的协同机制，保障服务稳定性。
“我们不会把某一类芯片永久固定为P节点或D节点。”罗伟强调，平台会根据模型、批量、上下文长度的瓶颈变化，动态调整不同芯片的角色分工，实现更高的可用性、灵活的组合和配比。
纵向拉效率：让整条路径性能最大化
在横向打通资源的同时，商汤大装置持续深化“模型×引擎×芯片”三层纵向优化，从模型适配到芯片运行时，充分释放整条执行路径的性能。
其中，在模型层，针对权重量化、显存预算进行精细化调优，平衡精度与吞吐；在引擎层，针对Attention、GEMM等核心算子进行并行优化；在芯片层，深度适配编译、访存调度与内存管理。而所有优化结果都会在真实负载中进行系统验证，规避单点效率的瓶颈。
03技术演进：从动态池化到模块拆分，持续提升Token生产效率
在成熟实践的基础上，罗伟进一步分享了异构协同走向更高效率、更高灵活性的两大关键技术演进方向。
技术演进方向一：从固定P/D到动态资源池
在资源调度层面，商汤大装置正在从固定P/D配比走向动态资源池化。不同业务、不同时间段的输入输出长度和流量热点不断变化，静态P/D组合容易造成局部排队和资源错配。
为此，商汤大装置分别构建Prefill Pool和Decode Pool，根据实时负载、KV Cache状态及节点健康度，动态完成请求路由和P/D资源匹配。当长输入导致Prefill压力升高时，系统可动态增加P节点；当长输出推高Decode负载时，则增加D节点，甚至通过角色切换实现P/D节点灵活转换，让资源跟着负载动态调整，在保障SLA的同时提升整体算力利用效率。
技术演进方向二：从P/D走向模块级资源池
面向未来多模态、MoE模型的发展，传统按P/D两阶段划分资源的方式将显现瓶颈。商汤大装置的架构演进方向，是进一步走向模块级资源池化：将Encoder、Attention、FFN、视觉编码等不同模块拆分为独立资源池，各自按负载特点弹性扩缩容，让资源匹配更精准、利用率更高。
演讲最后，罗伟表示，面向未来，作为“最懂大模型的AI基础设施”，商汤大装置将持续推动产品与技术迭代，与生态伙伴共同加速AI基础设施持续升级，推动普惠AI，智造美好未来。

title: 达卯科技完成新一轮融资，算电协同核心软件层“稀缺标的”
content:
达卯科技完成新一轮融资，算电协同核心软件层“稀缺标的”
打造算电协同领域“Windows”级操作系统
算电协同AI能源运营操作系统核心企业达卯科技，近期据悉已完成约2亿元新一轮融资。去年10月，达卯科技完成由宁德时代旗下溥泉资本领投的近亿元A+轮融资。
达卯科技成立于2021年，总部位于上海徐汇模速空间，是国内首家将能源大模型规模化落地算电协同、虚拟电厂与泛能源场景的AI企业，也是算电协同赛道的先行者。公司核心依托自研垂类能源大模型与AI智能体集群，打造算电协同平台、AI虚拟电厂平台、智能运维平台等产品矩阵，面向智算中心客户提供从咨询规划、投资测算、智能运营、精细化运维、能源增值交易的全生命周期服务。
公司推出的核心产品算电协同2.0平台・AIDC绿电直连能源运营操作系统，是算电协同产业链中的关键软件，已形成面向GW级智算中心绿电直连场景的全周期智慧能源运营闭环能力，核心技术指标处于行业领先水平，推动AIDC从传统“用电负荷”升级为“新型电力系统下可调度、可交易的柔性资源”。
目前，达卯科技股东阵容包含宁德时代、商汤科技、寒武纪等产业链龙头企业，具备优异的产业生态协同与资源聚合能力。
算电协同，系指通过数字化技术、智能算法和通信网络，将算力基础设施与电力系统（发电、输电、配电、用电环节）进行有机整合，实现资源动态匹配与优化配置的基建工程，以提升能源利用效率、保障算力供给稳定性，并推动低碳化发展。2026年初，算电协同首次写入政府工作报告，成为新基建重点方向。今年9月，国务院层面进一步明确提出，推动算电协同、算网融合，加快绿电直连、源网荷储项目落地。这是继多部门出台政策推动AI与能源双向赋能后，国家顶层再次点名绿电直连，将其作为支撑全国一体化算力网络建设的核心抓手，是绿电直连从试点示范走向规模化复制的关键信号。
算力产业的高速扩张持续放大电力供需矛盾，算电协同赛道迎来产业爆发窗口期。业内分析指出，算电协同产业链硬件环节参与者众多，但能够提供完整底层软件、实现算电协同全链路商业化落地的企业寥寥无几。达卯科技是赛道内率先跑通商业化闭环的企业，兼具能源大模型底层技术壁垒与全周期项目运营交付能力，是算电协同产业链软件层为数不多已实现商业落地的稀缺标的。
此前，达卯科技CEO简煜忞曾在媒体采访中表示，达卯科技定位不只是算电协同技术服务商，更是产业核心运营服务商。区别于传统软件售卖模式，达卯采用“技术赋能+运营落地”的商业模式，以价值销售为核心，交付长期能源运营价值，持续为客户挖掘收益提升空间。业务覆盖项目全周期：在智算中心规划阶段可前置介入，完成算电协同方案规划、经济性评估；项目落地阶段部署算电协同软件平台；运营阶段承接能源调度、电力交易与设施运维，并通过运营分成分享降本增值收益。
简煜忞提到，算电协同行业当前处于快速窗口期，政策、技术迭代节奏快，公司会持续投入技术研发与市场拓展，持续抢占赛道先机、夯实竞争壁垒。

title: 阿里千问AI平台全面升级模型服务、Agent服务、AI应用
content:
阿里千问AI平台全面升级模型服务、Agent服务、AI应用
覆盖MaaS、Agent服务、行业AI解决方案
允中 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
9月22日，在2026云栖大会MaaS & Agent技术主论坛上，阿里巴巴集团战略副总裁、ATH事业群MaaS业务线总裁文征宣布千问AI平台全面升级：以推动Agent进入生产作为建设核心，在模型服务基础上新增对Agent服务、行业AI解决方案的支持，并推出了API优速模式、Agent Studio、千问AI座舱解决方案等一系列能力，帮助企业将智能转化为生产力。
从消耗Token到交付结果，AI价值的衡量方式正在改变
文征表示，AI仍处于非常早期的阶段，用户覆盖、场景渗透和算力规模均有巨大增长空间。持续增长的Token用量说明，AI需求已不再是一道需要证明的题，关键在于谁能将智能转化为结果。单任务价值、Token生产效率和单Token能力，共同决定“智能价值密度”。

title: Envision Energy launches next generation offshore wind turbine
content:
Envision Energy has announced its next generation EN-252/16.7 offshore
wind turbine. The turbine is designed to deliver higher energy production,
increased reliability and improved project returns.
The turbine has a rated capacity of 16.7 MW and features a high performance
rotor tailored specifically for the European market. The design incorporates
vertically integrated component technologies, advanced safety and grid
capabilities, and AI powered lifecycle monitoring.
The swept area to power ratio is approximately 2.99 square meters per kilowatt.
For GW offshore wind farms, the turbine can deliver around 1% to 2% higher
annual energy production.
Christian Schrimpf, executive vice president of offshore wind at Envision
Energy, said: "The next phase of offshore wind is not simply about
increasing turbine scale. The real value of scale lies in how effectively
it translates into higher energy production, greater reliability and stronger
economics across the project lifecycle."
The design is based on Envision Energy's proven Model Z platform, which
has more than a decade of offshore operational experience.
Extensive testing has been carried out, including drivetrain system loading
tests and more than 600 hours of accelerated life testing to assess drivetrain
system interactions under challenging operating conditions.

title: Pacifico Energy secure survey license for Nam Trung Bo 3
content:
Pacifico Energy has secured sea survey licence approval for the development
of the 1.3GW Nam Trung Bo 3 offshore wind project.
The approval was granted by Vietnam's Ministry of Agriculture and Environment
and allows Pacifico Energy to carry out technical and environmental studies
to evaluate the approved offshore area.
Preliminary desktop assessments of the site and a detailed survey campaign
will be undertaken in preparation for field activities.
The field programme will include geotechnical and geophysical surveys,
wind measurement, meteorological and oceanographic studies, environmental
baseline surveys, and other technical investigations.
The project, located in Lam Dong Province, was identified in Vietnam's
Adjusted Power Development Plan VIII and is expected to begin commercial
operations between 2031 and 2035.
"It reflects our long-term confidence in Vietnam's offshore wind potential
and our commitment to supporting the country's energy security and sustainable
growth," said Nate Franklin, founder and group chairman of Pacifico
Pacifico Energy emphasised its commitment to supporting Vietnam's growing
electricity demand, with offshore wind expected to play a crucial role
in the country's energy transition.

will support offshore wind operations and maintenance activities located
in the North Sea.
The charter represents the second long-term deployment for Purus Horizon
during its operational life.
The vessel was originally deployed as one of the first generation of offshore
service operation vessels supporting the offshore wind sector.
Purus and Siemens Gamesa will continue their existing relationship through
the new long-term agreement.

title: Van Oord reveals two next generation flexible fall pipe vessels
content:
Van Oord reveals two next generation flexible fall pipe vessels TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Van Oord reveals two next generation flexible fall pipe vessels
Van Oord has unveiled Vindnes and Vestnes, two next-generation flexible
fall pipe vessels.
The vessels are expected to strengthen Van Oord's subsea rock installation
capabilities while supporting offshore wind, interconnector and other critical
infrastructure projects.
Designed from the keel up as dedicated subsea rock installation vessels,
the vessels will enhance safety, operational efficiency, installation performance
and future fuel flexibility, according to Van Oord.
The design aims to maximise productivity while minimising environmental
impact. To achieve this, the vessels balance carrying capacity, installation
rates, fuel efficiency and offshore workability.
Maurits den Broeder, managing director of Offshore Energy at Van Oord,
said: "We are investing not only in additional capacity, but in a
new generation of purpose-built subsea rock installation vessels designed
around productivity, efficiency and sustainability."
He added: "These vessels reflect our confidence in the continued growth
of offshore energy and reinforce Van Oord's commitment to remaining at
the forefront of seabed intervention."
The flexible fall pipe vessels are currently under construction at Yantai
CIMC Raffles Offshore in China, with delivery expected in 2028 and 2029.

title: Australia’s Sicona acquires Advano to expand silicon-carbon battery tech in US – Batteries International
content: Australia-headquartered Sicona Battery Technologies has acquired 100% of New Orleans battery tech company Advano, giving it a US operating based including a pilot manufacturing plant, R&D labs and cell-testing equipment. Sicona confirmed the deal, for an undisclosed sum, on September 16. The announcement came just weeks after Sicona secured a funding boost of up to A$45 million ($31 million) to demonstrate manufacturing of its advanced silicon-carbon battery anode material in Australia. The company plans to install its own SiCx silicon-carbon anode production process at the US plant to support Advano’s existing US customers — and expand the New Orleans operation into what it called a ‘super pilot’ facility to produce enough material for over three million battery cells. The facility will target a wide variety of applications including AI datacentre battery backup systems, robotics, power tools, autonomous systems, drones, electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft and defence. Sicona said the acquisition will solidify its position as one of the leading IP holders in the field of mechanical silicon anode materials and consolidate Advano’s silicon anode patent portfolio. Advano, founded in 2016, has developed a silicon-based anode material designed to increase lithium ion battery energy density and reduce cost per kilowatt hour. The company has raised around $46 million to date. Sicona founder and CEO Christiaan Jordaan said the deal has particular significance, coming as two US laws shift the economics of battery production towards American plants. From October 2027, one law prevents procurement of batteries produced by certain Chinese battery manufacturers while another already pays companies 10% of battery anode material production costs, if made within the US. Jordaan said Sicona will produce anode material inside the US before the 2027 restrictions take effect, which will allow an Australian company to compete for American contracts on price and origin. According to Sicona, its US plans have also been conditionally selected for unspecified congressional appropriations funding. Meanwhile, distinguished energy storage scientist Shirley Meng, most recently chief scientist at the Argonne Collaborative Center for Energy Storage Science, will join Sicona as scientific adviser. Meng said silicon-based anodes have the potential to deliver major improvements in battery energy, power and charging performance, but successful commercialisation depends on materials that can be manufactured safely, economically and at meaningful scale. title: AI Cuts Battery Testing Costs for Manufacturers
content:
Battery Manufacturing
EV Batteries
Automotive & Mobility
European manufacturers EAS Batteries and BMW Group each deploy machine learning models to predict cell performance, cutting development cycles from years to months.
September 23, 2026
6 Min Read
University of Zagreb and BMW researchers implement AI models for optimizing cell production.
BMW Group
At a Glance
EAS Batteries aims to boost cell service life by 10% and production yield by 15% through AI models
BMW Group cut material and time usage by over 50% in individual battery production testing processes
Traditional battery testing takes years as engineers must physically test every parameter set fully
Behind every new EV battery is a manufacturer that has spent years developing and refining its production process. The most costly step in that development cycle is testing. To validate real-world performance, battery engineers need to build new cells with real material and test them thoroughly over weeks or months. Engineers also need to hold onto valuable material and equipment throughout the testing process, which prevents them from developing other cell designs at the same time.
In the past, battery manufacturers could cover these high testing costs with higher prices. However, as
average battery prices have steadily fallen in recent years
, manufacturers have had to lower prices to remain competitive. All battery producers have therefore lost margins, some more than others. To recoup losses, companies are looking for ways to reduce testing costs because they have an outsized impact on overall product development costs.
Related:
$16 Million Prize to Boost US Critical Minerals Workforce
A growing number of battery producers see AI as a promising solution. These companies envision engineers using AI models trained on production and test data to predict how a process change will affect the finished cell before they run a test. With AI tools, engineers could validate the same cell technology with fewer tests and less time than traditional testing.
In recent months,
Battery Technology
has covered AI use in battery production by startups including
QuantumScape
SandboxAQ
as well as major research organizations such as
Honda R&D
. In this piece, we'll explain how AI can help battery engineers and two European manufacturers,
BMW Group
EAS Batteries
, that are leading their own AI projects.
AI’s appeal for battery manufacturers
Before releasing a new battery to market, manufacturers must perfect their production process to create cells with the desired performance consistently. Ordinarily, battery engineers rely on trial and error to find the optimal production settings. They would tweak a setting, like electrode coating, build a real cell, and physically test it. By testing many settings, engineers can gradually identify which production process yields the best cells.
Unfortunately, this testing approach is very costly. Trial-and-error is inherently slower than more efficient methods like predictions or simulations. The production line has many settings, and each setting affects the others, so engineers must test every parameter combination separately. Each test can also involve charging and discharging a cell hundreds of times over months so engineers can determine when the cell degrades. Because of these factors, battery testing often takes years to complete.
Related:
Tapping Battery Compound Production Potential
Close test chamber for eight pouch cells. Credit: Inficon.
To shorten the testing process, many battery engineers use
design of experiments (DOE)
, which is a statistical method that identifies ideal combinations for testing. DOE helps engineers reduce the number of tests, but they still spend time and resources building and physically evaluating each remaining test combination.
AI is a much more promising solution. Manufacturers already have the data AI models need, including coating measurements, defect images, and charging curves for every cell produced. With this data, engineers can train a model and ask it to find and evaluate production setting combinations they have never considered before.
Today’s AI models are more than capable for this application, as evidenced by a
2019 study
in which researchers used machine learning to predict LFP cell cycle life. The only remaining barrier is for battery producers to implement AI in real production environments.
Building a virtual cell at EAS Batteries
In July, a German consortium, led by EAS Batteries,
launched
a project to apply AI to battery production. Called KiBa-Pro, the project aims to combine the efforts of multiple partners to digitalize LFP cell production through June 2029. It’s received 2.4 million euros from the German Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space, and includes universities like Karlsruhe Institute of Technologie, and companies like Omron Europe.
Related:
Trump's Orders Secure Bulk Power System, Critical Minerals
KiBa-Pro targets LFP because
the chemistry is used in more than half of EV batteries and over 90% of energy storage systems
. The project aims to build a virtual LFP cell that battery manufacturers can use to simulate how different production settings affect the finished cell's properties. For example, an engineer can input coating thickness, porosity, throughput, and temperature data into the virtual cell and receive the expected service life and energy capacity.
Diagram of how EAS Batteries will coordinate its partners in KiBa-Pro development. Credit: EAS Batteries.
According to EAS, KiBa-Pro will help manufacturers increase cell service life by at least 10% and production yield by at least 15%. If the project meets those targets, battery producers can significantly reduce wasted material from testing and speed up new cell development.
These benefits are far from a guarantee because the project just started. EAS and its consortium plan to spend the rest of the first year capturing the production process digitally and running reference batches for AI training. Next, they plan to build out the model and validate it in industrial production over two years.
Predicting cell performance at BMW Group
In 2024, BMW Group and the University of Zagreb in Croatia
launched a joint project called Insight to apply AI across battery cell production
. The partners work at BMW's Battery Cell Competence Center (BCCC) in Munich, where BMW Group develops cell chemistry and production processes. Since the project started, researchers at BCCC have been training an AI system on past test data and live production data to predict process parameters and cell performance.
With predictions from the AI systems, engineers can quickly decide whether to shorten a test series or drop it. BMW
that teams using these predictions have cut material and time usage in individual process steps by more than 50%.
With the Insight joint research project, BMW Group and the University of Zagreb develop and implement practical AI models to optimize battery cell production. Credit: BMW Group.
In addition to improving testing, BMW claims that the Insight project can also speed up the final approval step in the battery production process. Typically, after a cell is charged for the first time at the end of production, it needs to be stored at a set temperature for a period of time to allow defects to appear. The company says that because its AI systems can fully analyze the cells for defects in advance, it can eliminate the final storage step.
While the Insight project has yielded promising results, BMW has proven the benefits only in a prototype environment. As the company readies the AI systems for a live production environment, BMW says it will transfer testing to a near-production facility in Parsdorf, Germany.
The Promise of future savings
To date, BMW and its Insight project have reported positive prototype results and are working to scale them into a live production environment. Meanwhile, the EAS-led KiBa-Pro project is currently capturing production data and plans to deliver real results by 2029.
Despite their promise, neither project has shown benefits on a running production line. In addition, neither project was designed to work across multiple factories simultaneously. Because each model is trained on one factory’s equipment and materials, what works at one site may not necessarily work at another. Only when an AI system works universally for any battery producer can companies recover lost margin from falling battery prices and release better batteries sooner.

title: Battery Fire Evacuates 500—New Tech Could Stop the Next One
content:
Stationary Batteries
Testing & Safety
Thermal Management
Battery News
As California firefighters battle thermal runaway across multiple storage systems, researchers are developing VOC monitoring, acoustic detection, and immersion cooling to prevent cascade failures.
September 23, 2026
At a Glance
Thermal runaway spread to second battery system at California water facility, keeping 500 homes evacuated since Tuesday.
Acoustic AI and VOC monitoring systems can detect battery failures minutes before thermal runaway begins, researchers say.
09/24/2026 Update
: According to local reporting, the number of homes under evacuation orders because of the battery fire
is now 500
rather than the 200 we originally reported.
A lithium-ion battery fire at a Metropolitan Water District facility in La Verne, California, has kept approximately 200 homes under evacuation orders since Tuesday, underscoring the persistent safety challenges facing battery energy storage systems (BESS) as they become increasingly critical to grid infrastructure.
The incident
The fire began at 11:40 a.m. on Tuesday, September 22, following a "minor explosion" in one of two battery storage systems located at the Wheeler Avenue facility, which houses the Weymouth Water Treatment Plant, according to the
Los Angeles Times
. The battery energy storage system was positioned near a solar panel field on the northeast side of the facility.
Fire crews arrived to find flames in a battery storage unit, and the situation quickly escalated. By Tuesday evening, firefighters determined that an adjacent second battery storage system had also suffered damage, with battery packs entering thermal runaway—a self-sustaining chemical reaction triggered by excessive heat that can spread rapidly to neighboring batteries.
Related:
Fail-Safe BESS Technology Prevents Thermal Runaway at Single-Cell Level
One civilian was injured at the outset and transported to a hospital,
CBS Los Angeles reported
. Grace Miller Elementary School, located less than half a mile from the facility, remained closed Wednesday as a precautionary measure.
The cause of the fire remains unknown and is under investigation.
The challenge of lithium-ion battery fires
La Verne Fire Chief Brandon Coatney reiterated the unique difficulties these fires present. Once thermal runaway begins, the process cannot be stopped, and batteries will burn for hours—or in cases involving multiple battery systems, for days. The fires release toxic gases including hydrogen fluoride, hydrogen chloride, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide,
the Los Angeles Times reported
. (You can find a detailed explanation of thermal runaway and its causes here: "
What Is Thermal Runaway? Here’s a Battery of Answers
"Later in the day, we were able to get that first battery storage system to a relatively stable point, to where it was not putting off any hazardous plume and the heat signature had gone down quite a bit," Coatney said at a Wednesday morning news conference.
Ernie Hernandez of the L.A. County Fire Department's hazardous materials team reported that air quality monitoring had not detected hazardous battery components in the vapor, though evacuation orders remained in place for homes immediately surrounding the facility as crews worked to cool the batteries with water.
Related:
How AI is Driving the Fastest Shift in Stationary Battery Applications in Decades
Prevention and detection technologies
The La Verne incident highlights why battery safety research has become increasingly urgent as BESS installations proliferate across the country. Several emerging technologies aim to prevent such fires or detect problems before they escalate.
Early warning systems
Metis Engineering's Cell Guard technology represents one approach to early detection. The system
monitors volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that batteries emit before failure
, providing crucial minutes to prevent thermal runaway from developing. This early detection capability could prove vital in facilities like the one in La Verne, where adjacent battery systems can be affected by a single unit's failure.
Thermal runaway induced in a lithium-ion battery cell for testing purposes by Metis Engineering. Credit: Metis Engineering
The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has developed an
AI-based acoustic detection system
that identifies battery failures by sound. In collaboration with Xi'an University of Science and Technology, NIST recorded sounds from 38 battery explosions to train the AI system, enabling it to recognize the acoustic signatures of impending failure.
Thermal management solutions
Related:
NeoVolta, SK On Announce One of Largest Domestic Battery Deals Since OBBBA Passage
Startup CARRAR has developed
immersion cooling technology using phase-change materials
that can prevent thermal runaway from spreading between battery cells. This approach addresses the exact scenario that unfolded in La Verne, where thermal runaway in one storage system threatened adjacent units.
A CARRAR battery in the lab. Credit: CARRAR
Viridi's anti-propagation technology takes a different approach, preventing thermal runaway from spreading beyond a single battery cell through
modular design and advanced containment systems
. Their fail-safe BESS technology aims to stop cascading failures at the cell level.
Material science advances
Research into modified electrodes and bio-inspired materials offers another prevention avenue. Thermal insulation remains the most widely used mitigation strategy, but newer materials can better withstand or mitigate temperature increases that trigger thermal runaway.
Industry response
The battery industry has increasingly focused on safety as BESS installations expand. Prevention strategies include product regulation, safety standards, and advanced monitoring systems that track pressure, temperature, and gas emissions.
Infrared cameras and multi-sensor warning systems provide additional layers of protection, though the La Verne incident demonstrates that even with modern safety measures, battery fires remain a significant challenge for first responders and facility operators.
Looking ahead
As battery energy storage systems become essential for grid stability and renewable energy integration, incidents like the La Verne fire underscore the critical importance of continued investment in safety technology. The combination of early detection systems, advanced thermal management, improved materials, and comprehensive monitoring represents the industry's best path forward.
As of Wednesday, La Verne residents await the all-clear as firefighters continue cooling operations, a reminder that while battery technology powers our clean energy future, managing its risks remains an evolving challenge requiring constant vigilance and innovation.

This all followed more than a decade of teaching English, ESL, literature, and argumentation as a lecturer at Eastern Michigan University (Ypsilanti, MI) and, for five years, at Sakura no Seibo Junior College (Fukushima, Japan).

title: What Is Black Mass in Lithium-Ion Batteries?
content:
Battery Recycling
Lithium-Ion Batteries
Batteries
Materials
Understanding black mass extracted from spent lithium-ion batteries is key to sustainable energy, supply chain resilience, and circular economies.
September 23, 2026
3 Min Read
Reclaimed materials from lithium-ion batteries.
John Keeble /Getty Images News
As the world transitions to cleaner energy sources, demand for lithium-ion batteries has surged, especially for electric vehicles (EVs), battery energy storage systems (BESS), and consumer electronics. However, this surge has also raised concerns about battery supply chain resilience, critical mineral allocations, and environmental impact. Black mass, a key component of battery recycling, offers a promising solution to these challenges. But what exactly is black mass, and why is it so important?
Understanding black mass
Black mass is a dark, powdery substance extracted from spent lithium-ion batteries during recycling. It is essentially a concentrated mixture of valuable metals and materials that are integral to manufacturing lithium-ion batteries. The name "black mass" comes from its dark, granular appearance, resulting from shredding and processing used batteries.
lithium-ion batteries
reach the end of their life cycle, they are disassembled, and their components are separated. The black mass is derived from the cathode and anode of the batteries, which contain critical minerals such as:
Related:
GM Launches Closed-Loop EV Battery Recycling Pilot Program
Manganese
Graphite
These critical minerals are essential for manufacturing new batteries, making black mass a valuable resource for battery supply chain resilience and for the circular economy.
The process of extracting black mass
Producing black mass involves several steps, starting with collecting used lithium-ion batteries. These batteries then undergo mechanical and chemical processes to recover critical minerals. The key steps include:
Battery collection and sorting: Used batteries are gathered and sorted based on their chemistry and size.
Shredding: The batteries are mechanically shredded to break them down into smaller components.
Separation: Advanced techniques, such as sieving and density separation, are used to isolate the black mass from other materials like plastics, aluminum, and copper.
Chemical processing: Hydrometallurgical or pyrometallurgical methods are employed to extract individual metals from the black mass.
GM engineers prepare an EV battery pack for testing. Courtesy of General Motors Co.
American companies leading the way in battery recycling
The US is home to several innovative companies that are at the forefront of
battery recycling
. These organizations are developing cutting-edge technologies to recover valuable materials from used lithium-ion batteries and contribute to a sustainable energy future. Key players include Redwood Materials, Cirba Solutions, American Battery Technology Company (ABTC), and more.
These companies are addressing the environmental challenges posed by battery waste and helping the US reduce its dependence on foreign sources of critical minerals, enhancing supply-chain resilience.
Related:
What Really Happens to Spent EV Batteries?
The future of battery recycling
As the demand for lithium-ion batteries continues to rise, battery recycling is poised to play a pivotal role in the global energy transition. A growing number of companies are adopting closed-loop recycling systems to extract black mass and reintegrate materials recovered from spent batteries into new battery production. For example, companies like Redwood Materials, Cirba Solutions, and GM are creating closed-loop systems.

title: Data Center Water Use: From WUE to Real-World Resilience
content:
Data centers are facing a new reality: water is no longer a background utility but a core constraint that shapes siting, design, operations, and community relations. The conversation is moving beyond average efficiency metrics to show that facilities can operate under peak stress conditions without exacerbating local water stress or pollution. This roundup of
Data Center Knowledge
articles connects technical, economic, and policy dimensions of data center water use and highlights where the industry is headed next.
Metrics and Measurements
WUE 101 – and Its Limits
Water Use Effectiveness (WUE) measures a data center’s total water consumed per kilowatt-hour of IT energy (liters/kWh). Tracking WUE supports sustainability goals, cost control, cooling optimization, and transparent community reporting. However, WUE can be misleading if taken alone because it doesn’t reflect water sourcing or consistently measured boundaries, and it’s a relative metric (not total water use). Ambient conditions and metering practices can also affect comparability across sites.
Related:
Beyond WUE: Assessing Data Center Water Resilience
Beyond WUE: Measuring Resilience Where It Matters
Water resilience for data centers can’t be judged by WUE or “waterless” claims alone; it must be proven under peak stress, according to water treatment specialist Dr. Marcello Serrano. Using
California’s Imperial Valley
dispute over a proposed AI data center as an example, Serrano argues that credible stewardship hinges on site-specific, transparent assessments that address five areas:
Peak operations under extreme heat
Water rights and curtailment risks during shortages
Reclaimed water availability and quality onsite
Discharge constraints (sewer capacity, permits, and thermal/chemical limits)
Water-energy tradeoffs vs. grid and environmental conditions
Applied early in site selection and operations, this framework helps operators and utilities plan, align on capacity and discharge requirements, and avoid escalating resource conflicts into litigation.
Cooling Technologies
Why Cooling Water Is Hard to Reuse
Since most data centers rely on direct evaporative cooling, most intake water exits as vapor, while the mineral-concentrated remainder is periodically flushed as blowdown, which typically requires treatment before any onsite reuse. While facilities can cut potable demand by implementing closed-loop or hybrid heat-rejection systems, treating blowdown, or repurposing residual water as graywater, these approaches add costs, complexity, footprint, and often higher electricity use in many climates. As of now, economics in many markets still favor conventional evaporative designs, though rising water prices and evolving regulations could change that.
Related:
Why Data Centers Rarely Reuse Cooling Water
Technology Trajectory: Evaporative Today, Liquid Tomorrow
Evaporative cooling remains prevalent because it is inexpensive to install and operate, scales effectively to very large facilities, and uses less electricity than mechanical refrigeration. However, it consumes large amounts of water and can strain local supplies. Alternatives such as liquid cooling (direct-to-chip and immersion), mechanical refrigeration, and free cooling are available, but high installation costs, energy availability constraints, and scalability considerations have slowed adoption.
Water Sources and Treatment
Practical Pathways to Lower Freshwater Demand
Most data centers use municipal water for cooling –
about 95%
of total data center water use – which can burden communities by contributing to shortages and higher costs. Alternatives can reduce pressure on potable systems, including surface water (rivers and lakes), seawater (with corrosion and distillation considerations), groundwater (where available), wastewater, and graywater. As data center power use grows and groundwater constraints intensify, shifting from municipal supplies to alternative sources is increasingly important for sustainability and community impact.
Related:
Liquid Cooling Options: RDHx, Direct-to-Chip, Immersion
Turning to the Sea: When Seawater Makes Sense
Standard evaporative cooling systems cannot use seawater without extensive pretreatment to manage scaling and corrosion. Alternative approaches, such as wet surface air cooling, can tap the sea as a heat sink. The main obstacle is financial, not technical, and growing water concerns alongside AI-driven demand may prompt more coastal facilities to evaluate seawater options despite higher upfront costs.
Siting and Infrastructure
AI-Scale Compute Makes Water a Siting Constraint
As dense GPU clusters concentrate unprecedented thermal loads, water is emerging as a siting constraint on par with power. Nearly all server energy becomes heat that must be rejected, and cooling choices create explicit electricity-water tradeoffs. Municipal systems, built for distributed, steady loads, can struggle to meet data centers’ high peaking factors during extreme conditions, and wastewater capacity and reclaimed water access are becoming strategic constraints.
Infrastructure Reality Check: Virginia’s Groundwater and Urban Utilities
A July 2026 Virginia DEQ
assessment
concluded that, under current permitting standards, no location in the Virginia Coastal Plain can support a major new groundwater withdrawal at the scale typical of some hyperscale data centers. Near the I-95 data center corridor, modeled sustainable capacity is below 30,000 gallons per day, with the highest regional estimate around 360,000 gallons per day in the eastern Northern Neck – still far below hyperscale needs. As a result, future developments in the region would need to rely on municipal or alternative water supplies, making water availability a key constraint alongside power and transmission.
Environmental and Health Impacts
Water Pollution Risks from Cooling Systems
Data centers’ evaporative cooling
can introduce
biocides, corrosion inhibitors, and metals into local waters, especially at high discharge volumes. To reduce the impact, operators should favor lower- or no-water cooling where possible, use safer chemistry, distribute discharges, and route or treat wastewater before release.
Policy and Governance
The Global Picture: Rapid Growth, Patchwork Governance
Data centers rank among the world’s top 10 most water-intensive industries, per a joint report by BSI Group and Waterwise. A single 1 MW facility can consume over 25 million liters of water annually. Many high-growth markets lack robust water governance and water-efficiency policies, even as the global data center capacity is
projected
to nearly double by 2030. Without coordinated policy, enforceable standards, and broader adoption of alternative cooling and non-potable water sources, AI- and cloud-driven expansion may deepen water stress in already constrained regions.
Community and Stakeholders
Community Impacts: Alberta’s Debate
Calgary and other Alberta communities have experienced recent water main breaks and restrictions, fueling concerns that data center growth may increase pressure on municipal systems. A large proposed campus near Calgary was rejected, with water use cited alongside environmental, power, and agricultural issues, even as other projects and AI hubs move forward. Given Canada’s cold climate, experts note that low- or zero-water cooling can be economically attractive and help mitigate municipal water dependencies, though it’s not universally necessary or appropriate in every region.
The Bottom Line
Proving water resilience is becoming central to data centers’ license to operate. That entails planning for extremes, matching designs to local hydrology and infrastructure, prioritizing non-potable sources and closed-loop systems where feasible, tightening discharge controls, and engaging transparently with regulators and communities. Metrics such as WUE remain useful, but context-based, site-specific resilience will determine whether facilities can grow sustainably in a water-constrained world.

title: How Comb Lasers Could Reshape AI Data Center Links
content:
Data center operators building AI clusters need more bandwidth without expanding power and space budgets. One emerging answer is better handling of the light that carries data.
Wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) increases fiber capacity by sending multiple colors of light down the same strand. The catch is economic and operational: operators need enough stable wavelengths, at reasonable cost and power, with high reliability.
The conventional method – using a separate laser for every wavelength – is straining as channel counts climb. Each added color brings another laser, driver, and control loop, increasing power draw, cost, and potential failure points. Optical frequency comb generators take a different approach, producing many evenly spaced wavelengths from a single source rather than an array of individual lasers.
Comb-based light sources aren’t new. They have circulated in telecom research for years. But the co-packaged optics that many designs envision remain
closer to pilot than volume production
Related:
How AI Is Reshaping Subsea and Terrestrial Networks
“Potentially, comb lasers allow you to pack many more wavelengths, much tighter together without fear of interference,” said Frank Smyth, founder and CTO of Pilot Photonics, in an interview with
Data Center Knowledge
How Frequency Combs Generate Many Stable Wavelengths
On a spectrum analyzer, a comb source appears as evenly spaced lines resembling the teeth of the comb. In a laser array, wavelength count and component count are directly linked. Add a wavelength, and you add another laser, driver, and locking loop.
“A comb breaks that link. One pump laser and one silicon nitride die produce all the wavelengths at once, on a grid set by the resonator itself, so the hardware does not grow as you add channels,” Marcello Girardi, CEO and co-founder of Solinide, told
Data Center Knowledge.
Where Conventional Laser Arrays Hit Scaling Limits
Arrays handle a handful of channels well, but they hit limits as the channel count rises. “Four wavelengths is a solved problem, and arrays solve it well,” Girardi said. “The difficulty starts at eight, and by 16, the component count limits you.”
Manufacturing and Yield: Fixed Spacing via Lithography
Because a comb’s wavelengths come from one pump laser and one passive resonator, spacing is set lithographically rather than tuned individually.
Steven Estrella, director of product management at Quintessent, said combs reduce the number of lasers required for the same channel count compared to conventional continuous-wave distributed feedback (CW DFB) arrays. “This translates to fewer points of failure, thereby increasing reliability, while also reducing wavelength control complexity over a changing environment,” he said. “With the current InP [indium phosphide] CW DFB laser supply shortage, reducing the number of required lasers is more important than ever.”
Related:
Why AI Performance Starts Long Before GPUs
Why Now: DWDM Density Is Moving from 4 to 32 Channels
Data centers used coarse WDM for years – often four widely spaced wavelengths per fiber. Denser, telecom-style plans now pack eight to 32 wavelengths closer together. “Now you have a much more challenging wavelength drift and laser array manufacturing yield issue,” Smyth said. “And this is where comb lasers can offer benefits.”
Where Combs May Land First
Opinions differ on the first deployment beachheads. Quintessent targets link distances between 30 and 100 meters. “Our comb lasers are designed to power DWDM links within the rack and between racks,” Estrella said. “This is another benefit of comb laser technology, since the power and bandwidth problem statement is most acute within the rack.”
Vivek Raghunathan, CEO and co-founder of Xscape Photonics, agreed, pointing to scale-up links between GPUs and switches as uniform enough to standardize a design.
Girardi sees a different starting point: “The first socket is scale-out, between rows, because that is where co-packaged optics is actually being deployed.” He agreed that scale-up is the better long-term fit, but said it awaits the next generation of optical scale-up networking.
Related:
Data Centers vs. Telcos: Different Roles, Shared Dependence
Smyth noted limits today in per-wavelength output power for scale-out, especially as per-lane rates climb, though he said his company is working to close that gap.
Raghunathan said total link-level power could drop by 2x to 3x by amortizing one pump laser and control loop across many wavelengths rather than duplicating the chain per channel. Lower link power cuts cooling needs. And when the light source sits in a swappable front-panel module rather than on the package, those watts come out of the budget that GPU silicon competes for. That placement also lets operators swap the light source – the least reliable optical component – without touching the rest of the system.
What’s Real Today and What’s Next
Comb lasers have struggled to gain adoption before. An independent analyst report, Cignal AI’s
Optical Component Startup Tracker
(July 2026), cites concerns about single-point-of-failure risk, tunability, and stability.
Maturity varies by company. “Various players seem to sit somewhere between lab demo and evaluation kit,” Smyth said.
Solinide says it already ships a product. “We have a product, and we sell it,” Girardi said. “Today, we ship rack-mounted units rather than modules, so the price sits in a different category, and the reason is form factor and volume, not the technology.”
A key enabler still missing across the industry is a standardized external laser source module for co-packaged optics. No qualified version exists yet. Girardi expects prototypes through 2027 and volume production in 2028, when he also expects costs to fall enough to enable a crossover against mature pluggable optics.
Estrella said Quintessent is sampling its comb lasers with customers.
Standards and Lock-In
Standards will determine whether comb deployments become a multi-vendor market or remain tied to a handful of closed systems. ELSFP (External Laser Source Small Form-factor Pluggable) covers the physical light-source module, and the OCI MSA (Optical Compute Interconnect Multi-Source Agreement) spans the broader interconnect. Together, these efforts would allow operators to qualify a socket rather than a specific vendor stack, helping to avoid single-supplier lock-in.
“When platforms move from eight channels to 16 and beyond, that’s the point where WDM has scaled past what incumbent laser arrays can yield, and it marks the transition from combs as one option among several to combs as the architecture,” Raghunathan said.
Smyth summed up what still stands between the technology and broader adoption: “The biggest things standing between here and wider adoption are power per wavelength and high-yield manufacturing.”

title: Battery revenues rise everywhere in Europe other than Baltics in August 2026 - Energy Storage
content: The potential revenues of battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Spain increased between 1% and 6% in August compared to July, according to the monthly analysis by the French consultancy Clean Horizon. This would imply a range of €482,000–€506,000/MW/year for 2 hours and €657,000–€689,000/MW/year for 4 hours. The positive trend was observed across durations and was driven by increases in aFRR capacity prices and continuous intraday market prices, while accessible spreads in the aFRR and day-ahead markets also widened. This trend further highlights the growing importance of market mix for BESS profitability. Participation in ancillary services can complement revenues from arbitrage in the day-ahead and intraday markets, allowing battery operations to be shifted towards markets with the most favorable economic signals at any given time. Clean Horizon’s analysis uses battery revenue indices that combine opportunities available in the wholesale and ancillary services markets. The performance in Spain contrasts with that of several other European markets, where BESS revenues declined in August due to lower volatility or reduced prices for balancing services. Differences between European markets Spain’s performance in August was just one part of the wider European landscape. In France, revenues increased by 6.1% to €294,000/MW/year, driven by a 17.7% rise in aFRR capacity prices, a 12.3% increase in aFRR energy spreads, and an 11.5% increase in day-ahead market spreads. FCR prices also rose by 7.9%. Italy saw a more moderate increase. The day-ahead market spread reached €131/MWh, 34% higher than the previous month, which boosted gross revenues for a two-hour battery by 2.2% to €331,000/MW/year. In Portugal, one of the markets closest to Spain, revenue from a two-hour battery increased by 16% in August. Clean Horizon attributes this growth to increased volatility in wholesale prices: the accessible spread in the day-ahead market grew by 32%, while the price in the continuous intraday market increased by 36% compared to July. In Germany, by contrast, battery revenues declined between 1% and 6%, depending on the duration. ‘aFRR DOWN’ prices remained high and positively correlated with solar production, but falling ‘aFRR UP’ reserve prices reduced revenues. In Finland, increased volatility in the day-ahead market benefited batteries. The average daily spread reached €65/MWh, approximately three times higher than in July, while volatility in the aFRR and mFRR energy markets followed a similar trend. Poland maintained high revenue levels despite an 8.6% monthly decline in the two-hour battery index. The day-ahead market spread increased by 32% to €237/MWh, while ancillary capacity reservation prices rose by an average of 8%. The Baltic markets showed a different trend. In Estonia, revenue from a two-hour battery decreased by 13% since July, to €152,000/MW/year, while in Latvia and Lithuania it fell by 17%, to €307,000 and €251,000/MW/year, respectively. In these latter two markets, mFRR capacity reserves continued to account for 54% of revenue. Romania saw an approximate 35% drop in demand for two- and four-hour batteries. In this case, Clean Horizon attributes the reduction to the decline in aFRR energy spreads and increased competition following the commissioning of new BESS assets, such as the Gura Ialomiței battery energy storage system . title: Green Flexibility plans 120 MW/480 MWh of BESS in Germany - Energy Storage
content: German battery storage developer and operator Green Flexibility is developing six large-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Lower Saxony with a combined capacity of 120 MW/480 MWh. The Kempten-based company has signed flexible grid connection agreements with German network operator EWE Netz for the six projects, allowing them to operate within dynamic grid constraints while maintaining a grid-neutral operating profile. The agreements are intended to make more efficient use of existing grid capacity, avoid additional network stress and support the integration of renewable energy in the region. The six BESS projects are located in Lindern, Bad Bederkesa, Hagen im Bremischen, Esterwegen, Bremervörde and Zeven. Most of the projects are ready for construction, while work on some is expected to begin this year. Green Flexibility plans to commission all six systems in 2027 and 2028. Lienert said the six projects will add flexibility to Lower Saxony’s electricity grid while ensuring that the storage systems are designed around local network requirements. The flexible connection agreements, known as flexible connection agreements (FCA), allow the batteries to adjust their operation according to available grid capacity. Similar arrangements are being used elsewhere in Germany. Developer Eco Stor has published a public dashboard showing how its 103 MW battery storage system in Schleswig-Holstein optimizes its operation within dynamic grid limits.
